title: 词根ANY-Awe-BACK-base
content:
一、词根 ANY（表示 “任何”）1️⃣ anybody / anyone — 任何人
意思相同，可互换使用。
发音差异：
英音：anybody（/ˈenɪbɒdi/）
美音：anybady（/ˈenibɑːdi/）


例句：
Anybody can use the pool. 任何人都可以使用游泳池。
Anyone can see that he is wrong. 任何人都能看出他错了。



✅ 结论： anybody = anyone = “任何人”，在口语与书面语中完全通用。

2️⃣ anyhow / anyway — 不管怎样
结构含义：
any（任何） + way（方式）→ 无论哪种方式 = “不管怎样”


用法区别：
anyhow → 英式英语更常见
anyway → 美式英语更常见


例句：
Cheer up anyhow!（振作起来！）
I decided to take the photo anyway. 不管怎样，我还是决定拍下这张照片。



✅ 语气： 表示“虽然别人反对，我仍然要做” → “不管怎样”“反正都要”。

3️⃣ anymore — 再也不（用于否定句）
结构： any（任何） + more（更多）→ “再也没有更多”
用法： 常与否定连用。
例句：
I couldn’t trust him anymore. 我再也无法信任他了。
I don’t trust him anymore. 我已经不再相信他了。



✅ 记忆法： “不再有更多信任” → “再也不”。

4️⃣ anything — 任何事情
结构： any（任何） + thing（事物）
用法： 否定句或疑问句中使用。
例句：
We can’t do anything. 我们什么也做不了。
Did you find anything? 你找到什么了吗？
No, I couldn’t find anything. 没有，我什么都没找到。




5️⃣ anywhere — 任何地方
结构： any（任何） + where（地方）
用法： 否定句或疑问句中。
对比：
anywhere → 否定/疑问句中 “任何地方”
somewhere → 肯定句中 “某个地方”




例句：
I can’t see it anywhere. 我哪儿都看不到它。
Can we go somewhere warm? 我们能去一个暖和的地方吗？




二、词根 AWE（原意：敬畏、畏惧）1️⃣ awful — 糟糕的、讨厌的
结构： all（敬畏） + full（充满的） → 充满敬畏的 → 可怕的 → 糟糕的
例句：
That’s an awful color. 这颜色真难看。
The weather last summer was awful. 去年夏天天气糟透了。



✅ 语义演变： 敬畏 → 畏惧 → 令人害怕的 → 令人讨厌的。

2️⃣ awesome — 极好的、令人惊叹的
结构： all（敬畏） + some（形容词后缀） → 让人惊叹的、了不起的。
例句：
An awesome sight. 惊人的景象。
Wow! That’s totally awesome! 太棒了！



✅ 对比：

awful → 糟糕的
awesome → 极好的


三、词根 BACK（表示“后面；回；背部”）1️⃣ back — 后面 / 回去
发音记忆： 背靠 → back。
例句：
I went back to bed. 我回到床上。
back pain 背痛
back door 后门




2️⃣ background — 背景
结构： back（后） + ground（地面、底） → “后面的底” → 背景。
常见短语：
cultural background 文化背景
educational background 学历背景
background information 背景资料



✅ 词源提示：

inform → information（告知 → 信息）
background information = 背景信息。


3️⃣ backpack — 背包
结构： back（背） + pack（包） → 背在背上的包。
例句：
He had a small green backpack. 他有一个小绿背包。




4️⃣ backwards — 向后
结构： back（后） + ward（方向） + s（副词后缀） → 向后地。
例句：
He took a step backwards. 他向后退了一步。


反义词： forward（向前）
He took a step forward. 他向前迈了一步。




四、词根 BASE（表示“基础、底部”）1️⃣ base — 基础；底部
名词： 根基、底部。
The base of the glass/bottle 杯底 / 瓶底
The lamp has a heavy base. 灯的底座很沉。


动词： 以……为基础
Base your decision on facts. 以事实为依据。




2️⃣ baseball — 棒球
结构： base（垒） + ball（球） → 需要触碰“垒”的球类运动。
相关词：
baseball bat 球棒
baseball team 棒球队
baseball stadium 棒球场




3️⃣ basement — 地下室
结构： base + ment（名词后缀） → “地基之下的空间” → 地下室。
例句：
a basement flat / apartment 地下室房间




4️⃣ basic — 基本的
结构： base（基础） + ic（形容词后缀） → 基本的、基础的。
例句：
basic information 基本信息
basic fact 基本事实
basic ideas 基本思想




✅ 总结表：词根与核心含义


词根
含义
派生代表词
典型意义



any
任何
anyone / anything / anywhere
任意、不确定


Awe
敬畏
awful / awesome
极坏 / 极好


back
后面
backward / background / backpack
背、后、返回


base
基础
basic / basement / baseball
地基、基础、根源

title: 词根chair-break-count-cover
content:
1. Chair
原义：椅子
衍生词 / 词缀逻辑：
Chairman：chair（椅子）+ man（人）→ 坐在椅子上的人 → 公司或组织的负责人
Chairperson：更中性的人 → 公司或组织负责人，不区分性别


例句：
Sarah is the chairperson of the company.（Sarah 是公司负责人）


短语 / 搭配：
sit in the chair 坐在椅子上
chair a meeting 主持会议


助记 / 联想：想象“坐在椅子上做决定的人”，记住 chair + man → chairman。


2. Break
原义：打破、折断
衍生词 / 词缀逻辑：
Broke / Broken：break 的过去式 / 过去分词
Breakfast：break（打破）+ fast（禁食）→ 结束禁食 → 早餐
Breakthrough：break（打破）+ through（穿过）→ 突破


例句：
My watch has broken.（我的手表坏了）
I had a big breakfast.（我吃了一顿丰盛的早餐）
The company made a breakthrough in China.（公司在中国取得了突破）


短语 / 搭配：
take a break / have a break 休息
break up 分手、分裂


助记 / 联想：想象“打破一块东西” → break，breakfast → 打破禁食 → 早餐，breakthrough → 打破障碍 → 突破


3. Count
原义：数数、计算
衍生词 / 词缀逻辑：
Account：ac（加强 / 朝向）+ count → 账户，计算每笔收支 → 帐户；也表示解释 → 解释清楚一件事
Discount：dis（不）+ count → 不算在内 → 打折；也可表示忽略


例句：
He can count from one to ten.（他能从一数到十）
Every point counts.（每一分都很重要）
I count on you.（我指望你）
They were selling everything at a discount.（他们所有商品都在打折）


短语 / 搭配：
count on somebody 指望某人
give/get a discount 给/得到折扣


助记 / 联想：想象把每一件东西算清楚 → count，每一点都重要 → every point counts。


4. Cover
原义：覆盖、遮盖

衍生词 / 词缀逻辑：

Coverage：cover + age → 报道范围 / 覆盖范围
Discover：dis（不）+ cover → 不覆盖 → 发现
Recovery：re（再次）+ cover → 再次覆盖 → 恢复


例句：

She covered her face with her hands.（她用双手遮住脸）

Snow covered the ground.（大雪覆盖了地面）

The story received wide coverage in the press.（这件事获得了广泛报道）

“press” 的用法概述：

动词
1️⃣ 按；压；挤  

中文释义：用手或工具对某物施加压力。  
例句：Press the button to start the machine.（按这个按钮启动机器。）  
注意事项：可作及物动词（+宾语）或不及物动词，如 “Press down firmly.”（用力往下按。）

2️⃣ 催促；逼迫；敦促  

中文释义：通过言语或行动促使某人做某事。  
例句：My parents pressed me to study medicine.（父母催促我学医。）  
常见搭配：“press sb. for sth.”（催促某人做某事），如 “They pressed her for an answer.”（他们逼她给出答案。）

3️⃣ 熨烫（衣物）  

中文释义：用熨斗使衣物平整。  
例句：I need to press this shirt before the meeting.（开会前我得熨一下这件衬衫。）

名词
1️⃣ 新闻媒体；报刊；记者（常作 the press）  

中文释义：指新闻机构、记者群体或报刊总称。  
例句：The press has been covering the election closely.（新闻媒体一直在密切报道选举。）  
注意事项：前面通常加定冠词 “the”，如 “a press conference”（新闻发布会）。

2️⃣ 出版社；印刷厂  

中文释义：出版书籍、报纸等的机构或印刷场所。  
例句：This novel was published by a small press.（这本小说由一家小出版社出版。）

3️⃣ 压；按；挤（可数）  

中文释义：按压的动作或压力。  
例句：One press of the switch and the light turns on.（按一下开关灯就亮了。）

“press” 是个多义词，具体含义要看语境～ 你是在哪个场景遇到它的呀？ 📰✂️


He is still recovering from his operation.（他还在手术后恢复中）



短语 / 搭配：

front cover 书的封面
media coverage 媒体报道
discover nature / yourself 探索自然 / 发掘自我


助记 / 联想：cover → 盖上 → 发现未盖之物 → discover；伤口盖上 → recover



5. Day
原义：一天、白天
衍生词 / 词缀逻辑：
Daylight：day（白天）+ light（光）→ 日光
Daytime：day + time → 白天的、日间的
Holiday / Birthday / New Year’s Day 特定的一天


例句：
I saw Tom three days ago.（我三天前见过 Tom）
I studied all day.（我学习了一整天）
The park is open during the daytime.（公园在白天开放）
How can he do this in broad daylight?（他怎么能光天化日之下做这件事？）


短语 / 搭配：
all day 一整天
daylight before dawn 黎明前的光
daytime TV show 白天播出的电视节目


助记 / 联想：day → 白天 → 日光、日间活动，all day → 一整天

title: 2. Improve Your Speaking and Conversational Skills
content:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=occTIMof2Vc
Improve Your Speaking and Conversational SkillsEnglish Conversation Practice – Easy English Talk PodcastHosts: Jason & Julia

1. Introduction
Speaking English confidently is one of the most common goals for learners.
With the right techniques, anyone can improve.
Speaking practice can be fun, not stressful, when done correctly.
This episode provides practical tips, examples, and exercises to make your conversations smoother and more natural.


2. Why Speaking Skills Matter
Communication, not just grammar
Speaking is about expressing ideas clearly and connecting with others.
Grammar and vocabulary are tools, not the goal.


Opportunities and confidence
Speaking well opens doors: friendships, job success, travel, and cultural exchange.
Confidence grows through practice, even with mistakes.


Thinking in English
The more you speak, the faster your brain starts forming sentences in English instead of translating from your native language.


Better listening and thinking skills
Speaking helps you notice patterns in pronunciation, structure, and rhythm.
Improves comprehension and fluency at the same time.




3. Step-by-Step Guide to Improving Speaking SkillsStep 1. Start Small and Simple
Avoid trying to speak perfect English at first.
Use short, simple sentences and common daily phrases.
Example:
❌ I am feeling exceptionally joyful today because the weather is delightfully sunny.
✅ I’m happy today. The sun is shining.


Focus on daily conversations: greetings, ordering food, asking directions.
Practice small sentences every day → confidence builds naturally.

Key idea:

Simple is powerful. Fluency begins with small, easy expressions.


Step 2. Listen and Repeat
Listen to native speakers (podcasts, videos, movies) to learn pronunciation and rhythm.
Repeat what you hear — copy tone, speed, and emotion.
Pause and mimic real speech (“shadowing”).
Example:
Listen: I’m going to the store.
Repeat: Say it exactly as you heard it.


This improves both pronunciation and listening comprehension.

Tip:

10–15 minutes of listen-and-repeat every day brings noticeable results in a few weeks.


Step 3. Practice Speaking Every Day
Daily practice builds automatic fluency.
Speak out loud even when alone.
Describe your actions in English:
“I’m cutting vegetables.”
“I’m cleaning my room.”


Record yourself to check pronunciation and rhythm.
Consistency is more important than duration — 5 minutes a day beats one long weekly session.
Practice with a partner for real conversation flow.

Key idea:

Speak daily. Fluency grows through repetition, not perfection.


Step 4. Ask Questions and Show Interest
Good conversations are two-way.
Ask follow-up questions to keep dialogue natural.
Examples:
“What’s your favorite movie?”
“What kind of books do you enjoy?”


React naturally with short phrases like:
“That’s amazing!” / “Wow, really?” / “Tell me more!”


Builds connection and keeps conversation lively.

Key idea:

Communication = curiosity + interest + response.


Step 5. Learn Useful Phrases and Idioms
Learn in chunks, not individual words.
Use real-life expressions:
“I’m completely exhausted.” (instead of “I’m very tired.”)
“It’s a piece of cake.” (means “It’s very easy.”)


Practice 3–5 new phrases each week in context.
Using idioms and expressions makes speech sound natural and fluent.

Example practice:

Question: How was your day?
Answer: It was a piece of cake! / I was running around all day!

Key idea:

Phrases are shortcuts to natural-sounding English.


Step 6. Correct Mistakes Without Fear
Mistakes are part of the learning process.
Each error = a chance to improve.
Example:
❌ “He go to school.”
✅ “He goes to school.”


Ask for feedback from teachers or partners.
Focus on communication first — accuracy improves with time.

Mindset:

Don’t be afraid of mistakes; be afraid of not trying.


Step 7. Practice with Real People
Apply what you learn in real situations.
Talk with:
Friends, colleagues, classmates
Online language partners
English clubs or conversation groups


Real dialogue trains your listening, thinking, and speaking together.
Even short daily chats help.

Examples:

“How was your day?”
“What do you like to eat?”

Key idea:

Real interaction = real progress.


4. Common Mistakes to Avoid
Speaking too little out of fear
Don’t wait for perfect grammar — just speak.


Overcomplicating sentences
Short and clear is better than long and broken.


Not listening actively
Listen carefully → reply naturally → keep the flow.



Formula for smooth conversation:

Speak → Listen → Respond → Repeat.


5. Stay Motivated & Connect to Real Life
Every small step counts:
Speaking for one minute without hesitation.
Using a new idiom correctly.


Celebrate progress.
Keep a journal or record your improvement.
Remember your “why”: speaking confidently changes your life — travel, work, friendships.

Motivation tip:

Practice consistently and enjoy the process — confidence grows naturally.


6. Mini Practice ActivityTry these short dialogues aloud or with a partner:
Dialogue 1 A: Hi, how are you? B: I’m good, thank you. How about you?
Dialogue 2 A: Hi, what did you do today? B: I went to the park and read a book. What about you?
Practice Tip:

Repeat daily.
Change the topic or verbs: “I cooked dinner.” / “I watched a movie.”
Speak naturally, not perfectly.


7. Final Takeaways
Start small. Use simple sentences.
Listen and repeat. Imitate native rhythm.
Speak daily. Consistency > perfection.
Ask questions. Keep conversations alive.
Learn idioms and phrases. Speak naturally.
Don’t fear mistakes. Learn from them.
Talk to real people. Practice brings confidence.


✅ Key Message:

Speak a little every day. Don’t worry about mistakes. Every word you say brings you closer to fluency.

title: 1. Talk English Without Thinking
content:
https://www.youtube.com/@EasyEnglishTalk2/videos

Talk English Without Thinking – Study GuidePodcast: REasy English Talk – English Conversation Practice Hosts: Jason & Julia

1. Introduction
Many English learners want to speak fast and naturally but stop to think too much.

Overthinking slows down conversation and reduces fluency.

Fluent speakers speak naturally without excessive translation or hesitation.

“excessive” 的用法概述：形容词（用于名词前或系动词后）
1️⃣ 过多的；过度的；过分的  

中文释义：超过合理或必要限度的，常含负面评价。  
例句：  
Excessive sugar intake can lead to health problems.（过量摄入糖会导致健康问题。）  
The company was criticized for its excessive spending on advertising.（这家公司因在广告上花费过多而受到批评。）


注意事项：后接不可数名词或复数可数名词；反义词是 “insufficient”（不足的）或 “moderate”（适度的）。

2️⃣ （行为等）极端的；过分的  

中文释义：形容行为、情绪等超出正常范围，显得不合理。  
例句：  
Her excessive anger over a small mistake surprised everyone.（她因一个小错误而表现出的过度愤怒让所有人都很惊讶。）  
The rules are excessive—no one can follow them strictly.（这些规定太苛刻了，没人能严格遵守。）



这个词在描述“超过合理限度”时非常精准，常用来表达批评或担忧的语气～ ⚠️




2. Why Learners Struggle
Translating from native language

Thinking in your first language slows sentence formation.

“formation” 的用法概述：名词（可数或不可数，具体含义需结合语境）
1️⃣ 形成；产生；组成（不可数）  

中文释义：事物从无到有或从简单到复杂的过程。  
例句：The formation of a new government took three months.（新政府的组建花了三个月。）  
注意事项：常与介词 “of” 搭配，表示“……的形成”。

2️⃣ 队形；排列方式（可数）  

中文释义：人、物或军队等按特定方式排列的状态。  
例句：The soldiers marched in a tight formation.（士兵们以密集队形行进。）  
常见搭配：“in formation”（成队形地），如 birds flying in formation（编队飞行的鸟）。

3️⃣ 结构；构造；形态（可数）  

中文释义：事物的内在结构或外在形态，尤用于地理、地质或生物学领域。  
例句：Rocks with a columnar formation are common in volcanic areas.（柱状结构的岩石在火山地区很常见。）

4️⃣ （社会团体、组织等的）建立（可数）  

中文释义：指组织、团体或机构的正式成立。  
例句：The formation of the students’ union improved campus life.（学生会的成立改善了校园生活。）

这个词在描述“过程”“结构”或“排列”时都很常用，你是在哪个场景遇到它的呀？ 🏗️


Brain works harder to find English words → speech becomes slow or blocked.



Fear of mistakes

Anxiety over grammar or pronunciation stops learners from speaking.
Mistakes are natural; native speakers also make them.
Goal: Communication, not perfection.


Insufficient speaking practice

Reading/writing/listening alone isn’t enough.
Speaking regularly helps the brain link words and ideas naturally.


“insufficient” 的用法概述：形容词（用于名词前或系动词后）
1️⃣ 不足的；不够的；不充分的  

中文释义：数量、程度或质量上未能达到必要或期望的标准，常含负面含义。  
例句：  
The evidence against him was insufficient to convict.（对他不利的证据不足，无法定罪。）  
Insufficient sleep can affect your concentration.（睡眠不足会影响你的注意力。）


注意事项：后接不可数名词或复数可数名词；反义词是 “sufficient”（足够的）或 “excessive”（过多的）。

2️⃣ （能力、资源等）不足以应付的  

中文释义：指能力、资源等无法满足特定需求或完成某事。  
例句：  
She felt insufficient for the demanding job.（她觉得自己无法胜任这份高要求的工作。）  
The team’s budget was insufficient to cover travel costs.（团队预算不够支付差旅费。）



这个词在表达“未达标”时很正式，常见于书面语或正式场合哦～ 📄




3. What “Talking Without Thinking Too Much” Really Means
Not: speaking without using your brain.
Yes: speaking naturally without pausing for every word or grammar rule.
Achieved when English words come automatically like your first language.
Requires practice, listening, repetition, and exposure.


4. How to Build Automatic English Thinking
Think directly in English
Link English words directly to objects or ideas, not translations.
Example: See a cup → think cup, not your native word first.


Daily listening and speaking
Podcasts, conversations, short videos.
Speak out loud, even to yourself.
Brain and mouth learn to respond quickly.




5. Practical Methods for Automatic Speakinga. Simple Sentences
Start with short, easy sentences for daily life.
Example: “I’m going to school.” / “I’m making tea.” / “It’s a beautiful day.”


Repeat often until automatic.
Describe daily actions aloud:
“I’m brushing my teeth.” / “I’m walking to the shop.”



b. Listen and Repeat (Shadowing)
Listen to native speakers and repeat exactly (words, tone, rhythm).
Use podcasts, YouTube videos, or short dialogues.
Benefits:
Speaks faster without thinking of grammar/vocabulary.
Mouth learns movement; brain memorizes patterns.


Daily 10–15 minutes is effective.


“shadowing” 的用法概述：名词（根据语境可作可数或不可数名词）
1️⃣ 语言学习中的“跟读训练”  

中文释义：一种语言学习方法，指逐句模仿母语者的语音、语调、节奏进行复述，以提升口语和听力。  
例句：Shadowing is a great way to improve your pronunciation and fluency.（跟读训练是提升发音和流利度的好方法。）  
注意事项：常与介词 “of” 搭配，如 “shadowing of native speakers’ audio”（跟读母语者音频）。

2️⃣ （职场中的）“影子学习”；跟班实习  

中文释义：指新手跟随有经验的人工作，观察并学习其技能和流程。  
例句：The new intern spent a week in shadowing the manager to learn daily operations.（新实习生跟班经理一周，学习日常运营。）  
常见搭配：“shadowing program”（影子学习项目）、“shadowing a colleague”（跟着同事实习）。

3️⃣ 遮蔽；阴影覆盖（正式语境，不可数）  

中文释义：物体被阴影笼罩的状态，或对某物的遮挡。  
例句：The shadowing of the garden by the tall building made it hard to grow plants.（高楼对花园的遮蔽导致植物难以生长。）

你提到的应该是语言学习中的“跟读训练”吧？这可是个超实用的技巧呢！🎧 你平时会用这个方法练习口语吗？

c. Learn Common Phrases
Using ready-made phrases saves time and sounds natural.
Examples: “I get it.”, “That’s a good idea.”, “I’m not sure.”


Write them down and practice daily.
Builds a “library of fast answers” for conversation.

d. Overcome Fear of Mistakes
Everyone makes mistakes; it’s part of learning.
Mistakes → faster improvement.
Focus: communication, not perfection.

e. Practice with Real People
Real conversations train your brain to respond quickly.
You don’t need to live in an English-speaking country:
Online language partners, English groups, friends.


Speak only in English; focus on idea-sharing, not correctness.


6. Suggested Daily Routine
Morning: Think in English for a few minutes. Describe surroundings or plans.
During the day:
Use simple sentences, practice phrases, or describe actions.


Listening & repeating: 10–15 minutes of shadowing podcasts/videos.
Speak with people: friends, online partners, or social groups.
Consistency matters: 20–30 minutes daily is more effective than occasional long sessions.


7. Motivation & Success Example
A student initially translated every word and feared mistakes.
Daily practice of simple sentences + listening & repeating + speaking with friends → gained confidence.
Within months, spoke freely and joined an English-speaking club.
Key takeaways: Daily practice + overcoming fear of mistakes = natural fluency.


8. Recap（概要） of Key Tips
Identify main problems: translating, fear of mistakes, lack of practice.

Build automatic English thinking: think directly in English.

Practice simple sentences daily.

Use listen & repeat and common phrases.

Speak with real people.

Follow a consistent daily routine.

Goal: natural communication, not perfection.

“recap” 的用法概述：动词 & 名词（非正式，口语和书面语均常用）
1️⃣ 动词：概括；扼要重述  

中文释义：简要回顾之前说过的内容，强调核心信息。  
例句：  
Let me recap the main points before we move on.（在继续之前，我来概括一下要点。）  
She quickly recapped what happened at yesterday’s meeting.（她简要重述了昨天会议的内容。）


注意事项：及物动词，直接接宾语（如 “recap the plan”“recap the story”）。

2️⃣ 名词：概要；回顾；总结  

中文释义：对已发生事件或讨论内容的简短总结。  
例句：  
Here’s a quick recap of today’s lesson.（这是今天课程的简要回顾。）  
The news ended with a recap of the day’s top stories.（新闻以当日头条的概要结束。）


常见搭配：“a quick recap”（快速回顾）、“recap of the event”（事件总结）。

这个词在学习、工作或日常对话中都很实用，比如开会前“recap”上次决议，追剧时“recap”前情～ 📝 你是在准备做总结吗？




 Takeaway: Start today. Speak a little every day, don’t fear mistakes, and practice consistently. Fluency will improve faster than you think.

“takeaway” 的用法概述：名词（英式英语常用，美式英语中常用 “takeout”）
1️⃣ 外卖食物；外卖餐  

中文释义：从餐馆购买后带回家或在其他地方食用的食物。  
例句：Let’s order Chinese takeaway for dinner tonight.（今晚我们点中式外卖当晚餐吧。）  
注意事项：可作不可数名词（指外卖这种概念）或可数名词（指一份外卖），如 “a pizza takeaway”（一份披萨外卖）。

2️⃣ （会议、演讲等的）核心要点；关键信息  

中文释义：从讨论或经历中获得的最重要的结论或教训。  
例句：The main takeaway from the meeting was the need to cut costs.（会议的核心要点是需要削减成本。）  
常见搭配：“key takeaway”（关键要点）、“main takeaway”（主要结论）。

3️⃣ 外卖餐馆；外卖店  

中文释义：专门提供外卖服务的餐馆。  
例句：There’s a good Indian takeaway near the station.（车站附近有一家不错的印度外卖店。）

这个词在日常对话和商务场景中都很常用，你是想表达“外卖”还是“核心要点”呢？ 😊

title: 5 common expressions-1
content:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=yC3H33ONPkA&list=PLzMXToX8Kzqggrhr-v0aWQA2g8pzWLBrR&index=2
5个英国常见英语表达a piece of cake
含义：非常容易，轻而易举。
词性：习语（idiom）
例句：That exam was a piece of cake.（那场考试太简单了。）
✅ 相似表达：easy peasy lemon squeezy（非常轻松，儿语式表达）


break a leg
含义：祝你好运（尤其用于比赛、演出或面试前）。
词性：感叹用语（interjection）
例句：You’ve got an interview today? Break a leg!（你今天要面试？祝你好运！）
💡 文化背景：在表演圈，直接说“good luck”被认为不吉利，于是改用“break a leg”。


it costs an arm and a leg
含义：非常昂贵。
词性：习语（idiom）
例句：My new bag cost an arm and a leg.（我的新包贵得离谱。）
💬 字面意思：花掉“一条胳膊和一条腿”，比喻“代价很大”。


to pop one’s clogs
含义：去世（委婉说法）。
词性：短语动词（phrasal verb）
例句：My neighbour’s popped his clogs.（我的邻居去世了。）
💡 语气：轻松、委婉，常用于避免直接说“die”这个词。


to call it a day
含义：收工、结束一天的工作或任务。
词性：短语动词（phrasal verb）
例句：I’m tired. Let’s call it a day.（我累了，我们就到这里吧。）
💬 延伸：也可用于“结束一个阶段的努力”——比如项目、会议或学习。

title: 5 common expressions-2
content:
一、Bits and bobs意思：零碎的小东西，杂七杂八的事物。 用法：表示各种各样的、不重要的小物件或事情。 例句：

What did you get for Christmas? — Just bits and bobs, nothing huge. （圣诞节我就收到一些小玩意儿，没什么大的。）


二、Gobsmacked意思：震惊、惊讶、目瞪口呆。 语气：可以用于正面或负面的惊讶。 例句：

Can you believe she left him? I’m absolutely gobsmacked! （你能相信她离开他了吗？我太震惊了！）


三、To lose the plot意思：发疯、做出离谱的事、失去理智。 语气：既可以责怪，也可半开玩笑。 例句：

You spent £300 on a pair of socks? You’ve completely lost the plot! （你花300英镑买袜子？你完全疯了吧！）


四、To take the mickey（或 to take the mick）意思：取笑、开玩笑（带点讽刺）。 注意：

有更粗俗的版本 to take the piss，只适合朋友间随意场合。 例句：
Three English lessons with a native teacher? Are you taking the mick? （三节母语老师的英语课？你在开玩笑吧？）


五、表达五：To pass with flying colours意思：非常成功地完成某事，取得优异成绩。 典型场景：考试、面试、选拔。 例句：

Lucy passed her university exams with flying colours. （Lucy 以优异成绩通过了大学考试。）


二、总结记忆法


表达
中文含义
示例



bits and bobs
零碎的小东西
I bought some bits and bobs.


gobsmacked
震惊、惊讶
I was gobsmacked by the news.


lose the plot
发疯、做傻事
He’s completely lost the plot.


take the mickey
取笑、开玩笑
Are you taking the mick?


pass with flying colours
取得优异成绩
She passed the exam with flying colours.

title: 2 how to use 'to get'
content:
一、动词 “get” 的多种含义Lucy 说明 “get” 在英语中非常常用，有超过 50种 不同用法。 她将其归纳为 6类核心意思：

表示 到达（to arrive / to travel）
“get” 可以替代 “arrive” 或 “travel”。


How did you get to London? = How did you travel to London? （你怎么去伦敦的？）
What time did you get here? = What time did you arrive here? （你几点到的？）


表示 获得 / 收到（to receive / to obtain）
“get” 可表示“得到”“收到”。


I got a letter in the post. = I received a letter. 我收到了信。
I hope I get a promotion. = I hope I receive a promotion. 我希望升职。
He’s not going to get an apology. 他不会得到道歉。
I get presents at Christmas. 我圣诞节会收到礼物。
Can I get a kiss? 我能得到一个吻吗？


表示 变得（to become）
“get + 形容词 / 比较级 / 过去分词” 表示“变成……”。


In summer it gets hot. 夏天变热。
I hope I get better at English. 我希望我的英语越来越好。
I’m getting bored. 我开始觉得无聊。


表示 拿 / 买 / 找（to bring / to buy / to find）
根据语境不同，意思会变化。


Can I get you a drink? 在酒吧 = 我请你喝一杯。 在家 = 我去拿饮料给你。
I need to get some new clothes. 我要去买新衣服。
Were you able to get the information? 你找到资料了吗？


与 have / have to 连用（意义不变）
“get” 可以与 “have” 或 “have to” 互换，语义相同。

① 表示“拥有” (have / have got)

I have so much money. = I’ve got so much money.
I don’t have any friends. = I’ve not got any friends.
Do you have enough time? = Have you got enough time?

② 表示“必须” (have to / have got to)

I have to tell her. = I’ve got to tell her.
She doesn’t have to come. = She hasn’t got to come.
Do you have to leave? = Have you got to leave?


常见固定表达（Expressions with “get”）
这些都是地道口语中的高频表达。


Do you get it? → 你明白吗？
Did you get it right? → 你答对了吗？
I need to get going. → 我该走了。
We didn’t get off to a good start. → 我们开局不太好。
You’re getting on my nerves. → 你让我心烦。


二、总结记忆法


含义
对应动词
例句



到达
arrive
I got here at 10.


收到
receive
I got a letter.


变得
become
It gets cold at night.


买 / 拿 / 找
buy / bring / find
Can I get you a drink?


拥有
have
I’ve got two cats.


必须
have to
I’ve got to go now.


表达
习语
Do you get it?



如果你只想记一个核心思路：

“GET = 到达 + 获得 + 变化 + 拿/买 + 拥有 + 必须 + 习语”

title: Advanced Everyday English Phrases-3
content:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VdeENKRVf-I&list=PLzMXToX8Kzqj3tX3m3vbIkrhyQzXFK3Mc&index=3

C1-C2高级形容词精讲Ambivalent
音标：/æmˈbɪv.əl.ənt/
含义：矛盾的；摇摆不定的（having or showing mixed feelings or contradictory ideas）
例句：
I feel ambivalent about moving abroad—excited but also nervous.
She has ambivalent feelings towards her hometown.



Capricious
音标：/kəˈprɪʃ.əs/
含义：善变的；反复无常的（given to sudden and unaccountable changes of mood）
例句：
The capricious weather made planning the picnic impossible.
His capricious nature made him difficult to work with.



Derogatory
音标：/dɪˈrɒɡ.ə.tər.i/
含义：贬低的；不敬的（showing a critical or disrespectful attitude）
例句：
He made several derogatory remarks about her appearance.
The article contained derogatory comments about immigrants.



Esoteric
音标：/ˌes.əˈter.ɪk/
含义：深奥的；难懂的（intended for or understood by only a small number of people）
例句：
The professor’s esoteric theories confused most students.
This ancient text contains esoteric knowledge.



Flippant
音标：/ˈflɪp.ənt/
含义：轻率的；无礼的（not showing a serious or respectful attitude）
例句：
His flippant response angered his teacher.
She regretted her flippant comment about the serious situation.



Grandiose
音标：/ˈɡræn.di.əʊs/
含义：浮夸的；不切实际的（impressive but impractical and lacking substance）
例句：
The dictator had grandiose plans for rebuilding the city.
His grandiose promises never materialized.



Histrionic
音标：/ˌhɪs.triˈɒn.ɪk/
含义：戏剧化的；做作的（overly theatrical or melodramatic）
例句：
Her histrionic reaction to the minor accident was unnecessary.
He gave a histrionic performance that lacked sincerity.



Incongruous
音标：/ɪnˈkɒŋ.ɡru.əs/
含义：不协调的；不一致的（strange and not suitable in a particular situation）
例句：
The modern furniture looked incongruous in the historic castle.
His casual attire was incongruous with the formal occasion.



Juxtaposed
音标：/ˈdʒʌk.stə.pəʊzd/
含义：并置的；对比的（placed together for contrast and comparison）
例句：
The exhibition featured juxtaposed images of wealth and poverty.
The artist juxtaposed bright and dark colors in her painting.



Laudable
音标：/ˈlɔː.də.bəl/
含义：值得赞扬的（deserving praise and commendation）
例句：
Her efforts to help the homeless were laudable.
The company’s environmental initiatives are laudable.



Mercurial
音标：/mɜːˈkjʊə.ri.əl/
含义：多变的；无常的（often changing in an unexpected way）
例句：
The CEO’s mercurial temperament made employees nervous.
British weather is famously mercurial.



Nonchalant
音标：/ˈnɒn.ʃəl.ənt/
含义：冷静的；漠不关心的（behaving in a calm, relaxed way without worry）
例句：
He tried to appear nonchalant about the exam results.
Her nonchalant attitude surprised everyone in the crisis.



Pernicious
音标：/pəˈnɪʃ.əs/
含义：有害的；恶性的（having a harmful effect, especially gradually）
例句：
The pernicious effects of smoking are well documented.
Racism is a pernicious problem in our society.



Quixotic
音标：/kwɪkˈsɒt.ɪk/
含义：不切实际的；空想的（exceedingly idealistic and unrealistic）
例句：
His quixotic quest to end world poverty continued for years.
The plan was dismissed as quixotic and impractical.



Resplendent
音标：/rɪˈsplen.dənt/
含义：灿烂的；华丽的（attractive and impressive through being richly colorful）
例句：
The queen appeared resplendent in her jeweled crown.
The garden was resplendent with autumn colors.



Subservient
音标：/səbˈsɜː.vi.ənt/
含义：卑躬屈膝的；顺从的（prepared to obey others without question）
例句：
She refused to be subservient to her husband.
His subservient behavior towards his boss was uncomfortable to watch.



Supercilious
音标：/ˌsuː.pəˈsɪl.i.əs/
含义：傲慢的；目中无人的（behaving as though superior to others）
例句：
The waiter gave us a supercilious look when we asked for tap water.
Her supercilious attitude made her unpopular with colleagues.



Tenacious
音标：/təˈneɪ.ʃəs/
含义：坚韧的；固执的（keeping a firm hold; not giving up easily）
例句：
Her tenacious pursuit of justice finally brought results.
The old tree had tenacious roots that survived the storm.



Ubiquitous
音标：/juːˈbɪk.wɪ.təs/
含义：无处不在的（very common or found everywhere）
例句：
Mobile phones have become ubiquitous in modern life.
The company’s logo was ubiquitous throughout the city.



Vicarious
音标：/vɪˈkeə.ri.əs/
含义：替代的；感同身受的（experienced through the feelings of another person）
例句：
She lived vicariously through her daughter’s adventures.
Reading travel books gave him vicarious pleasure.

title: Advanced Everyday English Phrases-2
content:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xhieBepo6_A&list=PLzMXToX8Kzqj3tX3m3vbIkrhyQzXFK3Mc&index=2
C1-C2高级动词精讲Advocate
音标：/ˈæd.və.keɪt/
含义：公开支持或提倡（to publicly support or recommend a particular policy or action）
例句：
Many doctors advocate a balanced diet and regular exercise.
The organization advocates for stricter environmental regulations.
She has long advocated reforming the education system.



Amplify
音标：/ˈæm.plɪ.faɪ/
含义：放大；增强（to make something louder or stronger; to increase the effect or impact）
例句：
The speaker used a microphone to amplify his voice.
Her passionate speech amplified the crowd’s enthusiasm.
Social media can amplify both positive and negative messages.



Articulate
音标：/ɑːˈtɪk.jə.leɪt/
含义：清晰表达；清晰发音（to express or explain something clearly; to pronounce words distinctly）
例句：
He struggled to articulate his complex ideas simply.
She articulates her words very clearly when teaching.
The report fails to articulate a clear strategy.



Comprehend
音标：/ˌkɒm.prɪˈhend/
含义：理解，领会（to understand the meaning or significance of something）
例句：
I cannot comprehend why he made that decision.
The child is too young to comprehend abstract concepts.
It’s important to fully comprehend the terms of the agreement.



Convey
音标：/kənˈveɪ/
含义：传达，表达（to communicate or express something to others）
例句：
Her smile conveyed more than words ever could.
The painting conveys a sense of deep loneliness.
Please convey my apologies to your family.



Corroborate
音标：/kəˈrɒb.ə.reɪt/
含义：证实，支持（to confirm or support a statement with evidence or testimony）
例句：
Several witnesses corroborated the victim’s account.
New research corroborates the original findings.
We need more evidence to corroborate this hypothesis.



Decipher
音标：/dɪˈsaɪ.fər/
含义：破译；辨认（to discover the meaning of something written in a code or difficult way）
例句：
Archaeologists are trying to decipher the ancient script.
I can’t decipher his messy handwriting.
It took experts years to decipher the secret code.



Differentiate
音标：/ˌdɪf.əˈren.ʃi.eɪt/
含义：区分，辨别（to distinguish or recognize differences between things）
例句：
It’s important to differentiate between facts and opinions.
The training helps doctors differentiate similar symptoms.
Can you differentiate these two species of birds?



Dissect
音标：/daɪˈsekt/
含义：剖析；仔细分析（to analyze or examine something in detail by breaking it down）
例句：
The professor dissected the poem line by line.
We need to dissect the problem to find the root cause.
The committee will dissect the proposal in detail.



Efface
音标：/ɪˈfeɪs/
含义：擦掉，抹去（to remove or erase something so it’s no longer visible）
例句：
Time had effaced the memories of that day.
The vandal tried to efface the historical monument.
Nothing could efface the impression she made on me.



Elaborate
音标：/iˈlæb.ə.reɪt/
含义：详尽阐述（to add more detail or explanation to something）
例句：
Could you elaborate on your previous statement?
She elaborated her plan with detailed diagrams.
The chef elaborated a simple recipe into a gourmet dish.



Exacerbate
音标：/ɪɡˈzæs.ə.beɪt/
含义：使恶化，加剧（to make a situation or problem worse）
例句：
His criticism only exacerbated the situation.
The drought has exacerbated food shortages in the region.
Stress can exacerbate existing health problems.



Extrapolate
音标：/ɪkˈstræp.ə.leɪt/
含义：推断，推知（to estimate or forecast something using existing knowledge）
例句：
We can extrapolate future trends from current data.
It’s dangerous to extrapolate from such a small sample.
The scientist extrapolated the results to the wider population.



Facilitate
音标：/fəˈsɪl.ɪ.teɪt/
含义：促进，使便利（to make something possible or easier to do）
例句：
The new software will facilitate faster communication.
A mediator was brought in to facilitate the discussion.
Good infrastructure facilitates economic development.



Galvanize
音标：/ˈɡæl.və.naɪz/
含义：刺激，激励（to shock or excite someone into taking action）
例句：
The tragedy galvanized the community into action.
Her inspiring speech galvanized the team to work harder.
The crisis galvanized public opinion against the government.



Integrate
音标：/ˈɪn.tɪ.ɡreɪt/
含义：整合，使融入（to combine or blend things together harmoniously）
例句：
The new students quickly integrated into the school community.
We need to integrate these different systems seamlessly.
The company aims to integrate sustainability into all operations.



Mitigate
音标：/ˈmɪt.ɪ.ɡeɪt/
含义：减轻，缓解（to make something less harmful or unpleasant）
例句：
Planting trees helps mitigate climate change effects.
The medicine can mitigate the symptoms but not cure the disease.
Safety measures are in place to mitigate potential risks.



Perceive
音标：/pəˈsiːv/
含义：认为；察觉（to think of something in a particular way; to become aware of something）
例句：
How do you perceive the current political situation?
I perceive a change in his attitude recently.
The public perceives the company as environmentally responsible.



Reconcile
音标：/ˈrek.ən.saɪl/
含义：使和解；调和（to make people become friends again; to make conflicting things compatible）
例句：
The couple finally reconciled after years of separation.
It’s difficult to reconcile his actions with his words.
We must find a way to reconcile these conflicting demands.



Scrutinize
音标：/ˈskruː.tɪ.naɪz/
含义：仔细检查，详审（to examine or inspect something very closely and thoroughly）
例句：
The committee will scrutinize every aspect of the proposal.
Her work was closely scrutinized by experts in the field.
Investors are scrutinizing the company’s financial reports.

title: Advanced Everyday English Phrases-1
content:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-M9vk7P13Jo&list=PLzMXToX8Kzqj3tX3m3vbIkrhyQzXFK3Mc
什么是押韵重叠词？核心概念
Rhyming Reduplication：通过改变单词开头的辅音或辅音簇，形成一个押韵的重复表达。
特点：非正式、有趣、轻松，能降低对话的正式程度。

作用与起源
人类大脑天生喜欢押韵的声韵模式。
常用于以轻松幽默的方式表达事物。

表达情绪与评价holy moly
词性 & 含义：感叹词，表示惊讶。
例句：Holy moly, there are a lot of examples!

jeepers creepers
词性 & 含义：感叹词，表示惊讶或震惊。源于避免使用”Jesus Christ”的亵渎语。
例句：Jeepers creepers, knock on the door before you just come in next time.

the bee’s knees
词性 & 含义：名词性习语，意思是极好的、出色的。
例句：Trust me, these expressions are the bee’s knees.

namby-pamby
词性 & 含义：形容词，形容人软弱、脆弱或过度情绪化（带侮辱性）。
例句：What a namby-pamby idea.

silly billy
词性 & 含义：名词，对行为不理智的小孩或宠物的昵称（注意语气，否则可能冒犯人）。
例句：Oh, you are a silly billy. Take that bucket off your head.

hoity-toity
词性 & 含义：形容词，形容人自命不凡、装腔作势。
例句：…so that you won’t sound hoity-toity.

3.2 描述状态与性质the nitty-gritty
词性 & 含义：名词，指本质的、重要的细节。
例句：Don’t worry. I’m going to show you the nitty-gritty.

itsy-bitsy
词性 & 含义：形容词，意思是非常非常小。
例句：We’re going to go from the itsy-bitsy… to the higgledy-piggledy.

higgledy-piggledy
词性 & 含义：形容词，形容混乱、杂乱无章。
例句：(同上)

lovey-dovey
词性 & 含义：形容词，形容恩爱、甜蜜（常指公开秀恩爱，即PDA - Public Displays of Affection）。
例句：Mum and dad are far too lovey-dovey.

fuddy-duddy
词性 & 含义：名词或形容词，形容人或事物老派、过时。
例句：Don’t be such a fuddy-duddy. Come out tonight.

helter-skelter
词性 & 含义：
名词：一种螺旋滑梯。
形容词：形容匆忙、混乱。


例句：We had a helter-skelter journey to the show.

willy-nilly
词性 & 含义：副词，形容做事无计划、随意、混乱。
例句：The new agency just sends its proposals willy-nilly.

行为与活动hocus-pocus
词性 & 含义：名词，指把戏、魔术或欺骗性的花招（巫师常用咒语）。
例句：Just be honest, stop all this hocus-pocus.

boogie-woogie
词性 & 含义：动词，意思是跳舞（略显过时）。
例句：Let’s go out next weekend and boogie-woogie.

okey-dokey
词性 & 含义：感叹词，意思是 “OK” 的轻松说法。
例句：Okey-dokey, let’s go.

押韵重叠词的特殊用法用于昵称
英国人喜欢用押韵词给人起绰号。
格式：形容词 + 人名，两者押韵。
示例：
Steady Eddie (稳重的埃迪)
Handy Andy (手巧的安迪)
Merry Geri (快乐的杰里)
Bonny Johnny (漂亮的约翰尼)
Smiley Kylie (微笑的凯莉)
Juicy Lucy (性感的露西 - Lucy自称)



童稚化表达
一种常见格式：将重复部分的首辅音替换成 “w”，显得非常孩子气。
示例：
Jenny-wenny
booky-wooky
doggy-woggy
homework-womework (Lucy开的玩笑)



Shm- 式重叠核心概念
Shm-reduplication：通过重复单词并将其首辅音替换为 “shm” 来构成。
起源：意第绪语。
用途：表示讽刺、怀疑、不屑一顾或作为感叹词，非常不正式。
警告：切勿在求职面试等正式场合使用。

常见示例rhyming shmyming
含义：用于强调，使概念更令人印象深刻。
语境：Lucy在视频中用它来总结这个话题。

money shmoney
含义：暗示钱并不重要或钱不是问题。

homework shmomework
含义：暗示有比做作业更好的事情。

bored shmored
含义：带有对抗性，表示**”我不相信你无聊”或“你不必无聊”**。

fancy schmancy
含义：讽刺某事**”装高级”或“浮华”**。
例句：”I feel fancy schmancy today.”

title: 4.Cloud Idioms
content:
一、主题：与“cloud（云）”相关的英语习语
1. Every cloud has a silver lining意思：黑暗中总有一线光明；塞翁失马，焉知非福。 解释：即使在困境中，也总有积极的一面。 例句：

I got fired yesterday, but at least I can spend more time writing my book. Every cloud has a silver lining. （我昨天被解雇了，但至少现在有时间写书了。祸中有福。） 补充：
还有一个反讽版说法：Every silver lining has a cloud，意思是“好事中也有坏的一面”，但 Lucy 建议还是用原版的积极表达。


2. To have your head in the clouds意思：脱离现实，空想，不切实际。 解释：形容一个人太理想化，不脚踏实地。 例句：

Lucy has her head in the clouds if she thinks she’ll reach 10,000 subscribers by the end of the year. （如果 Lucy 觉得年底能涨到 1 万订阅，那她真是太不现实了。）


3. On cloud nine意思：非常高兴，欣喜若狂。 解释：形容人处于极度幸福或兴奋的状态。 例句：

When I finished my exams last week, I was on cloud nine. （上周考试结束时，我高兴极了。）


二、总结记忆法


表达
中文意思
示例



every cloud has a silver lining
黑暗中总有光明
Don’t worry, every cloud has a silver lining.


have your head in the clouds
不切实际、爱幻想
He has his head in the clouds.


on cloud nine
欣喜若狂
She was on cloud nine after hearing the news.



这些习语都与“cloud（云）”相关，但情绪色彩不同：

积极乐观：every cloud has a silver lining
脱离现实：have your head in the clouds
极度开心：on cloud nine

title: 5 common expressions-3
content:
5 Common British English Expressions
① All right?** 意思：** 你好？你怎么样？（类似 “Hey, how are you?”） 📖 解释： 虽然字面意思是 “一切都好吗？”，但英国人平时用它来打招呼，不是真的在问你是否没事。 💬 对话例句：

A: All right?
B: Yeah, how are you? （A：你好啊？B：嗯，还好，你呢？）

注意： 不要误以为别人关心你出了什么事，这是日常寒暄！

② I’m easy** 意思：** 我随意 / 我都可以 📖 解释： 当别人让你做选择，而你无所谓时，就可以说 I’m easy. 💬 例句：

A: Would you prefer Italian or Chinese food tonight?
B: I’m easy. （A：今晚想吃意大利菜还是中餐？B：随便，都行。）


③ What’s he on about?意思： 他在说什么啊？（带点不耐烦或困惑） 📖 解释： on about = talking about，但语气通常是负面的。 💬 例句：

What’s he on about? = 他到底在说啥？ 适合在别人说了一堆莫名其妙的话时使用。


④ Bob’s your uncle意思： 就这样 / 大功告成 / 搞定！ 📖 解释： 用来结束一系列指令或步骤，表示事情完成得很顺利。 💬 例句：

To make a cup of tea, you boil the water, add a tea bag, let it brew, add milk and sugar, and Bob’s your uncle — you’ve got a cup of tea! （泡茶时：烧水、放茶包、泡一下、加奶和糖，搞定！）

** 小知识：** 这句成语的来源不确定，但在英国非常常见，带有一种“轻松完成”的感觉。

⑤ Easy peasy (lemon squeezy)意思： 太容易了 / 小菜一碟 📖 解释： 儿童口语，表示某事非常简单。 完整说法是：easy peasy lemon squeezy（押韵好玩）。 💬 例句：

A: How was the exam?
B: Easy peasy! （A：考试怎么样？B：太简单了！）

** 注意：** 不要在正式场合（比如工作面试）里用这个表达，只适合朋友之间轻松聊天。

总结表：


表达
含义
使用场合
示例



All right?
你好？
打招呼
“All right?” “Yeah, you?”


I’m easy
随便，都行
做选择时
“Pizza or sushi?” “I’m easy.”


What’s he on about?
他在说啥？
吐槽/困惑
“What’s he on about?”


Bob’s your uncle
搞定，大功告成
总结步骤
“Do this, then Bob’s your uncle!”


Easy peasy
很简单
非正式场合
“Exam? Easy peasy!”

title: 6. MUCH or MANY or A LOT OF
content:
MUCH or MANY or A LOT OF（可数名词与不可数名词的区别讲解）

一、核心区别


表达
适用名词类型
句式用法
示例
中文解释



much
不可数名词（uncountable）
常用于否定句和疑问句
I don’t have much water.Do you have much homework?
我没有太多水。你作业多吗？


many
可数名词（countable）
用于肯定、否定、疑问句
I have many apples.There aren’t many girls.
我有很多苹果。没有很多女孩。


a lot of / lots of
可数和不可数都可以
通用、自然、常用
I have a lot of apples.I have a lot of water.
我有很多苹果。我有很多水。



二、可数 vs. 不可数名词
Countable nouns 可数名词：能数清楚的事物。 → apple, window, girl, book, car ✅ 可以说：two apples, three books
Uncountable nouns 不可数名词：不能直接数的事物（通常是物质或抽象概念）。 → water, sugar, air, information, homework ❌ 不可以说：two waters, three informations


特殊例子：有时可以变为可数
在特定语境中，不可数名词可以被“单位化（unitize）”，变为可数。


Two coffees = two cups of coffee 两杯咖啡（而不是两种咖啡本身）
Two sugars = two sachets/cubes of sugar 两包 / 两块糖

👉 所以虽然 coffee 和 sugar 通常是不可数的，但当它们代表“份量”时，就可以变为可数。

三、为什么 “I have much water” 听起来不自然？
在日常会话中，肯定句里的 much 听起来太正式。 所以一般用 a lot of / lots of 替代。

推荐：

❌ I have much water.
✅ I have a lot of water. （我有很多水。）


💬 四、综合例句


错误表达 ❌
正确表达 ✅
中文意思



I have much apples.
I have many apples.
我有很多苹果。


I don’t have many water.
I don’t have much water.
我没有很多水。


I have much homework.
I have a lot of homework.
我作业很多。


Do you have many friends?
✅ 正确
你有很多朋友吗？


Do you have much time?
✅ 正确
你有很多时间吗？



✅ 总结口诀：
**“Many” 可数， “Much” 不可数， 肯定句多用 “A lot of”。

title: 7.PHRASAL VERBS! 4 Helpful Hints & 10 Useful Phrasal Verbs
content:
一、什么是 Phrasal Verb（短语动词）短语动词 = 动词（verb）+ 介词或副词（preposition/adverb） 例如：

look（动词）+ out（介词）→ look out
“I look out of the window.”（我向窗外看）
“Look out! There’s a car!”（小心！有辆车！）



在第二个例子中，意思完全变了，短语 look out 代表“当心、小心”。

二、四个重要提示（4 Helpful Hints）提示 1：不要逐词理解短语动词短语动词的意思往往不能从字面推出来。
例子：

turn on
“turn” 单独表示“转动”。
但 “turn on” 表示“打开、启动”。
“I turn on the television.”（我打开电视。）



 在听力或阅读考试中，不要逐个词理解，而要整体理解短语的意义。

提示 2：一个短语动词可能有多个意思同一个短语动词在不同语境中可能代表不同意思。
例子：take off

“Take off your jacket.” → 脱掉你的夹克（remove）
“The plane takes off soon.” → 飞机即将起飞（leave）

判断方法： 看上下文。如果看到 “jacket”，那是衣物 → remove。 如果看到 “plane”，那是飞机 → 起飞。

提示 3：有些短语动词是可分的（separable）某些短语动词可以把宾语放在中间或最后。
例子：put on（穿上）

“I put on my dress.”
“I put my dress on.” 意思完全一样。 但并不是所有短语动词都能分开，比如 “take off” 就不能分开。


提示 4：加介词可以让普通动词更口语化有时给普通动词加上介词，可以让语气更自然或更亲切。
例子：

“Eat your dinner.” → 普通
“Eat up your dinner.” → 更口语、更像对小孩说

同样的：

“Sit at the table.”
“Sit down at the table.” 意思相同，但第二个听起来更自然。


三、十个常见的短语动词（10 Common Phrasal Verbs）
Break up
“Tom and Joe have broken up.” → 他们分手了。
“School breaks up next week.” → 学校下周放假。


Carry on
“If you want to speak better English, carry on watching.”
继续（to continue）


Come on
“Come on! If you don’t hurry, we’ll miss the train.”
表示“快点、加油、催促”。


Find out
“I need to find out when the train leaves.”
意思是“查明、了解”。


Get on / Get along
“I get on very well with my flatmates.” → 我和室友相处很好。
“Get on badly” → 相处不好。
意思：相处、关系良好。


Grow up
“I grew up in a village near London.” → 我在伦敦附近的村庄长大。
“Grow up!” → 成熟点！（别幼稚）
意思：成长、变成熟。


Look after
“Can you look after my dog this week?”
意思：照顾、照看。


Pick up
“Your phone is ringing, pick it up!” → 接电话。
“Can you pick me up from work?” → 接我下班。
意思：捡起、接送、接电话。


Run out (of)
“Oh no! My phone battery has run out.”
意思：用尽、耗尽。


Throw away


“This milk is too old, I need to throw it away.”
意思：扔掉、丢弃。


四、总结
短语动词不是简单叠加词义，要整体理解。
语境（context）决定含义。
要注意哪些能分开，哪些不能。
多用听力和例句积累，形成语感。

title: 9.如何学习和记忆词汇
content:
1. 关键词：日常积累 + 观察 + 复习Lucy 的方法核心是把学习词汇融入生活，每天积累并复习，让大脑习惯用目标语言思考。

2. 方法步骤第一步：随时观察（Daytime Vocabulary Hunt）
目标：每天在生活中不断注意新词。
操作：
早上给自己一个提醒：今天我要寻找新单词。
可以贴便签在门上或冰箱上，手机设置提醒。


外出时看到不认识的单词或事物时，快速记录在手机上。
例如看到“bus stop”，不认识就记下；认识的就跳过。


全天持续观察，把遇到的新单词都记下来。


效果：训练大脑在第二语言中思考，形成语言敏感度。


第二步：整理单词（Evening Word Diary）
目标：将当天遇到的新单词系统化，形成自己的词汇记录。
操作：
回到家后，用笔记本做“单词日记”，建议每天两页。
写日期 + 简短日记（当天做了什么）。
把手机记录的当天不认识的单词整理到笔记本中。
上网查找单词的意思和发音，例如用 WordReference。
例：pigeon → Paloma；skyscraper → rascacielos。


每天完成一份完整的“新词列表”。




第三步：复习和内化
目标：通过复习，形成长期记忆。
操作：
第二天早上复习前一天的单词，回忆发音和意思。
随着时间积累，回看几个月前的单词，会发现很多以前不认识的词现在已经掌握。


效果：大脑不断确认已知词汇、标记未知词汇，词汇量稳步增长。


3. 核心理念
每天一点点，日积月累。
用目标语言思考，把新单词和真实情境联系。
及时记录 + 复习，让学习变成日常习惯。
查看词汇日记可以清楚看到自己的进步，增强学习动力。


4. Lucy 的小贴士
即使每天只积累 5–20 个新词，也能长期显著增加词汇量。
方法灵活：手机、便签、笔记本都可以，关键是坚持。
通过“词汇日记 + 复习”，大脑逐渐习惯用第二语言思考和表达。

title: 8.PHRASAL VERBS! 4 Helpful Hints & 10 Useful Phrasal Verbs
content:
Make or Do? How to Use Them Correctly1. Why They Are Confusing
Many students confuse make and do because in some languages (like Spanish), there is only one word for both actions (hacer).
Core difference:
Make → create something new.
Do → perform or complete a task.




2. Make (Creating / Producing)Use make when you create, produce, or generate something:
Daily life examples

Make a cup of tea / coffee → “Shall I make you one?”

Communication / Expressions

Make an offer / suggestion / promise / complaint
Make a mistake / discovery / noise

Business / Money

Make a profit / loss → “Last month I made a loss, but this month I want to make a profit.”
Make an investment / bet / fortune

Rule of thumb: Make = create something new

3. Do (Performing / Completing)Use do when you perform a task, duty, or activity:
Study / Exams

Do homework / tests / experiments / interviews / language courses

Housework / Chores

Do the shopping / dishes / ironing / housework

Performance / Actions

Do well / badly, do your best / worst
Do good → doing something positive (“Eating healthily does you good.”)


4. ExceptionsBusiness

General activity → do business with someone
Profit / loss → make a profit / make a loss

Housework

Most chores → do (do the laundry)
Specific → make the bed

Art

Drawings → do a drawing (not make)

Hair / Make-up

Do your hair / do your make-up


5. Quick Comparison


Category
Make
Do



Create something
make a cake, make a plan
×


Tasks / Chores
×
do homework, do the shopping


Performance / Actions
make a noise, make a decision
do well, do your best


Business / Money
make a profit, make an investment
do business


Hair / Beauty
×
do your hair, do your make-up


Exceptions
make the bed, make friends
do a drawing, do good


Lucy’s tip:

“Make = create something new. Do = perform a task.” Remember there are exceptions, so memorize collocations instead of only rules.

title: I use those words every day
content:
I use those words every day (www.youtube.com...)

on a roll

It’s best to do liaison (/liˈeɪzɒn/); otherwise, it’s a bit tongue-twisting

This lovely phrase on a roll means that you are on a streak of success. 一连串的成功

I have been productive all morning, I got everything done on my to-do list, I can’t believe it. I didn’t get sidetracked, I didn’t procrastinate, I’m on a roll. If you like to watch sports, you can also use this phrase, you might say, “They scored three goals in a row. They are on a roll!” Yes.



ahead of time

earlier than expected or required
eg:I finished my report ahead of time so I could relax


get out of hand.

What if I said, “during the week, dishes and laundry sometimes get out of control because we’re so busy.” Well, you can get the idea that there are dishes in the sink, dishes on the counter. There’s laundry in the basket, maybe there’s laundry even in the washer that hasn’t been dried yet.
There’s a little bit of chaos, because things get busy during the week. But we can use this great phrase instead, at least boost your vocabulary while you’re talking about chaos, you could say, “Dishes and laundry get out of hand during the week.” We can also use this to talk about people or places where people are involved. So take a look at this.
eg:I don’t want this task to get out of hand.


it’s too bad.

It’s too bad we don’t have a maid who could help to clean up our house.
it’s too bad that we elected someone else who is incompetent.
(I suggest It’s best not to use it. Sometimes it’s very difficult for us to distinguish between scenarios)


when the time comes for.

I’m learning English, so when the time comes for me to go to the US for vacation, I am going to be prepared.
When the time comes for Matilda, my baby to go to preschool, our house is going to be very quiet.


get some fresh air

Do you know what this means? It just means going outside.


come to think of it

Come to think of it, it is snack time. Let’s go eat something! 仔细想想，想来


to be spoiled 被宠坏

This is a way to truly show love, I think. So for me, I have several neighbors that are constantly sharing food together. I feel spoiled. I am spoiled that my neighbors share such good food with me. What do you think this means, to be spoiled? This just means that I am treated well. Maybe even above well. I am pampered. Someone is taking care of me more than is even necessary.
Your children are spoiled. We do sometimes use this negatively for children.


the fact that

The fact that he is late makes me angry.


accommodate

The hotel can accommodate up to 500 guests.（这家酒店最多可容纳500名客人。）
We will try to accommodate your special needs.（我们会尽力满足你的特殊需求。）
You should be able to accommodate your lifestyle to the new changes.（你应该能够使自己的生活方式适应这些新变化。 ）




Other word :

sidetracked 偏离轨道的

be/get sidetracked


procrastinate

拖延


grammatically

语法上的

title: 口语600句
content:
Maybe we’d better allow an extra month, so we won’t have to worry about being late.

Most of them remind me of the stuff that my nephew brings home from kindergarten.

Do you by any chance have a car available?

Frankly speaking, she got it working amazes me a lot

Frankly speaking 的本义是“真诚的，坦白的”。Frankly speaking 作为“坦白地说”，是口语中经常出现的固定搭配。
Amazed 的意思是“使……吃惊”。
Frankly speaking 在口语中常常用到，类似的表达还有 generally speaking、honestly speaking、comparatively speaking ，相对来说 theoretically speaking 理论来说 concretely speaking


I guess all those hours of practice in the past months are finally paying off.

Amaze somebody to do something. It amazes me to hear that you failed the exam

But in the letter, I just told him, frankly, I could no longer live with his poor management and stupid decisions

Thanks, but in view of the general response, you and I are definitely in the minority.

In view of 鉴于 考虑到
minority 少数的。


believe it a lot. That’s the last thing I’d ever want to do.

have something in view”：心中有什么打算或目的。例句：“He wanted to find a job, but has nothing particularly in view.”，意思是他想找份工作，可是没有什么具体的打算。“on view”：在展出，在陈列。例句：“Her paintings were on view at the new gallery.”“with a view to doing something”：为了……，指望……。例句：“They bought the cottage with a view to moving there when they retired.” 


It’s the first performance of the state Symphonic Orchestra in our city, so suit and tie is a must.

Named after the river that passes through the Congo, the Ebola virus originally manifested itself in the interior of Africa in 1976

If I were you, I’d skip it. We both have to get up earlier tomorrow, and anyway, I’ve heard it’s not as exciting as advertised

Of course, the conditions of work are very different. The polytechnic is offering a two - year contract, which could be renewed, but the language school is only offering a year’s contract. And that’s minor.

John really lost his temper in Mr. Brown’s class this morning.

But towards late afternoon, rain will spread from Scotland to cover most parts by midnight.

to make a difference to disrupt the status quo

Don’t forget the minus when you add them up. 求和时别忘了负号。

This follows successful talks between management and union representatives, which resulted in a new agreement on working hours and conditions.

What is the negative outlook on life and what is a positive outlook on life? When you want to leave this world, you’ll think about what is the biggest regret and comfort in your life, rather than how many fame and profits you have obtained and how many square - meter houses you have bought.
In this impetuous society, you should find out what you really want.

14. impetuous /ɪmˈpetʃuəs/adj — acting or done quickly and without thought or care中文释义: 冲动的；鲁莽的  
Examples:  

His impetuous behavior often gets him into trouble.  
She made an impetuous decision to quit her job.

Common Phrases:  

impetuous decision — 冲动的决定  
impetuous temperament — 鲁莽的性格

Synonyms:  

impulsive  
rash  
hasty

Word Root:  

Root: impet- (Latin: “attack, force”) → 与冲动、猛力相关  
Suffix: -uous 表形容词  
Formation: impet + -uous → impetuous  
Related Words:  
impetus — 推动力  
impetuosity — 冲动性

title: Bi站英语视频笔记--学习英语方法

content:
1. remediation /rɪˌmiːdiˈeɪʃən/n — the action of correcting a problem or improving a situation中文释义: 补救；改进措施；补习  
Examples:  

There’s going to have to be some remediation to fix the issue.  
The school offered remediation for students who failed the exam.

Common Phrases:  

remediation plan — 补救计划  
academic remediation — 学术补习

Word Root:  

Root: remed- (Latin: “to cure, remedy”) → 与治疗、补救相关  
Suffix: -ation 表示名词  
Formation: remed + -ation → remediation  
Related Words:  
remedy — 补救，治疗  
remedial — 补救的，矫正的




2. ordinary /ˈɔːrdəneri/adj — with no special or distinctive features; normal中文释义: 普通的，一般的  
Examples:  

She lived an ordinary but happy life.  
It was just an ordinary day at work.

Common Phrases:  

ordinary people — 普通人  
ordinary life — 普通生活

Word Root:  

Root: ordin- (Latin: “order, regularity”) → 与顺序、常规相关  
Suffix: -ary 表示形容词  
Formation: ordin + -ary → ordinary  
Related Words:  
ordinal — 顺序的  
coordinate — 协调




3. replicate /ˈreplɪkeɪt/v — to make an exact copy of something中文释义: 复制，重复  
Examples:  

The scientist tried to replicate the experiment.  
Artists often replicate famous paintings.

Common Phrases:  

replicate results — 重复实验结果  
replicate behavior — 模仿行为

Word Root:  

Root: plic- (Latin: “to fold, to twist”) → 与折叠、复制相关  
Prefix: re- 表示“再次”  
Formation: re + plic + -ate → replicate  
Related Words:  
replica — 复制品  
replication — 复制




4. extraordinary /ɪkˈstrɔːrdəneri/adj — very unusual or remarkable中文释义: 非凡的，特别的  
Examples:  

She has an extraordinary talent for music.  
The athlete achieved extraordinary results in the competition.

Common Phrases:  

extraordinary ability — 非凡的能力  
extraordinary event — 特别的事件

Word Root:  

Root: extra- (Latin: “beyond”) → 超出常规  
Suffix: -ordinary 表示形容词  
Formation: extra + ordinary → extraordinary  
Related Words:  
extraordinarily — 非凡地  
ordinary — 普通的




5. fraction /ˈfrækʃn/n — a small part or segment of something中文释义: 分数；一小部分  
Examples:  

Only a fraction of the students passed the exam.  
A tiny fraction of the population voted.

Common Phrases:  

a fraction of — 一小部分  
math fraction — 数学分数

Word Root:  

Root: fract- (Latin: “to break”) → 与分割、破裂相关  
Suffix: -ion 表示名词  
Formation: fract + -ion → fraction  
Related Words:  
fractional — 小部分的  
fracture — 骨折，裂缝




6. commission /kəˈmɪʃn/n — a group or body of people officially charged with a duty; also a payment for services中文释义: 委员会；佣金  
Examples:  

He earns money through sales commission.  
The government formed a commission to investigate the issue.

Common Phrases:  

European Commission — 欧洲委员会  
sales commission — 销售佣金

Word Root:  

Root: mittere (Latin: “to send”) → 与派遣、委托相关  
Prefix: com- 表示“共同”  
Formation: com + mission → commission  
Related Words:  
commissioner — 委员  
commissary — 代理




7. undertaking /ˈʌndərteɪkɪŋ/n — a task, project, or promise to do something中文释义: 承诺；事业，任务  
Examples:  

Building a bridge across the river is a major undertaking.  
She took on the undertaking of organizing the charity event.

Common Phrases:  

a difficult undertaking — 艰巨的任务  
give an undertaking — 作出承诺

Word Root:  

Root: take (Old English: “to grasp, seize”) → 与承担、接受相关  
Prefix: under- 表示“在下面，承担”  
Formation: under + taking → undertaking  
Related Words:  
undertaker — 承办者  
undertake — 承担




8. mission /ˈmɪʃn/n — an important task or purpose assigned to a person or group中文释义: 使命；任务  
Examples:  

Their mission is to provide clean water to the village.  
The team was sent on a secret mission.

Common Phrases:  

mission impossible — 不可能的任务  
life mission — 人生使命

Word Root:  

Root: mittere (Latin: “to send”) → 与派遣、任务相关  
Formation: mis + sion → mission  
Related Words:  
missionary — 传教士  
dismiss — 解散




9. operation /ˌɑːpəˈreɪʃn/n — the process of working, functioning, or performing surgery中文释义: 手术；运作，操作  
Examples:  

The patient is recovering well after the operation.  
The company launched a new operation in Asia.

Common Phrases:  

medical operation — 外科手术  
business operation — 业务运作

Word Root:  

Root: operari (Latin: “to work”) → 与工作、操作相关  
Suffix: -ation 表示名词  
Formation: oper + -ation → operation  
Related Words:  
operator — 操作员  
operative — 有效的，操作的




10. labor /ˈleɪbər/n — work, especially physical work; workforce中文释义: 劳动；劳动力  
Examples:  

Many jobs still require manual labor.  
Labor shortages are affecting the construction industry.

Common Phrases:  

manual labor — 体力劳动  
labor cost — 劳动力成本

Word Root:  

Root: labor (Latin: “work, toil”) → 与劳动相关  
Related Words:  
laborer — 工人  
laborious — 辛苦的



11. disseminate /dɪˈsemɪneɪt/v — to spread information, ideas, or knowledge widely中文释义: 传播，散布  
Examples:  

The internet helps to disseminate information quickly.  
The organization disseminates knowledge about healthy living.

Common Phrases:  

disseminate knowledge — 传播知识  
disseminate information — 传播信息

Word Root:  

Root: semin- (Latin: “seed”) → 与播种、传播相关  
Prefix: dis- 表示“分开、散布”  
Formation: dis + semin + -ate → disseminate  
Related Words:  
dissemination — 散布  
seminary — 神学院（原意“种子之地”）




12. reinforce /ˌriːɪnˈfɔːrs/v — to strengthen or support something中文释义: 加强，巩固  
Examples:  

The teacher used examples to reinforce the lesson.  
The government reinforced security measures after the incident.

Common Phrases:  

reinforce an idea — 加强观念  
reinforce security — 加强安全

Word Root:  

Root: force (Latin: “strength, power”) → 与力量相关  
Prefix: re- 表示“再次，加强”  
Formation: re + force → reinforce  
Related Words:  
reinforcement — 加强，援军  
enforce — 执行，实施




13. comprehensive /ˌkɑːmprɪˈhensɪv/adj — complete and including all or nearly all elements中文释义: 全面的，综合的  
Examples:  

The report provides a comprehensive overview of the problem.  
She has a comprehensive understanding of world history.

Common Phrases:  

comprehensive study — 综合研究  
comprehensive understanding — 全面理解

Word Root:  

Root: prehendere (Latin: “to grasp, seize”) → 与理解、掌握相关  
Prefix: com- 表示“完全”  
Formation: com + prehend + -sive → comprehensive  
Related Words:  
comprehend — 理解  
comprehension — 理解力




14. essential /ɪˈsenʃl/adj — absolutely necessary; fundamental中文释义: 基本的，必要的  
Examples:  

Water is essential for life.  
Good communication skills are essential for teamwork.

Common Phrases:  

essential skills — 必备技能  
essential requirements — 基本要求

Word Root:  

Root: esse (Latin: “to be”) → 与存在、本质相关  
Suffix: -tial 表示形容词  
Formation: essen + -tial → essential  
Related Words:  
essence — 本质  
essentially — 本质上




15. proficiency /prəˈfɪʃnsi/n — the ability to do something well; skill中文释义: 熟练程度  
Examples:  

She has high proficiency in English.  
Language proficiency is required for the job.

Common Phrases:  

language proficiency — 语言能力  
proficiency test — 熟练程度测试

Word Root:  

Root: facere (Latin: “to do, make”) → 与能力、技能相关  
Prefix: pro- 表示“向前”  
Formation: pro + ficien + -cy → proficiency  
Related Words:  
proficient — 精通的  
proficiently — 熟练地




16. mnemonic /nɪˈmɑːnɪk/n — a device or technique to aid memory中文释义: 助记符  
Examples:  

“HOMES” is a mnemonic for remembering the Great Lakes.  
She used a mnemonic to memorize the planets’ order.

Common Phrases:  

mnemonic device — 助记工具  
mnemonic rule — 助记规则

Word Root:  

Root: mnemon- (Greek: “mind, memory”) → 与记忆相关  
Suffix: -ic 表示名词或形容词  
Formation: mnemon + -ic → mnemonic  
Related Words:  
mnemonics — 记忆术  
amnesia — 健忘症




17. ubiquitous /juːˈbɪkwɪtəs/adj — present everywhere at the same time中文释义: 无处不在的  
Examples:  

Smartphones have become ubiquitous in modern life.  
The brand’s logo is ubiquitous across the city.

Common Phrases:  

ubiquitous technology — 无处不在的科技  
ubiquitous presence — 无处不在的存在

Word Root:  

Root: ubique (Latin: “everywhere”) → 与无处不在相关  
Suffix: -ous 表示形容词  
Formation: ubique + -tous → ubiquitous  
Related Words:  
ubiquity — 普遍存在  
ubiquitously — 无处不在地




18. upbeat /ˈʌpbiːt/adj — cheerful and optimistic中文释义: 乐观的，积极的  
Examples:  

She always remains upbeat despite challenges.  
The team maintained an upbeat attitude throughout the project.

Common Phrases:  

upbeat mood — 乐观的心情  
upbeat attitude — 积极态度

Word Root:  

Root: beat (Old English: “to strike, rhythm”) → 与节奏、心情相关  
Prefix: up- 表示“向上”  
Formation: up + beat → upbeat  
Related Words:  
upbeat music — 欢快音乐  
cheerful — 快乐的




19. resume /rɪˈzuːm/ (v)；/ˈrezəmeɪ/ (n)v — to begin again after interruption; n — a summary of work experience中文释义: 继续；简历  
Examples:  

He will resume work tomorrow.  
She updated her resume before applying for the job.

Common Phrases:  

resume work — 继续工作  
job resume — 工作简历

Word Root:  

Root: sumere (Latin: “to take up”) → 与重新开始、获取相关  
Prefix: re- 表示“再次”  
Formation: re + sume → resume  
Related Words:  
resumption — 重新开始  
summary — 总结




20. specific /spəˈsɪfɪk/adj — clearly defined or identified中文释义: 具体的，明确的  
Examples:  

Can you be more specific about your request?  
The instructions were very specific.

Common Phrases:  

specific details — 具体细节  
be more specific — 更明确

Word Root:  

Root: specere (Latin: “to look, see”) → 与看、明确相关  
Formation: spec + -ific → specific  
Related Words:  
specify — 具体说明  
specificity — 特性，明确性



21. specification /ˌspesɪfɪˈkeɪʃn/n — a detailed description of requirements, design, or standards中文释义: 规格，说明书  
Examples:  

The machine was built according to the specifications.  
Please read the product specification before using it.

Common Phrases:  

product specification — 产品规格  
technical specification — 技术说明书

Word Root:  

Root: spec (Latin: “to look, see”) → 与看、明确相关  
Suffix: -fication 表示名词  
Formation: spec + -ification → specification  
Related Words:  
specify — 具体说明  
specific — 具体的




22. indeed /ɪnˈdiːd/adv — truly; in fact中文释义: 的确，确实  
Examples:  

She is indeed a talented writer.  
Indeed, this is the best solution.

Common Phrases:  

yes indeed — 的确如此  
indeed true — 的确是真的

Word Root:  

Root: deed (Old English: “act, action”) → 与事实、行为相关  
Prefix: in- 强调  
Formation: in + deed → indeed  
Related Words:  
indeedly — 确实地（不常用）  
deed — 行为




23. rigorous /ˈrɪɡərəs/adj — extremely thorough and strict中文释义: 严格的，严厉的  
Examples:  

The athletes went through rigorous training.  
The review process is very rigorous.

Common Phrases:  

rigorous training — 严格训练  
rigorous standards — 严格标准

Word Root:  

Root: rigor (Latin: “stiffness, severity”) → 与严格、严谨相关  
Suffix: -ous 表示形容词  
Formation: rigor + -ous → rigorous  
Related Words:  
rigorousness — 严格  
rigid — 严格的




24. accurate /ˈækjərət/adj — correct, exact, and free from error中文释义: 准确的  
Examples:  

The data must be accurate to be useful.  
Make sure your measurements are accurate.

Common Phrases:  

accurate information — 准确信息  
accurate measurement — 精确测量

Word Root:  

Root: acuere (Latin: “to sharpen”) → 与精确、尖锐相关  
Formation: acu + -rate → accurate  
Related Words:  
accuracy — 精确性  
accurately — 精确地




25. rather than /ˈræðər ðən/conj — instead of中文释义: 而不是  
Examples:  

He chose tea rather than coffee.  
I would walk rather than take the bus.

Common Phrases:  

A rather than B — 选择 A 而不是 B  
would rather — 宁愿

Word Root:  

Root: rather (Old English: “more willingly”) → 与偏好相关  
Formation: rather + than → rather than  
Related Words:  
prefer — 更喜欢  
preference — 偏好




26. vaguly /ˈveɪɡli/adv — in a way that is not clear or exact中文释义: 模糊地；依稀  
Examples:  

I vaguely remember meeting her once.  
He vaguely understood the instructions.

Common Phrases:  

vaguely remember — 模糊地记得  
vaguely aware — 模糊地意识到

Word Root:  

Root: vagus (Latin: “wandering”) → 与不确定、模糊相关  
Suffix: -ly 表示副词  
Formation: vag + -ly → vaguely  
Related Words:  
vague — 模糊的  
vagueness — 模糊性




27. precisely /prɪˈsaɪsli/adv — exactly; accurately中文释义: 精确地，确切地  
Examples:  

That’s precisely what I mean.  
The instructions were precisely followed.

Common Phrases:  

precisely correct — 精确无误  
precisely defined — 明确定义

Word Root:  

Root: precisus (Latin: “cut short”) → 与精确、简明相关  
Suffix: -ly 表示副词  
Formation: precis + -ely → precisely  
Related Words:  
precision — 精确  
precise — 精确的




28. intuition /ˌɪntuˈɪʃn/n — the ability to understand something immediately, without reasoning中文释义: 直觉  
Examples:  

She had a strong intuition that he was lying.  
Trust your intuition when making decisions.

Common Phrases:  

trust your intuition — 相信你的直觉  
intuition-based — 基于直觉的

Word Root:  

Root: intueri (Latin: “to look at, consider”) → 与理解、洞察相关  
Formation: in + tuition → intuition  
Related Words:  
intuitive — 直觉的  
intuitively — 凭直觉地




29. vague /veɪɡ/adj — not clearly expressed, known, or defined中文释义: 模糊的，不明确的  
Examples:  

His explanation was too vague to understand.  
She had only a vague idea of the plan.

Common Phrases:  

vague idea — 模糊的想法  
vague description — 模糊的描述

Word Root:  

Root: vagus (Latin: “wandering”) → 与不确定、模糊相关  
Formation: vag + -ue → vague  
Related Words:  
vaguely — 模糊地  
vagueness — 模糊性




30. discipline /ˈdɪsəplɪn/n — a branch of knowledge; controlled behavior中文释义: 纪律；学科  
Examples:  

The school has strict rules of discipline.  
History is an interesting academic discipline.

Common Phrases:  

maintain discipline — 维持纪律  
academic discipline — 学术学科

Word Root:  

Root: disciplina (Latin: “instruction, knowledge”) → 与学习、纪律相关  
Formation: disciplina → discipline  
Related Words:  
disciplined — 有纪律的  
disciplinary — 纪律的



31. ultimately /ˈʌltɪmətli/adv — finally; in the end中文释义: 最终，最后  
Examples:  

Ultimately, the decision is yours.  
Success will ultimately depend on your effort.

Common Phrases:  

ultimately decide — 最终决定  
ultimately succeed — 最终成功

Word Root:  

Root: ultim- (Latin: “last, final”) → 与最后、终极相关  
Suffix: -ly 表示副词  
Formation: ultimate + -ly → ultimately  
Related Words:  
ultimate — 最终的  
ultimately responsible — 最终负责




32. precision /prɪˈsɪʒn/n — the quality of being exact and accurate中文释义: 精确，准确  
Examples:  

The work requires great precision.  
Precision is critical in scientific experiments.

Common Phrases:  

precision engineering — 精密工程  
with precision — 精确地

Word Root:  

Root: precisus (Latin: “cut short”) → 与精确相关  
Related Words:  
precise — 精确的  
precisely — 精确地




33. preface /ˈprefəs/n — an introduction to a book or speech中文释义: 序言；开端  
Examples:  

He wrote the preface to the book.  
The preface explains the purpose of the study.

Common Phrases:  

book preface — 书的序言  
preface remarks — 开场白

Word Root:  

Root: praefatio (Latin: “introduction”) → 与开端、前言相关  
Related Words:  
prefatory — 序言的  
preface to — ……的序言




34. premise /ˈpremɪs/n — a statement or proposition that forms the basis for reasoning中文释义: 前提，假设  
Examples:  

The argument is based on a false premise.  
His theory rests on the premise that humans are rational.

Common Phrases:  

basic premise — 基本前提  
false premise — 错误前提

Word Root:  

Root: premissa (Latin: “things sent before”) → 与先前提出的假设相关  
Related Words:  
premised on — 以……为前提  
assumption — 假设




35. frustration /frʌˈstreɪʃn/n — the feeling of being upset or annoyed because of inability to change or achieve something中文释义: 挫折，沮丧  
Examples:  

She felt frustration at her slow progress.  
His constant delays caused frustration among the team.

Common Phrases:  

deep frustration — 深深的挫折  
frustration with — 对……的沮丧

Word Root:  

Root: frustratio (Latin: “disappointment”) → 与挫折、失败相关  
Related Words:  
frustrate — 挫败  
frustrated — 感到沮丧的




36. significantly /sɪɡˈnɪfɪkəntli/adv — in a sufficiently great or important way中文释义: 显著地  
Examples:  

Sales have increased significantly this year.  
His health improved significantly after the treatment.

Common Phrases:  

increase significantly — 显著增加  
significantly better — 显著更好

Word Root:  

Root: significare (Latin: “to indicate, to mean”) → 与重要性、显著相关  
Suffix: -ly 表示副词  
Related Words:  
significant — 重要的  
significance — 重要性




37. impediment /ɪmˈpedɪmənt/n — an obstacle or hindrance中文释义: 障碍，阻碍  
Examples:  

Lack of funds is a major impediment to research.  
His speech impediment made communication difficult.

Common Phrases:  

speech impediment — 语言障碍  
impediment to progress — 阻碍进展

Word Root:  

Root: impedimentum (Latin: “hindrance”) → 与阻碍相关  
Related Words:  
impede — 阻碍  
impedimentary — 阻碍的

title: 美国人聊天反复使用的三十个短语
content:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vXZ0hkek5_g

Feel like - 想要做某事；感觉像…
I feel like I’ve died and gone to heaven.  
I feel like a drink.  
I feel like going for a walk.


Hit up (hit me up later) - 拜访；联系
Hit up a Traditional Chinese Medicine clinic.  
Hit me up later.  
Let’s hit up the new cafe tomorrow.


Laid back - 轻松自在，潇洒
Nothing worried him, he was really laid back.  
They seem more laid back than people here.  
I like people who are laid back.


Ask over - 请某人来自己家
I really must ask you over for dinner.
Let’s ask some friends over.  
We haven’t seen them for ages; why not ask them over for lunch?


Too bad … - 真可惜；真遗憾
Too bad only half my family’s gonna be there.  
It’s too bad that he couldn’t come.  
Too bad we missed the train.


Up for - 被提出；准备；被提名
This project is up for discussion.  
Who is up for the challenge?  
Are you up for a movie tonight?


Drop by - 顺便拜访
If you drop by, you visit someone informally.  
Drop by my place after work.  
I might drop by the shop later.


Sort of - 算是，有几分
It’s sort of a funny story.  
What sort of person would do that?  
There’s no way we could afford that sort of money.


Meet up - 约定在某处相会
Let’s meet up again next week.  
Who did they meet up with next?  
We should meet up for coffee.


Ask out - 约出去
How to ask out a girl on a date?  
You lived through it, time to ask out more guys.  
I asked her out for dinner.


Up to - 多种意思：至多 / 直到 / 由…决定 / 能胜任 / 正在做
Up to ten people can fit in this car.  
It’s up to you to decide.  
What have you been up to lately?


Go out - 出去玩 / 做某事
I go out with friends every weekend.  
If you go out to do something, you make a deliberate effort.  
Let’s go out tonight.


On me - 我请客
Dinner’s on me.  
Drinks are on me tonight.  
The coffee is on me.


Go for - 选择 / 去做
I typically go for spicy food.  
Go for a walk every morning.  
If you go for it, you will succeed.


Let me get a … - 让我拿 / 买 / 准备
Let me get a pencil.  
Let me get a hot dog.  
Let me get some water.


Come to - 苏醒 / 共计 / 谈到 / 突然想起
After a few minutes, he came to.  
The bill came to $50.  
It suddenly came to me that I left my keys.


I’ve got it - 我来付钱
I’ve got it this time.  
Don’t worry, I’ve got it.  
I’ll get the bill, I’ve got it.


Down for - 准备好做某事
I’m down for a movie tonight.  
Are you down for dinner?  
I’m down for anything.


Get it - 理解
I get it now.  
Do you get it?  
Finally, I get what you mean.


Chilling - 放松 / 恐惧
He is just chilling at home.  
That movie was chilling.  
I was chilling with friends.


Run into - 偶遇 / 遇到问题
We ran into some problems.  
I ran into my old teacher yesterday.  
They ran into trouble during the project.


Show around - 带着参观
The guide showed us around the museum.  
Can you show me around the campus?  
I’ll show you around the city.


Put off - 推迟 / 反感 / 脱下
They put off the meeting.  
The smell put me off my food.  
He put off his coat.


Screwed up - 搞砸 / 弄坏 / 紧张
He screwed up the exam.  
He is always screwed up before a performance.  
I really screwed up this project.


Chill out - 冷静 / 放松
You need to chill out.  
Let’s chill out at home.  
He just chills out after work.


Catch up - 叙旧 / 跟上进度
Let’s catch up today.  
We had a lot to catch up.  
Catch up with your emails.


Take up - 占用 / 接受 / 开始做
Sorry to take up your time.  
She took up the challenge.  
This table takes up too much space.


Make up - 补偿 / 和解 / 化妆
Make up with your ex.  
You should make up for lost time.  
She made up her face beautifully.


Put up with - 忍受
I wouldn’t put up with that.  
My girlfriend is a saint to put up with me.  
They have to put up with the noise.


Mix up / Keep on / Carry on - 搞混 / 继续
Don’t mix up the two seeds.  
Keep on until you get there.  
Carry on doing your work.

title: Vocabulary A系列常用单词
content:
📘 Vocabulary Notes (A 开头)1. from A to B
释义: from one place to another place
例句: The train goes from A to B without stopping.


2. from A to Z
释义: including everything there is to know about something
例句: He explained the project from A to Z.


3. aback
释义: to be shocked or surprised by sb/sth
例句: She was completely taken aback by his anger.


4. abacus
释义: a frame with small balls which slide along wires, used as a tool or toy for counting
例句: Children are learning to count with an abacus.


5. abalone
释义: 鲍鱼
例句: Abalone is considered a delicacy in many countries.


6. abandon
释义: 放弃，遗弃
常见形式: abandoned, abandonment
例句: He decided to abandon the plan.


7. abase
释义: to act in a way that shows you accept sb’s power over you; 表现卑微，卑躬屈膝
例句: He refused to abase himself before the king.


8. abashed
释义: embarrassed and ashamed because of sth you have done
反义词: unabashed
例句: He looked abashed at his mistake.


9. abate
释义: 减弱，减轻
派生: abatement
例句: The storm shows no signs of abating.
例句: Steps are to be taken to abate pollution.


10. abba
释义: 爸爸；阿爸


11. abbess
释义: 女修院院长


12. abbot
释义: 男修院院长


13. abbreviate
释义: 缩写
近义词: shorten
派生: abbreviation
例句: Where appropriate, abbreviated forms are used.


14. abdicate
释义: to give up the position of being a king or queen
例句: He abdicated in favor of his son.
例句: She was forced to abdicate the throne of Spain.


15. abdomen
释义: 腹部（胸部以下的身体部位，包含胃部）
派生: abdominal
例句: He was punched in the abdomen.


16. abduct
释义: to take sb away illegally, especially using force 绑架/诱拐
派生: abduction (n.), abductee, abductor
例句: The child was abducted by a stranger.
额外: abed (old use = in bed)


17. aberrant
释义: 违反常规的，异常的
派生: aberration (异常，反常现象)
例句: The police are investigating his aberrant behavior.


18. abet
释义: 教唆，煽动
例句: He was abetted in the deception by his wife.


19. abeyance
音标: /əˈbeɪəns/
释义: 搁置，暂时不用
例句: The project is being held in abeyance.


20. abhor
释义: 憎恨，厌恶（尤指道德原因，不用于进行时）
派生: abhorrence (n.), abhorrent (adj.)
例句: I abhor cruelty to animals.


21. abide
释义:
无法容忍: I can’t abide people with no sense of humor.
逗留，停留 (old use/formal): May joy and peace abide in us all.
遵守，遵循 (abide by sth): You have to abide by the rules of the club.


派生: abiding = lasting for a long time
例句: He couldn’t abide the thought of being cooped up in the office.


22. ability
释义: 能力；才能
常见搭配:
ability to do sth
a woman of her ability
do the job to the best of my ability


例句: Almost everyone has some musical ability.


23. abroad
释义: 在国外；到国外
例句: She studied abroad for two years.


24. absence
释义: 缺席；不在
例句: His absence was noticed by everyone.

title: 《肖申克的救赎》核心词汇整理-
content:
Core Themes

Redemption /rɪˈdempʃn/
Meaning: The act of being saved from sin, error, or evil; in the movie, it represents Andy’s moral and emotional liberation.
Example: The film’s title suggests that Shawshank is a place where redemption is possible, even in darkness.


Hope vs. Despair
Hope: Andy’s famous line: “Hope is a good thing, maybe the best of things.“
Despair: Brooks’ suicide shows the danger of losing hope.


Institutionalization /ˌɪnstɪˌtuːʃənəlaɪˈzeɪʃn/
Meaning: The psychological effect of long-term imprisonment, making freedom terrifying.
Example: Red says, “These walls are funny. First you hate ‘em, then you get used to ‘em.”



2. Prison Life Vocabulary

Parole /pəˈroʊl/: Conditional release from prison.
Example: Red is denied parole multiple times because he doesn’t “reform.”


Warden /ˈwɔːrdn/: The prison’s chief administrator.
Example: The warden pretends to care about justice but is corrupt.


Solitary Confinement /ˈsɑːlətɛri kənˈfaɪnmənt/: Punishment in isolation.
Example: Andy spends a month in solitary for playing Mozart over the speakers.



3. Key Plot Terms

Escape /ɪˈskeɪp/: Andy’s meticulous plan to break free.
Phrase: “A escape that took 19 years to plan.”


Innocence /ˈɪnəsns/: Andy’s wrongful conviction.
Example: “I didn’t kill my wife… but I wish I had.”


Perseverance /ˌpɜːrsəˈvɪrəns/: Andy’s slow progress with the rock hammer.
Quote: “Geology is the study of pressure and time.”



4. Famous Quotes & Phrases

“Get busy living, or get busy dying.”
Grammar: Imperative mood (command).


“Some birds aren’t meant to be caged.”
Metaphor: Freedom is innate.


“Fear can hold you prisoner. Hope can set you free.”

5. Words for Character Traits

Resourceful (Andy): Clever at solving problems (e.g., creating a fake identity).
Resilient (Red): Able to recover after decades in prison.
Corrupt (Warden Norton): Willing to break laws for power.

title: 《肖申克的救赎》核心词汇整理-1
content:
🎬 Dialogue & Expressions Notes1. rehabilitated
释义: 改过自新，使恢复正常生活
例句:
Do you feel you’ve been rehabilitated?
Yes sir, absolutely sir. I mean I learned my lesson. I can honestly say I am a changed man. I am no longer a danger to society. That’s God’s honest truth.




2. how’d it go?
释义: = how did it go? 常用于口语，表示“事情进展得怎么样？”
例句:
How’d it go?
Same old shit, different day.




3. I know how you feel.
释义: 我理解你的感受。
例句:
I know how you feel. I am up for rejection next week.




4. up for
释义: 有意愿做某事；准备要做某事
常见搭配:
I am up for rejection next week.
I am going to…
I am in the mood for…




5. rejection
释义: 拒绝，被拒绝
例句:
I got rejected last week.
Yeah, it happens.




6. bump me a deck
释义: （俚语/可能翻译误差）应为 borrow me a deck（借我一副牌/一包烟）
例句:
Bump me a deck.




7. get out of my face
释义: 滚开，别烦我（粗鲁用法，不建议使用）
例句:
Get out of my face, you are into me for five packs already.




⚠️ 注意：这句话属于粗俗监狱俚语，在日常生活里最好不要说。


8. con
释义: 诈骗犯；罪犯
例句:
There must be a con like me in every prison in America.

title: 《肖申克的救赎》核心词汇整理-2
content:
《肖申克的救赎》核心词汇整理1. redemption
释义: 赎回；救赎；补救；兑现

例句:

Redemption lies within.
He prayed for redemption from his sins.
The bonds are due for redemption next year.


2. repayment
释义: 偿还；报答

例句:

The repayment period for the loan is 20 years.
He made full repayment of the debt.
Kindness like that deserves repayment.


3. confrontation
释义: 对抗；冲突；对峙

例句:

Mr. Dufresne, describe the confrontation you had with your wife the night she was murdered.
The confrontation between workers and management escalated.
She tried to avoid a confrontation with her angry neighbor.


4. bitter
释义: 苦的；难以接受的；充满仇恨的；严寒的

例句:

It was very bitter. She said she was very glad I knew.
He spoke with a bitter tone.
Winters in Canada are bitterly cold.


5. sneaking around
释义: 鬼鬼祟祟地；偷偷摸摸

例句:

She hated all the sneaking around.
The kids were sneaking around the kitchen looking for cookies.
Stop sneaking around and just be honest with me.


6. divorce
释义: 离婚

例句:

She wanted a divorce in Reno.
They finally agreed to divorce after years of unhappiness.
Divorce is more common now than it was fifty years ago.


7. grant
释义: v. 授予；允许；承认 | n. 拨款；补助金

例句:

I told her I would not grant one.
The university granted him a scholarship.
She was granted permission to leave early.


8. hell
释义: 地狱；见鬼（粗话）

例句:

I’ll see you in hell before I see you in Reno.
What the hell are you doing?
Go to hell!


9. confront
释义: 面对；直面；对峙

例句:

I drove to his house to confront them, but they weren’t home.
She confronted him with the evidence.
We must confront the challenges ahead.


10. turnout
释义: 出席人数；集会；岔道

例句:

I parked in the turnout and waited.
The concert had a huge turnout.
Voter turnout was higher than expected.


11. intention
释义: 意图；目的

例句:

With what intention?
He had no intention of staying long.
Her original intention was to study medicine.


12. sober
释义: 清醒的；未醉的；冷静的

例句:

He appeared calm and sober during the trial.
It was a sober reminder of how dangerous driving can be.
She’s been sober for three years.


13. hazy
释义: 朦胧的；模糊的

例句:

It was very hazy. I was confused, drunk, and angry.
The details of the night are still hazy.
The mountains looked hazy in the distance.


14. riddle
释义: 谜语；神秘的人或事

例句:

Life is sometimes a riddle we cannot solve.
She was a riddle, a mystery I could never understand.
The old man asked us a riddle.


15. caliber
释义: 枪的口径；能力水平

例句:

A .38 caliber revolver was found at the scene.
He’s a writer of the highest caliber.
The school only accepts students of a certain caliber.


16. coincidence
释义: 巧合

例句:

It’s just a coincidence you find her murdered the same night.
It was pure coincidence that we met in Paris.
By coincidence, we were on the same flight.


17. maintain
释义: 保持；主张；维修

例句:

He maintains his innocence to this day.
The building is old but well maintained.
It’s hard to maintain friendships over long distances.


18. accused
释义: 被告

例句:

The accused was found guilty.
The accused will rise. （法庭常用语）
He is the accused in the murder trial.


19. remorseless
释义: 毫无悔意的；冷酷的

例句:

Cold-blooded, remorseless murder.
The dictator was remorseless in his cruelty.
She gave him a remorseless stare.


20. rehabilitation
释义: 改造；康复；恢复名誉

例句:

You feel you’ve been rehabilitated?
The rehab program helped him with drug rehabilitation.
The government focuses on rehabilitation of prisoners.


21. rejection
释义: 拒绝

例句:

I know how you feel. I am up for rejection next week.
Rejection can be very hard to deal with.
He faced rejection after his job interview.


22. con
释义: 骗子；诈骗

例句:

There must be a con like me in every prison in America.
He’s a real con artist.
Don’t fall for that con.
