下面是完整补充：

23.loan
音标: /loʊn/
释义: 贷款
例句:


The bank approved the loan.
He applied for a loan to buy a house.
Loan repayment can be difficult without steady income.


24.loans
音标: /loʊnz/
释义: 贷款（复数）
例句:


Student loans can take decades to pay off.
The company defaulted on several loans.
Banks tightened rules for granting loans.


25.payment
音标: /ˈpeɪmənt/
释义: 付款；支付
例句:


The payment is due next Monday.
She made a partial payment on the invoice.
Online payment methods are convenient.


26.refinancing
音标: /ˌriːˈfaɪnænsɪŋ/
释义: 重新融资；再贷款（通常为更好的条款）
例句:


They are refinancing their mortgage to get a lower rate.
Refinancing can reduce monthly payments.
Consider refinancing only if fees are justified.


27.loan repayment / repayment period
音标: /ˈriːpeɪmənt/ /rɪˈpeɪmənt ˈpɪriəd/
释义: 偿还（贷款）；还款期
例句:


The repayment period for the loan is 20 years.
Early loan repayment may save interest.
She set up automatic payments for loan repayment.


28.lover
音标: /ˈlʌvər/
释义: 情人；恋人
例句:


I get hazy where the cleaning woman shows up the following morning and find your wife in bed with her lover riddled with 38-caliber bullets. （电影原句节选）
He was jealous of her new lover.
The novel tells the story of two star-crossed lovers.


29.confused
音标: /kənˈfjuːzd/
释义: 困惑的；糊涂的
例句:


I was confused about the instructions.
He looked confused after hearing the news.
The explanation only made things more confused.


30. drunk
音标: /drʌŋk/
释义: 醉的；喝醉的
例句:


He admitted he was drunk that night.
Don’t drive if you are drunk.
The party got out of hand when people got drunk.


31. scare (v.)
音标: /sker/
释义: 使害怕；恐吓
例句:


I think mostly I wanted to scare them. （基于原文内容）
Loud noises scare small children.
The news scared many investors.


32. sobering up / sober
音标: /ˈsoʊbərɪŋ ʌp/ ; /ˈsoʊbər/
释义: 醒酒；（adj.）清醒的、严肃的
例句:


I was sobering up when I threw the gun into the river. （基于原文）
He’s been sober for three months now.
The accident was a sobering reminder to slow down.


33. along the way
音标: /əˈlɔːŋ ðə weɪ/
释义: 在途中；一路上；期间
例句:


Along the way, I threw my gun into the Royal River. （电影原句）
We met many interesting people along the way.
She learned a lot along the way to success.


34.clear (adj./v.)
音标: /klɪr/
释义: 清楚的；明确的；（v.）澄清
例句:


I’ve been very clear on this point. （基于原文）
The sky became clear after the storm.
Please clear up any misunderstandings.


35.hazy
音标: /ˈheɪzi/
释义: 朦胧的；模糊的
例句:


I get hazy where the cleaning woman shows up the following morning. （基于原文）
My memory of that day is hazy.
The horizon was hazy with mist.


36.show up
音标: /ʃoʊ ʌp/
释义: 出现；到场；露面
例句:


People show up and actually lobby for their candidates. （基于你给的例句）
He finally showed up an hour late.
Don’t bother if you’re not going to show up.


37. riddle / riddled with
音标: /ˈrɪdl/
释义: 谜；（v.）使充满漏洞/洞；riddled with = 充斥/布满（弹孔、问题等）
例句:


…find your wife in bed with her lover riddled with 38-caliber bullets. （电影原句）
The story is riddled with inconsistencies.
The old wall was riddled with holes.


38. caliber
音标: /ˈkælɪbər/
释义: 口径；水准、才干
例句:


A 38-caliber bullet was found at the scene. （基于原文）
He’s a leader of high caliber.
The rifle is of small caliber.


39. strike (v.) / strike me as
音标: /straɪk/
释义: 打击；袭击；给人印象（strike me as）
例句:


Does that strike you as a fantastic coincidence? （电影原句）
He strikes me as an honest man.
The news struck the whole town with shock.


40. coincidence
音标: /koʊˈɪnsɪdəns/
释义: 巧合；同时发生的事
例句:


Does that strike you as a fantastic coincidence, or is it just me? （电影原句）
It was a coincidence that we both wore red.
By coincidence, they arrived at the same time.


41. maintain
音标: /meɪnˈteɪn/
释义: 维持；坚持（某说法）；保养
例句:


Yet you still maintain you threw the gun into the river… （电影原句）
He maintains his innocence.
Keep the equipment maintained for safety.


42. convenient
音标: /kənˈviːniənt/
释义: 方便的；合适的；（有时含讥讽）便利的（“正好”为自己省事）
例句:


“That’s very convenient.” （电影语境常含讥讽）
Online banking is more convenient for many people.
It’s convenient that you finished early.


43. drag (v.)
音标: /dræɡ/
释义: 拖；打捞（river）；拖延
例句:


The police dragged that river for three days… （电影原句）
He had to drag the heavy box upstairs.
They dragged the issue out for months.


44. nary
音标: /ˈneəri/
释义:（古或口）一个也没有（= not a/ hardly any）
例句:


…and nary a gun was found. （电影原句）
There was nary a cloud in the sky.
He had nary a clue what to do next.


45. comparison
音标: /kəmˈpærɪsən/
释义: 比较；对照
例句:


So no comparison could be made between your gun and the bullets. （电影原句）
The comparison between the two reports is striking.
Don’t make comparisons — every case is unique.


46. bloodstained / bloodstain
音标: /ˈblʌdˌsteɪnd/ ; /ˈblʌdˌsteɪn/
释义: 血迹斑斑的 / 血迹
例句:


…the bloodstained corpses of the victims. （电影原句）
The shirt was covered in bloodstain.
The scene was bloodstained and horrifying.


47. corpses
音标: /ˈkɔːrpsɪz/
释义: 尸体（复数）
例句:


…the bloodstained corpses of the victims. （电影原句）
The rescuers found several corpses after the disaster.
Identification of the corpses took several days.


48. victims
音标: /ˈvɪktɪmz/
释义: 受害者；牺牲者
例句:


The victims were laid to rest.
Many victims needed medical help.
The charity supports victims of natural disasters.


49. footprints
音标: /ˈfʊtprɪnts/
释义: 脚印；足迹
例句:


We have footprints. （电影原句情境）
Footprints in the snow led to the cabin.
The detective photographed the footprints at the scene.


50. tire / tyre & tire tracks / tracks
音标: /taɪər/ (US) /ˈtaɪər/ (UK)
释义: 轮胎；轮胎痕迹（tire tracks） / 跑道，轨迹（tracks）
例句:


Tire tracks. （电影证据陈述）
The tire burst on the highway.
The snow preserved the truck’s tire tracks.


51. scatter
音标: /ˈskætər/
释义: 散开；撒布
例句:


Bullets scattered on the ground. （电影证据陈述）
The wind scattered the leaves across the yard.
The crowd scattered when the alarm sounded.


52. bear (v.)
音标: /ber/
释义: 承受；带有；生（孩子）；表现（bear oneself）等多义
例句:


The evidence bears his fingerprints. （电影语境）
Please bear with me for a moment.
The tree bears fruit every summer.


53.bourbon
音标: /ˈbɜːrbən/
释义: 波旁威士忌（酒名）；也可指波旁王朝（历史）
例句:


A broken bourbon bottle, likewise with fingerprints. （电影证据陈述）
He poured himself a glass of bourbon.
Bourbon is popular in the southern U.S.


54. likewise
音标: /ˈlaɪk-waɪz/
释义: 同样地；也；类似地
例句:


…a broken bourbon bottle, likewise with fingerprints. （电影证据句）
She felt the same way, and likewise he agreed.
The second experiment likewise failed.


55. sin
音标: /sɪn/
释义: 罪；罪孽（道德层面）
例句:


They had sinned, but was their crime so great as to merit death? （电影原句节选）
He repented for his sins.
Sin and guilt are central themes in the novel.


56. merit
音标: /ˈmerɪt/
释义: 值得；应受；价值；优点
例句:


Does their crime merit a death sentence? （电影质问）
The proposal merits serious consideration.
His work has merit despite its flaws.


57. revolver
音标: /rɪˈvɒlvər/
释义: 左轮手枪（revolver）
例句:


A revolver holds six bullets, not eight. （电影原句）
The suspect carried a small revolver.
The detective examined the revolver for fingerprints.


58. condone
音标: /kənˈdoʊn/
释义: 宽恕；容忍（多含批评）
例句:


You may understand, if not condone. （电影论述上下文）
Society cannot condone such violent acts.
He refused to condone cheating on exams.


59. revenge
音标: /rɪˈvɛndʒ/
释义: 报复；复仇
例句:


This was revenge of a much more brutal nature. （电影原句）
He sought revenge for the betrayal.
Revenge rarely brings peace.


60. brutal
音标: /ˈbruːtəl/
释义: 残忍的；野蛮的
例句:


The murders were brutal and cold-blooded. （电影原句上下文）
The attack was brutal and unprovoked.
The critics were brutally honest in their review.


61. cold-blooded / cold-blooded nature
音标: /ˌkoʊldˈblʌdɪd/
释义: 冷酷无情的（犯罪等）
例句:


This was a cold-blooded murder.
He acted in a cold-blooded manner.
Cold-blooded killers show no remorse.


62. stop to (do sth) / stop doing sth
音标: /stɒp/
释义: 停下来去（做某事） / 停止做某事
例句:


He stopped to reload so he could shoot them again. （电影原句描述）
Let’s stop to eat before we continue.
He stopped smoking last year.


63. particularly
音标: /pərˈtɪkjələrli/
释义: 特别地；尤其是
例句:


You strike me as a particularly icy and remorseless man. （电影原句）
She’s particularly talented at languages.
I’m not particularly fond of spicy food.


64. icy
音标: /ˈaɪsi/
释义: 冰冷的；冷淡的
例句:


He gave me an icy stare. （电影原句上下文）
The road was icy and dangerous.
Their relationship turned icy after the argument.


65. remorseless / remorse / remorselessly
音标: /rɪˈmɔːrsləs/ ; /rɪˈmɔːrs/
释义: 无悔意的；无情的 / 懊悔，自责
例句:


You strike me as remorseless. （电影原句）
He felt deep remorse for his actions.
The storm battered the coast remorselessly.


66.chills / chill (v./n.)
音标: /tʃɪlz/ ; /tʃɪl/
释义: 寒意；使寒冷/使恐惧
例句:


It chills my blood just to look at you. （电影原句）
A chill went down my spine when I heard the noise.
The news sent chills through the crowd.


67. hereby
音标: /ˌhɪrˈbaɪ/
释义: 特此；以此方式（正式）
例句:


I hereby order you to serve two life sentences… （电影原句）
I hereby certify that the information is true.
By this letter, I hereby resign my post.


68. back-to-back
音标: /ˌbæk tə ˈbæk/
释义: 连续的；背靠背的
例句:


He was ordered to serve two life sentences back-to-back. （电影原句）
They had back-to-back meetings all day.
The team won back-to-back championships.


69. so be it
音标: /soʊ bi ɪt/
释义: 就让它这样吧；照办吧（表示接受）
例句:


So be it. （电影原句/法庭或宣判时常用）
If that’s your decision, so be it.
He shrugged and said, “So be it.”


70. altercation / confrontational / showdown / brawl / disagreement
音标: /ˌɔːltərˈkeɪʃən/ ; /kənˈfrʌnteɪʃənəl/ ; /ˈʃoʊdaʊn/ ; /brɔːl/ ; /ˌdɪsəˈɡriːmənt/
释义: 争吵；对抗性的；摊牌；大打出手；分歧
例句:


The altercation outside the bar turned violent.
He adopted a confrontational tone during the meeting.
The showdown finally resolved the long dispute.

title: 理性之战
content:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qdzNKQwkp-Y第一部分：对“进步”的重新定义段落 1原文: A question that I often get is: Do you believe in progress? Well, I don’t believe in progress, at least not as a force in the Universe. To quote Fran Lebowitz, “I don’t believe in anything you have to believe in.” Because there isn’t any arc bending toward justice. There is no force that’s lifting us ever upward.
中文翻译: 我经常被问到一个问题：你相信进步吗？我不相信进步，至少不认为它是宇宙中的一种力量。引用 Fran Lebowitz 的话：“我不相信任何你必须相信的东西。”因为不存在任何朝向正义弯曲的弧线，也没有任何力量在不断把我们提升。
重点词汇/表达:

progress 进步
arc bending toward justice 指向正义的历史弧线
force lifting us upward 提升我们的力量

例句:

Many people have a naive belief in automatic progress.
The concept of an arc bending toward justice is philosophically appealing but empirically unproven.
There’s no invisible force lifting us upward - improvement requires conscious effort.

段落 2原文: Quite the contrary. The Universe often seems to be out to get us. There are parasites that want to eat us from the inside. There’s the laws of entropy: there are more ways for things to go wrong than to go right. There’s human nature: we were not selected by the processes of evolution to be particularly nice.
中文翻译: 恰恰相反。宇宙似乎总是与我们作对。有些寄生物想从内部吞噬我们。还有熵定律：事情出错的方式比顺利进行的方式更多。人性如此：我们不是通过进化选择出来的特别善良的物种。
重点词汇/表达:

entropy 熵，混乱度
human nature 人性
not selected to be nice 进化不选择善良

例句:

The second law of thermodynamics explains why entropy always increases.
Understanding human nature requires acknowledging our selfish instincts.
Evolution selects for survival, not necessarily for moral virtue.

段落 3原文: We have the capacity for revenge and exploitation. So that’s what’s lined up against us. But nonetheless, progress has happened. How do we explain that? What might seem like a miracle? The answer is ‘rationality.’ If people deploy their rationality, their cognition, their language with the goal of making other people better off — then the result, over time, is what we call ‘progress.’
中文翻译: 我们有复仇和剥削的能力，这就是对我们不利的因素。然而，进步仍然发生了。我们如何解释呢？这看似奇迹的东西是什么？答案是“理性”。如果人们运用理性、认知和语言，目标是让他人生活更好，那么随着时间推移，结果就是我们称之为“进步”的东西。
重点词汇/表达:

capacity for revenge and exploitation 复仇与剥削的能力
deploy rationality 运用理性
better off 境况更好

例句:

Humans possess both a capacity for great cruelty and great compassion.
Learning to deploy rationality in emotional situations is a mark of maturity.
Well-designed policies can make entire societies better off.

第二部分：理性的证据与挑战段落 4原文: Can we become more rational? It’s a pressing question because irrational beliefs lead to public health disasters. They can lead to wars and genocides. We’d really be better off if more of us were more rational. My name is Steve Pinker. I am a Professor of Psychology at Harvard University. My most recent book is called “Rationality: What It Is, Why It Seems Scarce, Why It Matters.”
中文翻译: 我们能变得更理性吗？这是一个紧迫的问题，因为非理性信念会导致公共卫生灾难，甚至引发战争和种族灭绝。如果更多人更理性，我们的生活会更好。我是 Steve Pinker，哈佛大学心理学教授。我的最新著作是《Rationality: What It Is, Why It Seems Scarce, Why It Matters》。
重点词汇/表达:

pressing question 紧迫问题
irrational beliefs 非理性信念
public health disasters 公共卫生灾难

例句:

Climate change is the most pressing question of our generation.
Irrational beliefs about vaccines have caused unnecessary outbreaks.
Addressing public health disasters requires evidence-based approaches.

段落 5原文: There is a capacity in us to become collectively more rational — we can just see it looking backwards. The three great things people desire are to be healthy, wealthy, and wise — and so we can start with those three. Health: meaning in life, is to be alive rather than dead, and longevity has vastly increased. We live more than twice as long as our ancestors.
中文翻译: 我们有能力变得集体更理性 — 回顾过去就能看到。人们渴望的三件大事是健康、财富与智慧 — 因此我们可以从这三件事入手。健康意味着活着而非死亡，而且寿命大幅增加。我们现在的寿命是祖先的两倍多。
重点词汇/表达:

collectively more rational 集体更理性
longevity 寿命
vastly increased 大幅增加

例句:

Societies can become collectively more rational through education and good institutions.
Medical advances have dramatically improved human longevity.
Agricultural productivity has vastly increased over the past century.

段落 6原文: So we have not just extra life, but as if we’ve been granted an extra life. Wealthy: 200 years ago, 90% of the world lived in extreme poverty. Today, about 9% of the world lives in extreme poverty, and that proportion falls every day. Wise: our natural state is illiteracy and ignorance. And until pretty recently, a small, aristocratic minority was able to read and write.
中文翻译: 所以我们不仅有额外的生命，好像我们被赋予了额外的生命。财富方面：200年前，全球有90%的人生活在极端贫困中。如今，大约只有9%的人生活在极端贫困中，这一比例每天都在下降。智慧方面：我们的自然状态是文盲和无知。直到不久前，只有少数贵族才能读写。
重点词汇/表达:

granted 被赋予
extreme poverty 极端贫困
illiteracy and ignorance 文盲与无知

例句:

Modern medicine has granted us decades of additional healthy life.
The dramatic reduction in extreme poverty is one of humanity’s greatest achievements.
Universal education is the antidote to illiteracy and ignorance.

段落 7原文: Now it’s a majority; 90% of the world’s population under the age of 25. As Barack Obama said a decade ago, “If you had to choose a period of history to live in, you’d pick now.” When people see my argument that many things have, on average, gotten better: the reaction is often, “Oh, it’s so nice. You’re an optimist.” And I always resist that. I don’t really consider myself an optimist, I just consider myself someone who looks at data rather than headlines.
中文翻译: 现在是大多数了：全球25岁以下人口占90%。正如奥巴马十年前所说：“如果你必须选择一个历史时期生活，你会选择现在。”当人们看到我说很多事情总体上变好了时，常常会说：“哦，好棒，你真乐观。”但我总是拒绝这个称呼。我不认为自己是乐观主义者，我只是认为自己是看数据而不是标题的人。
重点词汇/表达:

optimist 乐观主义者
looks at data 看数据
on average 平均而言

例句:

Being an optimist doesn’t mean ignoring problems, but recognizing progress.
Scientists must look at data objectively, not just confirm their biases.
On average, living standards have improved dramatically worldwide.

段落 8原文: Headlines are guaranteed to make you pessimistic, even cynical, or fatalistic because headlines are a non-random sample, of the worst things happening on Earth, at any given time. It’s when you plot data — and that includes gradual trends — you see with your own eyes how things have gotten better, as a fact about human history.
中文翻译: 标题保证会让你悲观，甚至愤世嫉俗或宿命论，因为标题是地球上最糟事情的非随机样本。当你绘制数据——包括渐进趋势——你就能亲眼看到事情变得更好，这是一条关于人类历史的事实。
重点词汇/表达:

pessimistic, cynical, fatalistic 悲观、愤世嫉俗、宿命论
non-random sample 非随机样本
plot data 绘制数据

例句:

Constant exposure to negative news can make anyone pessimistic.
Media coverage represents a non-random sample of reality.
When you plot data over decades, positive trends become visible.

第三部分：理性的悖论与叙事段落 9原文: Raising the question of how rational our species is bumps you immediately up against a kind of paradox: By some measures, we’ve never been more rational. We have evidence-based medicine, we’ve got 3D printing, we’ve got robotics, we’ve got artificial intelligence. That’s at the high end, but we are also seeing an awful lot of what you might call ‘Rationality Inequality.’ That is, at the other end, there’s an awful lot of fallacies and irrationalities.
中文翻译: 提出人类有多理性的问题，你会立即碰到一种悖论：按某些衡量标准，我们从未如此理性。我们有循证医学，有3D打印，有机器人技术，也有人工智能。这是高端例子，但我们也看到大量所谓的“理性不平等”。在另一端，有大量谬误和非理性行为。
重点词汇/表达:

paradox 悖论
evidence-based medicine 循证医学
Rationality Inequality 理性不平等

例句:

The paradox of modern life is our technological sophistication coexists with persistent superstition.
Evidence-based medicine has saved countless lives by rejecting tradition in favor of data.
Rationality Inequality may be as important as economic inequality in understanding social problems.

段落 10原文: There are conspiracy theories such as that the Covid vaccines are actually a plot by Bill Gates to inject microchips to surveil us. There’s the big lie that the American Election of 2020 was stolen in defiance of all evidence. How do you explain, or how do I explain — as someone who claims to know a thing or two about rationality — how the same species could indulge in both? Part of the answer is that we are storytelling animals. We spin narratives. That’s one of the ways that we make sense of the world.
中文翻译: 有些阴谋论，比如说新冠疫苗实际上是比尔·盖茨为了监控我们而注射芯片的阴谋。还有一个大谎言：2020年美国大选被窃取，完全无视证据。如何解释，或者说我如何解释——作为一个自称对理性略知一二的人——同一种物种为什么会同时沉迷于两者？部分原因是我们是讲故事的动物。我们编造叙事，这是理解世界的一种方式。
重点词汇/表达:

conspiracy theories 阴谋论
big lie 大谎言
storytelling animals 讲故事的动物

例句:

Conspiracy theories often provide simple explanations for complex problems.
The big lie technique relies on repetition rather than evidence.
As storytelling animals, humans naturally gravitate toward compelling narratives over dry statistics.

段落 11原文: But we do have a habit to fall back on narratives when it comes to big important questions, like: “How did the world come into being?” “What really happens in the White House?” The ones that make you and your tribe look great, that make your enemies look evil and stupid; that convey the right moral message. We often aren’t so committed to the factual voracity of beliefs that are more in the realm of mythology. We don’t care whether they’re true or false — they’re good things to believe, in that moral community.
中文翻译: 但在涉及重大问题时，我们确实习惯依赖叙事，例如：”世界是如何形成的？””白宫到底发生了什么？”那些让你和你的群体看起来很棒、让你的敌人看起来邪恶愚蠢的叙事；传达正确的道德信息。我们通常不会太在意那些更偏向神话领域信念的真实性。在那个道德群体中，它们是真是假无关紧要——信它们是一件好事。
重点词汇/表达:

tribe 部落，群体
moral community 道德共同体
factual voracity 事实准确性

例句:

People’s political views are often shaped by their tribe rather than independent analysis.
Within a moral community, certain beliefs function as social glue rather than factual claims.
The factual voracity of a story matters less than its social function in many contexts.

第四部分：理性如何运作段落 12原文: Now, if you’re a scientist, if you’re a historian, if you’re a journalist, you say, “Well, we could find the answers to those questions.” Cosmology tells us how old the Universe is, and government transcripts of conversations among leaders tell us what actually happened in the White House. Our feats of rationality come from institutions, in scientific societies, in government recordkeeping agencies, in responsible journalistic outlets.
中文翻译: 现在，如果你是科学家、历史学家或记者，你会说：”我们可以找到这些问题的答案。”宇宙学告诉我们宇宙有多古老，政府记录领导人谈话的文稿告诉我们白宫究竟发生了什么。我们的理性成就来自机构——科学社团、政府档案机构、负责任的新闻媒体。
重点词汇/表达:

cosmology 宇宙学
government transcripts 政府记录文稿
feats of rationality 理性成就

例句:

Cosmology has determined the universe’s age with remarkable precision.
Government transcripts provide invaluable historical records of decision-making.
Humanity’s greatest feats of rationality emerge from collaborative institutions.

段落 13原文: With this complicated apparatus, we can be, collectively, much more rational than any of us is individually. But it crucially depends on the rules of the game. Such as, admit you’re wrong when you’re wrong. If you have a claim, you gotta prove it — you can’t just jam it down people’s throats by authority, or power, or prestige. You gotta test your ideas with experiments or data. All of these rules and norms are what allow networks of us to blunder our way toward rationality and truth.
中文翻译: 有了这一复杂体系，我们集体上可以比任何个体更加理性。但这关键依赖于”游戏规则”。比如，当你错了就承认。如果你有一个主张，你必须证明它——不能仅凭权威、权力或威望强行灌输。你必须通过实验或数据检验你的想法。所有这些规则和规范让我们网络能够在犯错中逐步走向理性与真理。
重点词汇/表达:

apparatus 机构，体系
jam it down people’s throats 强行灌输
blunder our way toward 在犯错中前进

例句:

The scientific apparatus includes peer review, replication studies, and academic journals.
Good teachers explain concepts clearly rather than jamming them down students’ throats.
Science blunders its way toward truth through trial and error.

第五部分：培养理性的挑战段落 14原文: Can more people become more rational? A common answer among, you know, my people is “education!” We’ve got to teach kids critical thinking, but education can’t be the only part of the answer. And the reason is all too familiar: Students take a course, they cram for the exam. The exam is over, by the time the ink is dry, they forgot most of what they crammed for in the exam.
中文翻译: 更多人能变得更理性吗？在我圈子里一个常见答案是”教育！”我们必须教孩子批判性思维，但教育不能是唯一答案。原因很熟悉：学生上课，为考试死记硬背。考试结束，墨水刚干，他们就忘了大部分死记硬背的内容。
重点词汇/表达:

critical thinking 批判性思维
cram for the exam 为考试死记硬背
the ink is dry 墨水刚干（比喻立即）

例句:

Teaching critical thinking requires fundamentally rethinking how we educate.
Cramming for exams produces short-term recall but not genuine understanding.
The information is often forgotten once the ink is dry on the test paper.

段落 15原文: It can’t just be you take a course in critical thinking. It’s gotta be that the principles of critical thinking are just part of what it means to be a decent, thinking, respectable person. So if you’re writing an op-ed, or a blog post, or commenting on a tweet, or even having an argument in a bar, you gotta keep those principles of critical thinking. It’s gotta be part of our norms. It’s gotta be, like, not going out naked in public.
中文翻译: 不仅仅是上批判性思维课程，而是批判性思维的原则必须成为成为一个正直、有思考能力、有尊严的人的一部分。因此，无论你写专栏、博客、评论推文，甚至在酒吧争论，都必须坚持这些批判性思维原则。它必须成为我们的规范之一，就像不要在公共场合裸奔一样。
重点词汇/表达:

decent, thinking, respectable person 正直、有思想、可敬的人
op-ed 专栏文章
norms 社会规范

例句:

A decent, thinking, respectable person changes their mind when presented with good evidence.
Writing an op-ed requires making logical arguments supported by evidence.
Social norms around rationality are as important as formal education.

第六部分：希望与展望段落 16原文: Several hundred years ago people believed in the existence of werewolves and unicorns. People believed that you could placate angry gods by sacrificing innocent people. People would take the whole family out to laugh at the insane in an asylum for entertainment on a Sunday afternoon. So there is hope. It doesn’t happen instantly. It doesn’t happen to everyone. They’ll always be pockets of irrationality. But we can try to kind of steer the ocean liner, slowly and gradually, in the direction of greater rationality.
中文翻译: 几百年前，人们相信狼人和独角兽的存在。人们认为可以通过牺牲无辜者来安抚愤怒的神灵。人们会带上全家在星期日下午去笑看精神病院里的病人作为娱乐。所以还是有希望的。这不会瞬间发生，也不会发生在每个人身上。总会有非理性的存在。但我们可以尝试慢慢地、逐步地引导”巨轮”，朝着更理性的方向前进。
重点词汇/表达:

placate angry gods 安抚愤怒的神灵
pockets of irrationality 非理性的角落
steer the ocean liner 引导巨轮（比喻稳步推进）

例句:

Ancient civilizations tried to placate angry gods through various rituals.
Even in highly educated societies, pockets of irrationality persist.
Social change requires patience - we must steer the ocean liner gradually.

Where exactly do you work?

What do you like most about [place / work]?你最喜欢…什么？

What do you like most about your city?
What do you like most about your job?

That sounds interesting, tell me more.

I can relate to that我能理解

I can relate to that, I’ve been there.

I can relate to your experience.

婉转问名字 / 询问I didn’t catch your name我没听清你的名字

Sorry, I didn’t catch your name.

What’s your full name?你全名是什么？

May I know your full name?
Can I have your full name?

Do you go by a nickname?你有昵称吗？

Do you go by a nickname?
Can I call you Les?
Do you prefer a shorter name?

How do you spell that?怎么拼写？

How do you spell that?

I’m not sure how to spell it.

Is it okay if I call you…?我可以叫你…吗？

Is it okay if I call you Anna?

Do you mind if I call you Les?

寒暄 / 问近况How’s the weather there?那边天气怎么样？

How’s the weather there today?
Is it sunny or rainy?

How’s your family doing?你家人都好吗？

How’s your family doing?

Are you busy these days?最近忙吗？

Are you busy these days?
Have you been busy lately?

Did you have a good weekend?周末过得好吗？

How was your weekend?
What did you do over the weekend?

How’s work / school going?工作/学习怎么样？

How’s work going?
How’s school?

询问兴趣 / 喜好Do you like [place / activity]?你喜欢…吗？

Do you like this cafe?
Do you like watching movies?

Have you tried [food / activity]?你尝试过…吗？

Do you often watch movies?

提出建议 / 邀请Do you want to…? / Would you like to…?你想…吗？

Do you want to grab coffee?
Would you like to join us for dinner?
Do you want to go for a walk?

How about…? / What about…?…怎么样？

How about going to the park?
What about watching a movie tonight?
How about having lunch together?

Let’s… / Why don’t we…?我们…吧

Let’s grab a coffee.
Why don’t we go hiking this weekend?

Are you free…? / When are you free?你什么时候有空？

Are you free this evening?

It was nice talking to you / I enjoyed our chat很高兴聊天

It was nice talking to you.
I enjoyed our chat, see you later.
Great talking with you, take care.

title: 绝望的主妇--
emperor|grove|lack|traditional
content:
learn from bilibili

英语单词整理emperor
词义：皇帝
词源：emper (命令, 统治) + -or (人/物)
例句：
The emperor ruled the country wisely. 皇帝明智地治理国家。
He was crowned emperor at the age of 18. 他18岁时加冕为皇帝。
The emperor’s decisions affected millions. 皇帝的决定影响了数百万民众。
The emperor maintained absolute authority. 皇帝保持绝对权力。




grove
词义：小树林
例句：
We walked through a small grove of olive trees. 我们穿过一片橄榄树林。
The grove provided shade for the picnic. 小树林为野餐提供了阴凉。
A grove of cherry trees blooms beautifully in spring. 一片樱花林在春天开得很美。
He built a cabin near a pine grove. 他在一片松树林旁建了木屋。




lack
词义：缺乏
例句：
The project failed due to lack of funding. 项目因缺乏资金而失败。
There is a lack of interest in classical music among young people. 年轻人对古典音乐缺乏兴趣。
Lack of sleep affects your health. 缺乏睡眠影响健康。
He struggled due to a lack of experience. 他因缺乏经验而吃力。




traditional
词义：传统的
例句：
They wore traditional clothes for the festival. 他们穿着传统服装庆祝节日。
Traditional medicine has been used for centuries. 传统医学已经使用了几百年。
She followed the traditional way of cooking. 她遵循传统烹饪方式。
Traditional values shape the society. 传统价值观塑造了社会。




pardon
词义：原谅；赦免
例句：
The president pardoned the prisoner. 总统赦免了囚犯。
I beg your pardon, could you repeat that? 对不起，你能重复一遍吗？
She pardoned him for his mistake. 她原谅了他的错误。
He asked for pardon from the court. 他向法院请求宽恕。




regent
词义：摄政王，评议员
例句：
The regent took over until the king was old enough. 摄政王接管政务直到国王年满。
The Regent Hotel has a great view. 丽晶酒店视野极佳。
Thailand punishes insulting the regent harshly. 泰国对侮辱摄政者的行为惩罚严格。
The regent carried out reforms efficiently. 摄政王高效实施了改革。




burgeon
词义：v. 发芽；n. 芽
例句：
Confidence began to burgeon later in life. 随着年龄增长，信心开始增强。
The city began to burgeon with new technology. 城市因新技术而迅速发展。
These efforts were insufficient to contain the burgeoning crisis. 这些努力不足以抑制迅速扩散的危机。
A new economy is burgeoning in this region. 该地区的新经济正在迅速发展。




argue
词义：辩论；争论；说服
例句：
They argued about politics for hours. 他们就政治争论了好几个小时。
She argued successfully for higher pay. 她成功争取到了加薪。
We argue logically to solve problems. 我们用逻辑争论来解决问题。
Don’t argue with someone who won’t listen. 不要与不听的人争论。




barely
词义：几乎不，勉强
例句：
She barely passed the exam. 她勉强通过了考试。
I could barely hear him over the noise. 噪音太大，我几乎听不见他说话。
He barely managed to finish on time. 他勉强按时完成。
The car barely fits in the garage. 车几乎放不进车库。




methane
词义：甲烷
例句：
Methane is a potent greenhouse gas. 甲烷是一种强效温室气体。
The farmer collects methane from cow dung. 农民从牛粪中收集甲烷。
Methane emissions contribute to climate change. 甲烷排放会导致气候变化。
Scientists are studying methane on Mars. 科学家正在研究火星上的甲烷。




hierarchy
词义：等级制度，层次体系
例句：
She rose up the corporate hierarchy quickly. 她在公司等级制度中迅速晋升。
Social hierarchies exist even in deserts. 即便在沙漠中也存在社会等级。
He’s high in the management hierarchy. 他位居管理层要职。
Understanding hierarchy helps improve organization. 了解等级制度有助于改善组织结构。




anarchy
词义：混乱；无政府状态
例句：
After the revolution, anarchy ruled. 革命后，处于无政府状态。
Economic anarchy scourged the post-war world. 战后世界遭遇经济混乱。
There was complete anarchy in the classroom. 班上完全一片混乱。
The collapse of authority led to anarchy. 权威的崩溃导致了混乱。




guidance
词义：指导
例句：
All activities took place under the guidance of an experienced tutor. 所有活动在经验丰富导师指导下进行。
She followed the guidance carefully. 她仔细遵循指导。
The project proceeded under proper guidance. 项目在正确的指导下推进。
Students seek guidance on career choices. 学生寻求职业指导。




easy-going
词义：随和，悠闲
例句：
Athenians have a very easy-going attitude to life. 雅典人对生活非常随和。
He is easy-going and friendly. 他随和且友善。
Her easy-going nature made her popular. 她随和的性格使她很受欢迎。
The boss is surprisingly easy-going. 老板出乎意料的随和。




electrical / electronic
词义：电的 / 电子的
例句：
Electrical appliances must be handled safely. 电器必须安全使用。
He studied electrical engineering. 他学习电气工程。
Electronic devices are everywhere. 电子设备无处不在。
Electronic voting machines were tested. 电子投票机进行了测试。




chronic
词义：长期的，慢性的
例句：
He suffers from chronic back pain. 他患有慢性背痛。
Chronic stress affects health. 长期压力影响健康。
Chronic diseases require ongoing care. 慢性疾病需要持续护理。
Smoking can cause chronic respiratory problems. 吸烟会导致慢性呼吸系统问题。




desirable
词义：令人满意的，理想的
例句：
A stable job is desirable. 稳定的工作很理想。
Physical fitness is desirable for everyone. 身体健康对每个人都很重要。
This property is highly desirable. 这处房产非常理想。
Being bilingual is a desirable skill. 双语能力是一种理想技能。




明白，我将继续把你剩下的单词整理成 MD格式，保持前面相同风格，包括词义、例句和中文翻译。下面是接下来的部分：

consortium
词义：财团，联合体
例句：
A consortium of banks funded the new project. 一个银行财团为新项目提供资金。
The consortium includes five leading companies. 该联合体包括五家领先公司。
Universities formed a research consortium. 大学组成了研究联合体。
The consortium aimed to improve regional infrastructure. 财团的目标是改善地区基础设施。




buckle
词义：n. 扣子；v. 扣住
例句：
Please buckle your seatbelt before takeoff. 起飞前请系好安全带。
He buckled his shoes tightly. 他把鞋带系紧。
The bridge began to buckle under the weight. 桥在重量下开始弯曲。
She fastened the buckle on her bag. 她扣好包上的扣子。




curry
词义：咖哩饭菜；咖哩粉
例句：
We had chicken curry for dinner. 我们晚餐吃了鸡肉咖喱。
This curry is too spicy for me. 这个咖喱对我来说太辣了。
He bought curry powder at the market. 他在市场买了咖喱粉。
Curry is a popular dish in India. 咖喱是印度的流行菜肴。




subconscious
词义：潜意识
例句：
Fear can influence behavior through the subconscious. 恐惧会通过潜意识影响行为。
Dreams reveal our subconscious thoughts. 梦境揭示我们的潜意识想法。
She acted on a subconscious impulse. 她根据潜意识的冲动行动。
Subconscious motives often guide decisions. 潜意识动机经常引导决策。




subliminal
词义：潜意识的，下意识的
例句：
Subliminal messages can affect behavior. 潜意识信息可以影响行为。
The ad used subliminal techniques. 广告使用了潜意识技巧。
He sensed a subliminal threat. 他感受到一种下意识的威胁。
Subliminal cues can influence perception. 潜意识提示可以影响感知。




chamber
词义：室；室内；私人房间
例句：
The king met his advisors in a private chamber. 国王在私人会议室会见顾问。
The chamber was filled with smoke. 房间里充满烟雾。
He worked in a chamber deep underground. 他在地下深处的房间工作。
The hotel has luxury chambers for guests. 酒店为客人提供豪华客房。




frequent
词义：频繁的
例句：
He is a frequent visitor to the library. 他经常去图书馆。
Traffic jams are frequent in the city. 城市里经常堵车。
Frequent exercise improves health. 经常锻炼有益健康。
She suffers frequent headaches. 她经常头痛。




prospect
词义：前景，展望
例句：
The job offers good career prospects. 这份工作提供良好的职业前景。
Investors are optimistic about market prospects. 投资者对市场前景持乐观态度。
The prospect of travel excites him. 旅行的前景让他兴奋。
She considered the prospects carefully. 她仔细考虑了前景。




prosperous
词义：繁荣的，兴旺的
例句：
They live in a prosperous city. 他们住在繁荣的城市。
A prosperous economy benefits everyone. 繁荣的经济惠及每个人。
The region has become prosperous over the years. 多年来，该地区变得繁荣。
He had a prosperous business career. 他有一个成功繁荣的商业生涯。




desperate
词义：绝望的
例句：
She made a desperate attempt to save him. 她做出了绝望的尝试去救他。
People were desperate for food after the disaster. 灾后人们急需食物。
He felt desperate about his job situation. 他对自己的工作状况感到绝望。
Desperate times call for desperate measures. 苦境需要采取极端措施。




prosperity
词义：繁荣，兴旺
例句：
Economic prosperity benefits all citizens. 经济繁荣惠及所有公民。
The nation enjoyed years of prosperity. 国家经历了多年的繁荣。
Education contributes to prosperity. 教育促进繁荣。
Peace is essential for prosperity. 和平对繁荣至关重要。




purpose
词义：目的
例句：
He acted on purpose. 他是故意这么做的。
The purpose of the meeting is to discuss plans. 会议的目的是讨论计划。
Life without purpose can feel empty. 没有目标的生活会感觉空虚。
She pursued her purpose relentlessly. 她不懈追求自己的目标。




variety
词义：多样性，种类
例句：
A variety of fruits is available in the market. 市场上有各种水果。
The program offers a wide variety of activities. 该项目提供多种活动。
Variety makes life interesting. 多样性使生活有趣。
There is a variety of opinions on this issue. 对这个问题有各种不同意见。




immigration
词义：移民，移居
例句：
Immigration has shaped the country’s culture. 移民塑造了国家文化。
The government introduced new immigration laws. 政府出台了新的移民法。
Immigration can boost the economy. 移民可以促进经济发展。
Many seek better opportunities through immigration. 许多人通过移民寻找更好的机会。




natural
词义：自然的，天生的
例句：
The body has natural defense mechanisms. 人体有自然的防御机制。
She was the natural choice for the position. 她是这个职位的理想人选。
He has a natural talent for music. 他有天生的音乐才能。
Natural disasters can strike unexpectedly. 自然灾害可能会突发。




nature
词义：自然；本性；种类
例句：
Science can reveal many mysteries of nature. 科学能揭示自然界的许多奥秘。
It’s human nature to worry about change. 对变化感到担忧是人之常情。
Let nature take its course. 顺其自然吧。
The exact nature of the problem is unclear. 问题的确切性质不清楚。




bet
词义：打赌；you bet = 当然
例句：
You bet I will help you. 当然，我会帮你。
He made a bet on the football game. 他在足球比赛上打赌。
I bet it will rain tomorrow. 我打赌明天会下雨。
She bet all her savings on the venture. 她把所有积蓄都投在了这项事业上。




presume
词义：假定，推测
例句：
I presume you have completed your work. 我假定你已经完成工作。
Presume that the system is secure. 假定系统是安全的。
One should not presume too much. 不应过度推测。
Let us presume he agrees. 我们假设他同意。




resume
词义：简历；重新开始
例句：
Please send me your resume. 请把你的简历发给我。
He will resume work after the holiday. 假期后他将恢复工作。
The game will resume shortly. 比赛很快将重新开始。
She resumed her studies after a break. 她休息后重新开始学习



好的，我继续把剩余单词整理成 MD 格式：

physician
词义：内科医生
例句：
The physician diagnosed him with flu. 医生诊断他得了流感。
She visited a physician for a routine check-up. 她去看医生做例行检查。
Physicians recommend regular exercise. 医生建议定期锻炼。
He consulted a physician about his symptoms. 他就症状咨询了医生。




physical
词义：身体的，实体的
例句：
Regular physical activity improves health. 定期身体活动有助于健康。
The store has a physical location downtown. 这家商店在市中心有实体店。
She experienced physical pain after the accident. 她在事故后感到身体疼痛。
Physical strength is important for athletes. 身体力量对运动员很重要。




equal
词义：平等的，相等的
例句：
All citizens are equal under the law. 所有公民在法律面前平等。
He treats everyone as an equal. 他把每个人都当作平等对待。
Equality in education is essential. 教育平等至关重要。
The two sides made equal contributions. 双方做出了同等贡献。




resort
词义：胜地；求助
例句：
The island is a popular tourist resort. 该岛是一个受欢迎的旅游胜地。
In desperate times, they resorted to extreme measures. 在绝望时，他们求助于极端手段。
The hotel is a luxury resort. 这家酒店是豪华度假胜地。
Resort to violence should be avoided. 应避免诉诸暴力。




leadership
词义：领导力
例句：
Effective leadership is key to a successful team. 有效的领导力是团队成功的关键。
She demonstrated strong leadership skills. 她展现了强大的领导能力。
Leadership requires vision and decision-making. 领导力需要远见和决策能力。
Good leadership inspires others to follow. 优秀的领导力能激励他人跟随。




equity
词义：股票；公平
例句：
He invested in company equity. 他投资了公司的股票。
The principle of equity ensures fair treatment. 公平原则确保公正对待。
Home equity increased over the years. 多年来房产净值增加了。
Equity in education is a global challenge. 教育公平是全球性挑战。




excavate
词义：挖掘
例句：
Archaeologists excavate ancient ruins. 考古学家挖掘古代遗址。
They excavated the site for construction. 他们为施工挖掘了该地。
The workers excavated a trench. 工人们挖了一条沟。
Excavation revealed historical artifacts. 挖掘揭示了历史文物。




cave
词义：洞穴
例句：
Explorers entered a deep cave. 探险者进入了一个深洞穴。
Bats live in caves. 蝙蝠生活在洞穴中。
The cave walls were covered in ancient drawings. 洞穴墙上覆盖着古老的壁画。
Tourists can visit the limestone cave. 游客可以参观石灰岩洞穴。




nuclear
词义：核能的；原子能的
例句：
Nuclear energy can produce electricity. 核能可以产生电力。
The country has a nuclear power plant. 该国有一座核电站。
Nuclear weapons pose global risks. 核武器带来全球风险。
Scientists study nuclear reactions in labs. 科学家在实验室研究核反应。




词根词汇背单词整理 https://www.bilibili.com/video/BV1sA411Y7UJ/?p=3&vd_source=8db2bf2ffb3ab22965fccab48d4389ba)
code
解释：密码；法典  
短语：dress code 着装规范  
词根/衍生：来自拉丁语 codex，意为“书本、法典”  
例句：  
The company has a strict dress code. 公司有严格的着装规范。  
He broke the secret code. 他破译了秘密密码。  
Learning the building code is essential for architects. 学习建筑法规对建筑师很重要。  
The criminal ignored the moral code. 罪犯无视道德规范。




seek
解释：寻求；寻找；试图  
词根：来自古英语 sēcan，意为“去寻找”  
例句：  
I seek for advice before making a decision. 我在做决定前寻求建议。  
They seek to improve their skills through practice. 他们努力通过练习提升技能。  
She is seeking a new job in the city. 她正在寻找城市里的新工作。  
The researchers seek to find a solution to the problem. 研究人员试图找到问题的解决方案。




item
解释：条目；项目；物品  
短语：category item 分类项目  
例句：  
Each item in the list must be checked. 列表中的每一项都必须检查。  
This store sells a variety of items. 这家商店出售各种物品。  
I forgot to pack one item from my suitcase. 我忘记收拾行李中的一件物品。  
The news report covered several items today. 今日的新闻报道包含了几个条目。




crown
解释：王冠；皇冠  
例句：  
The crown was set with precious jewels ─ diamonds, rubies and emeralds. 王冠上镶嵌着稀世珍宝——有钻石、红宝石、绿宝石。  
He was crowned king at the age of 18. 他在18岁时加冕为国王。  
The crown symbolizes authority and power. 皇冠象征权威和力量。  
She wore a golden crown on her head. 她头戴金色王冠。




effort
解释：努力；尝试  
短语：make an effort 努力  
例句：  
We need to make an effort to reduce waste. 我们需要努力减少浪费。  
She put a lot of effort into her presentation. 她在演讲上付出了很多努力。  
The project succeeded thanks to everyone’s effort. 项目成功得益于每个人的努力。  
Learning a new language requires constant effort. 学习一门新语言需要持续努力。




point
解释：要点；指向；分数  
例句：  
He made an important point during the meeting. 他在会议中提出了一个重要观点。  
Can you point to the right direction? 你能指出正确的方向吗？  
The student scored full points on the test. 学生在考试中得了满分。  
The main point is that we must act now. 关键点是我们必须立即行动。




review
解释：复习；回顾；评论  
例句：  
I need to review my notes before the exam. 我需要在考试前复习笔记。  
The manager reviewed the team’s performance. 经理回顾了团队的表现。  
She wrote a positive review of the book. 她写了该书的好评。  
Let’s review the plan before finalizing it. 在最终确定前，让我们回顾一下计划。




fabrication
解释：制造；建造；虚构的谎言  
词根：来自拉丁语 fabricare，意为“制造，建造”  
例句：  
The factory specializes in metal fabrication. 这家工厂专门从事金属制造。  
The story was a complete fabrication. 这个故事完全是虚构的。  
Fabrication of evidence is illegal. 伪造证据是违法的。  
He excelled in the fabrication of complex machines. 他在复杂机械制造方面很出色。




series
解释：系列；连续；一连串  
例句：  
This TV series has five seasons. 这部电视剧有五季。  
A series of meetings will be held next week. 下周将举行一系列会议。  
The company released a series of new products. 公司推出了一系列新产品。  
The athlete won a series of competitions. 这名运动员赢得了一连串比赛。




variation
解释：变化；变动；变体  
例句：  
There is a wide variation in temperature across the country. 全国各地温度差异很大。  
Genetic variation is important for evolution. 遗传变异对进化很重要。  
The menu includes several variations of the same dish. 菜单中有同一道菜的几种变体。  
She noticed slight variations in the pattern. 她注意到图案中有细微的变化。

title: 20. sponsored| rationale |composition
content:
1. sponsored /ˈspɒnsərd/adj — supported financially or promoted by someone or an organization中文释义: 赞助的；由……支持的。  
Examples:  

The event was sponsored by a major tech company.  
She attended a sponsored seminar on digital marketing.

Common Phrases:  

sponsored event — 赞助活动  
sponsored program — 赞助项目  
sponsored post — 付费推广文章

Synonyms:  

funded  
supported  
promoted

Word Root:  

Root: sponsor (Latin: “to pledge, to promise”) → 与支持、担保相关  
Suffix: -ed 表示形容词  
Formation: sponsor + -ed → sponsored  
Related Words:  
sponsor — 赞助，资助  
sponsorship — 赞助，资助




2. rationale /ˈræʃənəl/n — the reasons or principles that explain a particular decision, belief, or action中文释义: 基本理由；根本原因。  
Examples:  

The rationale behind the policy is to reduce waste.  
Can you explain the rationale for your decision?

Common Phrases:  

underlying rationale — 潜在原因  
rationale for — ……的理由  
clear rationale — 清晰理由

Synonyms:  

reason  
explanation  
justification

Word Root:  

Root: ratio (Latin: “reason, calculation”) → 与理由、原因相关  
Formation: ratio + -nale → rationale  
Related Words:  
rational — 理性的  
rationalize — 合理化




3. composition /ˌkɒmpəˈzɪʃən/n — the act of writing, creating, or putting together something; the makeup or arrangement of something中文释义: 作品；作文；构成。  
Examples:  

She submitted a composition for the writing contest.  
The composition of the committee includes five members.

Common Phrases:  

musical composition — 音乐作品  
written composition — 书面作文  
chemical composition — 化学成分

Synonyms:  

structure  
arrangement  
creation

Word Root:  

Root: componere (Latin: “to put together”) → 与组成、排列相关  
Suffix: -tion 表示名词  
Formation: compose + -tion → composition  
Related Words:  
compose — 组成，创作  
composed — 镇静的，组成的

title: 3.堅持每天30分鐘練習英語聽力2個月
content:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=usRXxVuGPcw
英语口语听力精华 - 对话式学习文档
日常安排与时间1.

A: What time is good for you? (什么时间你方便？)
B: Anytime after three. (三点以后都可以。)

2.

A: I must get these out before noon. (我必须在中午前把这些寄出去。)  
B: Wait outside whenever you have time is fine. (在外面等吧，你什么时候有空都行。)

外表与状态3.

A: You look good in everything. (你穿什么都好看。)
B: I don’t care about the way I look. (我不在乎我的外表。)

4.

A: You’ve got dirt on your face. (你脸上有脏东西。)
B: Okay, I need to freshen up. (好吧，我需要梳洗一下。)

5.

A: How old do I sound? (我听起来多大年纪？)
B: Well, you look about 20. (嗯，你看起来大约20岁。)
A: Age is just a number. (年龄只是一个数字。)

6.

A: How do you keep in shape? (你是怎么保持身材的？)
B: I sleep a lot. (我睡很多。)
A: What kind of exercises do you do? (你做什么运动呢？)
B: I used to play a lot of tennis. These days I just work out. (我过去常打网球。最近我只是健身。)

7.

A: You’ve lost a lot of weight. (你瘦了很多啊。)  
B: I was a bit overweight back then. (我那时候是有点超重。)

8.

A: Those shoes are on point. (这双鞋真时髦。)
B: Yeah, I bought them yesterday. (是的，我昨天买的。)

9.

A: Your hair looks nice. (你头发看起来不错。)
B: I just got it cut this morning. (我今天早上刚剪的。)

10.

A: You have incredibly thick hair. (你的头发真浓密。)
B: I have split ends. (我头发有分叉。)

11.

A: Blue is your color. (蓝色很衬你。)
B: Tuck your shirt in. (把你的衬衫塞进去。)

个人情况与能力12.

A: What kind of person are you? (你是个什么样的人？)
B: I’m such an idiot. (我真是个傻瓜。)
A: He’s got a great personality. (他个性很好。)
B: That’s the way I am. (我就是这样的人。)

13.

A: What else is good about you? (你还有什么优点？)
B: I have a good memory. (我记忆力很好。)

14.

A: What’s he like at basketball? (他篮球打得怎么样？)
B: We need another player. Um, don’t ask him to play. He’s more of a soccer player. (我们还需要个队员。嗯，别叫他打。他更像是个踢足球的。)

15.

A: Is he any good at math? (他数学好吗？)
B: You’ll have to ask him. (你得自己去问他。)

16.

A: Can you change a tire on a car? (你会换车胎吗？)
B: Yeah, I think I can do that. Um, actually I’ve never driven a car. I’ll just call a taxi. (是的，我想我会。嗯，其实我从没开过车。我还是叫出租车吧。)
A: Well, what about the car keys? (那车钥匙呢？)
B: Drop them off at the table. (放桌上就行。)

17.

A: Where did you put it? (你把它放哪儿了？)
B: Right on the shelf. (就在架子上。)

18.

A: Would you like another one? (你想再来一个吗？)
B: I couldn’t possibly eat anymore. (我实在吃不下了。)
A: What are you afraid of? (你怕什么？)
B: I’ve been eating too much. (我吃得太多了。)
A: Don’t forget about the dishes. (别忘了洗碗。)
B: I’ll be sure to clean up after dinner. (我保证饭后会收拾干净。)

19.

A: What does your mom do? (你妈妈是做什么的？)
B: She works at a diner. (她在小餐馆工作。)
A: I’m not a picky eater. (我不挑食。)
B: I don’t like mushrooms overall. (我总的来说不喜欢蘑菇。)

20.

A: What are your feelings about him? (你觉得他怎么样？)
B: He can be such a jerk sometimes. (他有时候真是个混蛋。)
A: We spoke on the phone the other day. (我们前几天通过电话。)
B: Just put him on the phone. (让他接电话。)

21.

A: Why don’t you rest a little? (你为什么不休息一下？)
B: I want a day off. (我想放一天假。)

22.

A: Do you have any hobbies? (你有什么爱好吗？)
B: My main interest is jazz. (我主要对爵士乐感兴趣。)

23.

A: What is it that you’re looking for? (你在寻找什么？)
B: I’ve always wanted to be a singer. (我一直想当个歌手。)

24.

A: I’m not sure how the others feel. (我不确定其他人怎么想。)
B: I’ll find out soon enough. (我很快就会知道的。)

25.

A: When is the application due? (申请什么时候截止？)
B: It’s due next Friday. (下周五截止。)
A: I don’t know how to fill it out. Could you help me out with it? (我不知道怎么填。你能帮帮我吗？)
B: I’ve always been lazy. (我一直很懒。)
A: Don’t be so hard on yourself. (别对自己太苛刻了。)

观点与反应26.

A: It’s a little scary. (有点吓人。)
B: I think you can handle it. (我觉得你能应付。)

27.

A: This is just not my kind of thing. (这真不是我的菜。)
B: Keep your mind open. (保持开放的心态。)

28.

A: I’ve watched every episode. It’s one of my favorites. (每一集我都看了。这是我最喜欢的之一。)
B: How was your reaction? (你觉得怎么样？)
A: I thought it was the best movie ever. (我觉得这是有史以来最好的电影。)
B: The movie is starting to drag on. (电影开始变得拖沓了。)
A: That’s just what I was thinking. (我也是这么想的。)
B: Do you find it fun? (你觉得好玩吗？)
A: I’m not into action movies. (我不喜欢动作片。)

29.

A: She said it’s not good enough. (她说这不够好。)
B: She’s got a point. (她说得有道理。)

30.

A: Could you stay a little later? (你能晚点走吗？)
B: You know I don’t have any plans after work anyway. (你知道我反正下班后也没安排。)
A: That’s a great idea. It’ll be a lot of fun. I’ve got tickets already. (好主意。一定会很有趣。我已经有票了。)

31.

A: Where should I meet you? (我在哪儿见你？)
B: I’ll meet you halfway. (我们找个中间点见吧。)
A: The bus comes every half hour. (公交车每半小时一班。)
B: Are you sure about it? (你确定吗？)
A: We were late and you got angry. (我们迟到了，你当时很生气。)
B: I’ll make sure to leave on time. (我会确保准时出门的。)

冲突与解决32.

A: She screwed up everything. (她把一切都搞砸了。)
B: She was just trying to help. (她只是想帮忙。)

33.

A: He never lets me go out. (他从不让我出门。)
B: He wants to keep you out of trouble. (他是想让你远离麻烦。)

34.

A: We got into a fight today. (我们今天吵架了。)
B: I don’t want any trouble. (我不想惹麻烦。)
A: Where were you when it happened? (事发时你在哪儿？)
B: I was out in the street. (我在外面的街上。)

35.

A: Did I wake you up? (我吵醒你了吗？)
B: I’m a light sleeper. (我睡觉很轻。)

36.

A: I’m sorry about last night. (昨晚的事很抱歉。)
B: I think I was probably overreacting. (我想我可能反应过激了。)
A: She’s always had a problem with me. (她一直对我不满。)
B: You two need to talk it out. (你们俩需要好好谈谈。)

提议与请求37.

A: Do you mind if I sit here? (你介意我坐这儿吗？)
B: I don’t see why not. (我看没什么不行的。)

38.

A: It’ll be nice in the park today. (今天公园里应该很不错。)
B: I think I’ll go for a walk. (我想我会去散个步。)

39.

A: I’ve had enough of that food. I want something else. (那种食物我吃够了。我想要点别的。)
B: You can’t go around looking like that. (你不能就这个样子到处走。)
A: Dad, I’m 17. I can wear what I want. (爸，我17岁了。我想穿什么就穿什么。)

40.

A: I got caught up at work. (我被工作耽搁了。)
B: I’ve been waiting for 20 minutes. (我已经等了20分钟了。)

41.

A: Watch where you’re going. (看着点路。)
B: I’m in a terrible rush. (我急着赶时间。)
A: I’m trying to get some work done. (我正想干点活呢。)
B: I didn’t realize it bothered you. (我没意识到打扰到你了。)

42.

A: Do you mind if I took your picture? (你介意我给你拍张照吗？)
B: Well, that’ll be a dollar. (嗯，那要一美元。)

43.

A: What would you like for Christmas? (你想要什么圣诞礼物？)
B: I’m hoping for a brand new bike. (我想要一辆全新的自行车。)

44.

A: You’re not alone anymore. (你不再是孤单一人了。)
B: I’ll be there in a minute. (我马上就到。)

45.

A: Can I borrow your pen? (能借你的笔吗？)
B: I’m afraid mine has just run out. (恐怕我的刚好没水了。)

46.

A: It’s a little hot in here. (这里有点热。)
B: Let me turn on the air conditioning. (让我把空调打开。)

47.

A: Let’s wait a bit longer. (我们再等一会儿吧。)
B: I don’t think he’s gonna show up. (我觉得他不会来了。)
A: Well, that’s surprising. I didn’t expect him to show up either. (哦，真意外。我也没指望他会来。)

48.

A: I’m afraid the cost will be 200. (恐怕费用是200。)
B: I thought you said it would be 50. (我记得你说的是50。)

49.

A: That guy really irritates me. (那家伙真让我恼火。)
B: They’re all like that. (他们都一个样。)

50.

A: I don’t think I can make it. (我觉得我做不到/赶不上了。)
B: You’re doing fine. (你做得很好。)

51.

A: I got my driver’s license today, mom. (妈，我今天拿到驾照了。)
B: I’m behind you all the way. (我完全支持你。)

52.

A: My friend’s car got stolen. (我朋友的车被偷了。)
B: When did it happen? (什么时候发生的？)

53.

A: Sorry about the mess. (不好意思，这里很乱。)
B: No problem, you should see my apartment. (没事，你真该看看我的公寓。)

54.

A: My internet is having issues right now. It’s lagging a little bit. (我的网络现在有问题。有点卡。)
B: I’ll let you go. (那我先不打扰你了。)
A: I gotta go back to work. (我得回去工作了。)

55.

A: Can you shut the door please? (请问能关下门吗？)
B: We’re just gonna leave it open. (我们就开着吧。)

56.

A: I locked myself out of my house. I was hoping you could help me. (我把自己锁在门外了。希望你能帮帮我。)
B: I’m sorry you feel that way. I think we can move on. (我为你这么想感到遗憾。我想我们可以翻篇了。)

57.

A: I’d like to take you to lunch. (我想请你吃午饭。)
B: Why don’t we all get dinner? (我们何不一起去吃晚饭呢？)
A: Do you want to go to the movies tonight? (今晚想去看电影吗？)
B: I’d rather just stay home. (我宁愿呆在家里。)
A: You need to loosen up and have fun. I’m gonna put some music on. (你需要放松找点乐子。我来放点音乐。)

58.

A: Can I borrow the car tonight? (今晚能借车用吗？)
B: Yeah, if you take out the trash first. (可以，如果你先把垃圾倒了。)

59.

A: I need your advice. (我需要你的建议。)
B: You don’t usually come to me for advice. (你通常可不来找我拿主意。)

60.

A: Are you all right taking the bus home? (你坐公交回家行吗？)
B: I can drive you home, you know. (我可以开车送你回家的，你知道。)
A: I just came from work. I know how busy you are. (我刚下班。我知道你有多忙。)

61.

A: Are you nervous about your trip? (你对旅行感到紧张吗？)
B: I’ve never been this far away from home before. (我以前从没离家这么远过。)

62.

A: I couldn’t have done it without you. (没有你我不可能完成。)
B: I enjoyed working on it with you. (我很享受和你一起完成它。)
A: Thank you for all of your efforts. (感谢你所有的努力。)
B: I’m extremely grateful to you. (我非常感激你。)

63.

A: Tomorrow everybody has the day off. (明天大家都放假。)
B: That sounds like fun. (听起来很有趣。)

title: 10.centimeter | indicate |diagram
content:
centimeterverb — a unit for measuring length; one hundredth of a meter (written abbreviation: cm)中文释义: 厘米；长度单位，为一米的百分之一。Examples:  

The table is about 80 centimeters high.  
She measured the fabric and found it was 120 centimeters long.


indicateverb — to show that something is true or exists中文释义: 表明；显示；说明某事为真或存在。Examples:  

The results indicate that the treatment is effective.  
A survey indicates a growing interest in online education.

verb — to point to or direct attention to something中文释义: 指出；指向。Examples:  

The sign indicates the entrance to the museum.  
She indicated the correct answer on the chart.

verb — to make a signal or gesture showing what you mean or intend to do中文释义: 示意；打信号（如车辆打转向灯）。Examples:  

He indicated left before turning the car.  
She nodded to indicate that she understood.


diagramnoun — a simple drawing that shows how something works or what parts it contains中文释义: 图表；示意图；结构图。Examples:  

The teacher drew a diagram on the board to explain the process.  
This diagram shows the layout of the new office.

verb — to represent something in a diagram中文释义: 用图示表示；画出……的示意图。Examples:  

The structure of the machine is diagramed below.  
The data can be diagramed to show the relationship between variables.

title: 1.Mission | Disseminate |Assignment
content:
1. mission /ˈmɪʃən/n — an important job that someone is given to do, especially when it is difficult or dangerous. (Oxford)中文释义: 使命；任务。  
Examples:  

Their mission is to provide clean water to the village.  
The astronauts completed their mission successfully.

Common Phrases:  

secret mission — 秘密任务  
life mission — 人生使命  
military mission — 军事任务

Synonyms:  

task  
assignment  
duty

Word Root:  

Root: miss- (Latin: “to send”) → 与派遣、任务相关  
Suffix: -ion 表示名词  
Formation: miss + -ion → mission  
Related Words:  
missionary — 传教士  
remission — 宽恕，减免






2. disseminate /dɪˈsemɪneɪt/v — to spread information, knowledge, ideas, etc. so that they reach many people. (Oxford)中文释义: 传播；散布。  
Examples:  

The internet helps to disseminate information quickly.  
The organization disseminates educational materials to schools.

Common Phrases:  

disseminate knowledge — 传播知识  
disseminate information — 散布信息  
widely disseminated — 广泛传播

Synonyms:  

spread  
circulate  
distribute

Word Root:  

Prefix: dis- (Latin: “apart”) → 分开，散开  
Root: semin- (Latin: “seed”) → 与播种、传播相关  
Suffix: -ate 表示动词  
Formation: dis + semin + -ate → disseminate  
Related Words:  
dissemination — 传播，散布  
seminate — 播种





3. assignment /əˈsaɪnmənt/n — a task or piece of work that is given to someone as part of their job or studies. (Oxford)中文释义: 作业；任务；分配。  
Examples:  

The teacher gave us a challenging assignment.  
He completed the assignment ahead of schedule.

Common Phrases:  

homework assignment — 家庭作业  
project assignment — 项目任务  
assignment deadline — 作业截止日期

Synonyms:  

task  
duty  
job

Word Root:  

Root: sign- (Latin: “mark, sign”) → 与标记、指派相关  
Suffix: -ment 表示名词  
Formation: assign + -ment → assignment  
Related Words:  
assign — 分配，指派  
reassignment — 重新分配

title: 11.crosswords | alternative | summarize
content:
crosswordsnoun — a puzzle in which words are written horizontally and vertically into a grid, often using clues中文释义: 填字游戏；纵横填字谜。Examples:  

She enjoys doing crosswords in the morning.  
The newspaper publishes a new crossword every day.


alternativeadjective — available as another possibility or choice中文释义: 可供选择的；替代的。Examples:  

We need to find an alternative route due to road construction.  
Soy milk is a good alternative to cow’s milk.

noun — a choice between two or more possibilities中文释义: 替代品；另一种选择。Examples:  

You have the alternative of working from home.  
There are several alternatives to this expensive solution.


summarizeverb — to give a brief statement of the main points中文释义: 总结；概述。Examples:  

Please summarize the main ideas of the article.  
She summarized the meeting in a few sentences.

title: 12.outcome| slot |assist
content:
outcomenoun — the result or effect of an action, situation, or event中文释义: 结果；后果；成果。Examples:  

The outcome of the experiment was unexpected.  
We are waiting to see the final outcome of the election.


slotnoun — a narrow opening, especially for putting something into or through中文释义: 狭缝；投口；插槽。Examples:  

Put the coin into the slot to start the machine.  
The letter won’t fit through the slot in the door.

noun — a specific time, position, or place in a schedule or system中文释义: 时间段；职位；位置。Examples:  

I managed to get a slot for an interview tomorrow morning.  
The show was given the 8 p.m. time slot on television.

verb — to put something into a narrow opening or to fit something into a position or schedule中文释义: 插入；安置；安排。Examples:  

He carefully slotted the card into the reader.  
The meeting was slotted between two other appointments.


assistverb — to help someone or make it easier for them to do something中文释义: 帮助；协助。Examples:  

The nurse assisted the doctor during the operation.  
Can you assist me with carrying these boxes?

noun — the act of helping someone or something to succeed中文释义: 帮助；助攻（体育中常用）。Examples:  

She scored with an assist from her teammate.  
We appreciate your assist in completing the project.

title: 13.stimulating| come up with |campaigns
content:
stimulatingadjective — making you feel interested, excited, or full of new ideas中文释义: 激发兴趣的；令人兴奋的；启发思维的。Examples:  

The lecture was so stimulating that everyone wanted to join the discussion.  
She finds working in a creative environment very stimulating.


come up withphrasal verb — to think of or produce an idea, plan, answer, or solution中文释义: 想出；提出（主意、计划、答案等）。Examples:  

He came up with a brilliant idea for the new project.  
We need to come up with a solution before Friday.


campaignsnoun — organized activities or efforts to achieve a particular goal, such as social, political, or marketing purposes中文释义: 活动；运动（尤指社会、政治或商业方面的有组织行动）。Examples:  

The company launched several advertising campaigns this year.  
Many volunteers joined the campaign to clean up the beach.

verb — to take part in or lead activities to achieve a particular goal中文释义: 开展活动；从事运动。Examples:  

They are campaigning for equal pay for all workers.  
The group campaigned to raise awareness about climate change.

title: 14.perks| allowance |technically
content:
perksnoun — special benefits or advantages that come with a job or position中文释义: 额外津贴；特殊待遇；附加福利。Examples:  

One of the perks of working here is free lunch every day.  
Company cars and health insurance are common employee perks.


allowancenoun — an amount of money regularly given to someone for a specific purpose中文释义: 津贴；补助；零用钱。Examples:  

She gets a monthly allowance from her parents.  
The company provides a travel allowance for business trips.

noun — a permitted amount or acceptable limit of something中文释义: 限额；允许量。Examples:  

The baggage allowance on this flight is 20 kilograms.  
There’s a small allowance for human error in the system.


technicallyadverb — according to the exact meaning, rules, or facts中文释义: 严格来说；根据确切定义；从技术上讲。Examples:  

Technically, you’re not allowed to park here.  
The system is technically outdated but still functional.

adverb — relating to the practical skills or knowledge in a particular field中文释义: 技术上地；在技术方面。Examples:  

She’s technically skilled in software engineering.  
The film was impressive, both artistically and technically.

title: 15. red tape| bureaucracy |chained to a desk
content:
red tapenoun — official rules and processes that seem unnecessary and cause delays中文释义: 繁文缛节；官僚手续（指不必要的行政程序或规定导致拖延）。Examples:  

The project was delayed for months because of government red tape.  
We need to cut through the red tape to get this approved faster.


bureaucracynoun — a system of government or management with many complicated rules and officials中文释义: 官僚体制；繁杂的行政体系。Examples:  

The new policy got stuck in the layers of bureaucracy.  
Many people complain that too much bureaucracy slows down innovation.

noun — the officials or administrators who work in such a system中文释义: 官僚机构；官僚人员。Examples:  

The bureaucracy decided to reject the proposal.  
He left the public sector because he was tired of dealing with bureaucracy.


chained to a deskidiom — forced to spend all your working time sitting at a desk, usually in an office中文释义: 被困在办公桌前；整天坐在办公室里工作。Examples:  

I don’t want a job where I’m chained to a desk all day.  
He felt chained to his desk, with no time for outdoor activities.

title: 17. presentation| client contact |agency
content:
1. presentation /ˌprezənˈteɪʃən/n — the act of showing, describing, or giving something to an audience, or the way in which it is done. (Oxford)中文释义: 演示；展示；汇报。  
Examples:  

She gave an excellent presentation on climate change.  
The presentation included charts and graphs to illustrate the data.

Common Phrases:  

business presentation — 商务演示  
slide presentation — 幻灯片演示  
oral presentation — 口头报告

Synonyms:  

demonstration  
display  
speech

Word Root:  

Root: present- (Latin: “to place, to show”) → 与展示、呈现相关  
Suffix: -ation 表示名词  
Formation: present + -ation → presentation  
Related Words:  
present — 展示，呈现  
presenter — 演讲者，汇报人




2. client contact /ˈklaɪənt ˌkɒntækt/n — the act of communicating with a person or organization that you do business with. (Oxford)中文释义: 客户联系；与客户接触。  
Examples:  

Maintaining good client contact is essential for business success.  
She manages all client contacts for the company.

Common Phrases:  

client contact list — 客户联系名单  
maintain client contact — 保持客户联系  
regular client contact — 定期客户沟通

Synonyms:  

communication  
liaison  
interaction

Word Root:  

Root: client- (Latin: “one who leans on another; dependent”) → 客户、依赖者  
Root: contact (Latin: “touch”) → 接触  
Formation: client + contact → client contact  
Related Words:  
clientele — 顾客群  
contact — 联系




3. agency /ˈeɪdʒənsi/n — a business or organization that provides a particular service on behalf of other people or organizations. (Oxford)中文释义: 代理机构；经办公司。  
Examples:  

She works for a marketing agency.  
The travel agency arranged their entire trip.

Common Phrases:  

advertising agency — 广告公司  
government agency — 政府机构  
employment agency — 人才中介

Synonyms:  

bureau  
organization  
office

Word Root:  

Root: agent- (Latin: “doer, performer”) → 与代理、执行相关  
Suffix: -cy 表示名词  
Formation: agent + -cy → agency  
Related Words:  
agent — 代理人  
agential — 代理的

title: 18. aircraft| rapport |originality
content:
aircraftnoun — any vehicle that can fly, such as an airplane or helicopter中文释义: 飞行器；航空器（包括飞机、直升机等）。Examples:  

The aircraft took off smoothly despite the strong wind.  
Modern aircraft are designed to use less fuel and reduce noise.


rapportnoun — a friendly and harmonious relationship in which people understand each other well中文释义: 融洽的关系；和谐的沟通（指人与人之间相互理解、信任和共鸣）。Examples:  

The teacher built a strong rapport with her students.  
Good rapport between team members improves cooperation.  
When I joined the agency, I hit it off with my colleagues immediately. I still get on well with them and there’s a very good rapport between us. This is all part of my job satisfaction.
this is all part of 固定表达 是什么的一部分
Exercise is part of a healthy lifestyle.





originalitynoun — the quality of being new, unusual, and creative rather than copied from something else中文释义: 独创性；原创性；新颖独特。Examples:  

The originality of her artwork impressed everyone at the exhibition.  
Good writing often combines clarity with originality.  
I work in advertising. I love my work! It’s really rewarding and stimulating – satisfying and interesting. Originality and creativity are very important in this industry, of course; we have to come up with – produce – lots of new ideas.

title: 19. inheritance| redundancy |fascination
content:
1. inheritance /ɪnˈherɪtəns/n — money, property, or qualities passed down from someone after they die中文释义: 遗产；继承物。  
Examples:  

She received a large inheritance from her grandmother.  
Inheritance laws vary from country to country.

Common Phrases:  

inheritance tax — 遗产税  
legal inheritance — 法定继承  
inheritance rights — 继承权

Synonyms:  

legacy  
bequest  
heritage

Word Root:  

Root: her- (Latin: “to inherit”) → 与继承相关  
Suffix: -ance 表示名词  
Formation: inherit + -ance → inheritance  
Related Words:  
inherit — 继承  
heritable — 可继承的  
inheritor — 继承人




2. redundancy /rɪˈdʌndənsi/n — the state of being no longer needed, superfluous, or repetitive中文释义: 多余；冗余；重复。  
Examples:  

The company announced redundancies due to restructuring.  
Avoid redundancy in your essay to make it concise.

Common Phrases:  

job redundancy — 裁员  
redundancy in writing — 写作冗余  
system redundancy — 系统冗余

Synonyms:  

surplus  
repetition  
excess

Word Root:  

Root: dun- (Latin: “to lead, to push”) → 与重复或多余相关  
Prefix: re- 表示“再次、重复”  
Suffix: -ancy 表示名词  
Formation: re + dund + -ancy → redundancy  
Related Words:  
redundant — 多余的  
redundantly — 冗余地  
redundancy plan — 冗余计划




3. fascination /ˌfæsɪˈneɪʃən/n — a strong interest or attraction for someone or something中文释义: 着迷；极大兴趣。  
Examples:  

He has a fascination with ancient history.  
The child watched the magician’s tricks with fascination.

Common Phrases:  

intense fascination — 强烈兴趣  
fascination with — 对……着迷  
scientific fascination — 科学兴趣

Synonyms:  

captivation  
attraction  
enchantment

Word Root:  

Root: fascin- (Latin: “to enchant, to bewitch”) → 与吸引、迷惑相关  
Suffix: -ation 表示名词  
Formation: fascin + -ation → fascination  
Related Words:  
fascinate — 使着迷  
fascinating — 迷人的  
fascination for — 对……的兴趣

title: 16. sense of achievement| no sense at all |hit it off with
content:
sense of achievementnoun — a feeling of pride or satisfaction when you have done something well or successfully中文释义: 成就感；完成某事后的自豪或满足感。Examples:  

Finishing the marathon gave her a great sense of achievement.  
You’ll feel a real sense of achievement once the project is complete.


no sense at allphrase — completely illogical, unreasonable, or without meaning中文释义: 毫无道理；完全讲不通；没有意义。Examples:  

What he said made no sense at all to me.  
It makes no sense at all to spend so much money on that.


hit it off withidiom — to quickly become friendly or have a good relationship with someone中文释义: 一拍即合；与某人很快相处融洽。Examples:  

I really hit it off with my new colleagues at the office.  
They met at a party and immediately hit it off with each other.

title: 2.Pursuit |Excellence |Intermediate
content:
pursuit /pərˈsuːt/noun — the action of trying to achieve or obtain something中文释义: 追求；追逐。  
Examples:  

His pursuit of knowledge never ends.  
The police were in pursuit of the suspect.

Synonyms: quest, chase, striving  
Common Phrases
in pursuit of — 追求；寻求  
She traveled the world in pursuit of adventure.


pursuit of excellence — 追求卓越  
Continuous learning is essential in the pursuit of excellence.






excellence /ˈɛksələns/noun — the quality of being outstanding or extremely good中文释义: 卓越；杰出。  
Examples:  

The school is known for academic excellence.  
She strives for excellence in all her work.

Synonyms: superiority, distinction, brilliance  
Common Phrases
pursuit of excellence — 追求卓越  
Employees are encouraged to engage in the pursuit of excellence.


academic excellence — 学术卓越  
Scholarships are awarded for academic excellence.


center of excellence — 卓越中心  
The hospital is a center of excellence for heart surgery.






intermediate /ˌɪntərˈmiːdiət/adjective — at a level between beginner and advanced中文释义: 中级的；中等水平的。  
Examples:  

He is taking an intermediate English course.  
This recipe is suitable for cooks of intermediate skill.

Synonyms: middle-level, moderate, transitional  
Common Phrases
intermediate level — 中级水平  
Students at an intermediate level can participate in this workshop.


intermediate course — 中级课程  
The school offers beginner, intermediate, and advanced courses.


intermediate skills — 中级技能  
Developing intermediate skills is key to progressing further.

content:

title: 4.Controversial |Organized |Thematic
content:
controversial /ˌkɒntrəˈvɜːrʃəl/adjective — causing disagreement or discussion中文释义: 有争议的；引起争论的。  
Examples:  

The new policy is highly controversial among politicians.  
His speech on climate change was controversial.

Synonyms
disputed, debatable, contentious

Common Phrases
controversial issue — 有争议的问题  
The death penalty remains a controversial issue worldwide.


controversial topic — 有争议的话题  
Smoking in public places is a controversial topic.






organized /ˈɔːrɡənaɪzd/adjective — arranged or structured in a systematic way中文释义: 有组织的；安排有序的。  
Examples:  

She kept her files neatly organized.  
The event was well organized and ran smoothly.

Synonyms
systematic, orderly, structured

Common Phrases
well organized — 组织良好的  
A well-organized schedule helps reduce stress.


organized effort — 有组织的努力  
The organized effort of volunteers cleaned the park.




thematic /θɪˈmætɪk/adjective — relating to a particular subject or theme中文释义: 主题的；有关主题的。  
Examples:  

The report follows a thematic structure.  
The museum organized a thematic exhibition on ancient civilizations.

Synonyms
topical, subject-based, focused

Common Phrases
thematic approach — 主题方法  
The teacher used a thematic approach to teaching literature.


thematic analysis — 主题分析  
Researchers conducted a thematic analysis of the interviews.
