title: 5.Logistics |Coordination |Finance
content:
1. logistics /ləˈdʒɪstɪks/n — the detailed organization and implementation of a complex operation中文释义: 物流；后勤管理。  
Examples:  

The company improved its logistics to speed up delivery.  
Event logistics require careful planning and coordination.

Common Phrases:  

supply chain logistics — 供应链物流  
logistics management — 物流管理  
logistics support — 后勤支持

Synonyms:  

supply management  
operations  
coordination

Word Root:  

Root: log- (Greek: “study, word, reason”) → 与计算、安排和组织相关  
Formation: logistic + -s → logistics  
Related Words:  
logistician — 物流专家  
logistics system — 物流系统




2. coordination /kɔːˌɔːrdɪˈneɪʃən/n — the organization of people or things to work together effectively中文释义: 协调；配合。  
Examples:  

Coordination between departments is crucial for success.  
They worked in close coordination to complete the project.

Common Phrases:  

in coordination with — 与……协调  
coordination meeting — 协调会议  
team coordination — 团队协调

Synonyms:  

organization  
collaboration  
integration

Word Root:  

Root: ordin- (Latin: “order, arrange”) → 与安排、秩序相关  
Suffix: -ation 表示名词  
Formation: coordinate + -ion → coordination  
Related Words:  
coordinate — 协调  
coordinator — 协调员  
coordinate system — 坐标系统




3. finance /ˈfaɪnæns/n — the management of money, banking, investments, and credit中文释义: 财务；金融。  
Examples:  

The finance department handles all company budgets.  
She studied finance at university.

Common Phrases:  

personal finance — 个人理财  
corporate finance — 企业财务  
public finance — 公共财政

Synonyms:  

money management  
banking  
accounting

Word Root:  

Root: fin- (Latin: “end, limit”) → 与钱财、支付有关  
Formation: finance ← fin + -ance  
Related Words:  
financial — 财务的  
financier — 金融家  
refinance — 重新融资

title: 6.explicit |Cross Reference |over to you
content:
1. explicit /ɪkˈsplɪsɪt/adj — stated clearly and in detail, leaving no room for confusion or doubt中文释义: 明确的；清楚的。  
Examples:  

The instructions were explicit and easy to follow.  
He was explicit about his expectations for the project.

Common phrases:  

explicit instructions — 明确的指示  
explicit content — 色情或暴力内容  
make explicit — 明确说明

Synonyms:  

clear  
precise  
straightforward

Word Root:  

Root: plic- (Latin: “to fold, intertwine”) → 与展开、阐明有关  
Formation: explicit ← ex- (out) + plic (fold) + -it  
Related Words:  
explicate — 解释  
explicitness — 明确性




2. cross reference /ˌkrɒsˈrɛfərəns/noun — a mention of related information in another place, such as another book, document, or section中文释义: 交叉引用；互查。  
Examples:  

The report includes cross references to other studies.  
Use cross references to navigate the manual efficiently.

Common phrases:  

cross-reference table — 交叉对照表  
cross-reference section — 交叉引用部分  
make a cross-reference — 做交叉引用

Synonyms:  

citation  
referral  
index

Word Root:  

Root: fer- (Latin: “ferre”, meaning “to carry, bring”) → 与传递、携带信息相关  
Prefix: cross- 表示“交叉、相互”  
Formation: cross + reference → cross-reference  
Related Words:  
refer — 提及，参考  
transfer — 转移  
confer — 授予，商议




3. over to you /ˌoʊvər tuː juː/phrase — used to indicate that the responsibility, task, or discussion is now with someone else中文释义: 轮到你；交给你。  
Examples:  

That’s all from me, over to you for the next part.  
Over to you, John, to explain the results.

Common phrases:  

hand over to you — 交给你  
it’s over to you — 轮到你了  
pass over to you — 转交给你

Synonyms:  

your turn  
your responsibility  
handed to you

Word Root:  

Root: 无特定词根，为短语固定搭配  
Formation: over + to + you → 形成口语表达，表示交接  
Related Words:  
hand over — 移交  
turn over — 交接  
pass on — 传递

title: 7.material |corpus |allegation
content:
1. material /məˈtɪriəl/n — the matter from which a thing is or can be made; information used for a purpose中文释义: 材料；资料；素材。  
Examples:  

The building is made of strong material.  
The reporter collected material for the article.

Common Phrases  

raw material — 原材料  
study material — 学习资料  
reference material — 参考资料

Synonyms  

substance  
fabric  
content

Word Root  

Root: mater- (Latin materia, meaning “matter, substance”)  
Formation: mater + -ial → material  
Related Words: maternal, materialize, materialism


2. corpus /ˈkɔːrpəs/n — a collection of written or spoken texts used for study or reference中文释义: 文集；语料库。  
Examples:  

The linguists studied a corpus of English texts.  
A legal corpus includes all statutes and judgments.

Common Phrases  

linguistic corpus — 语言语料库  
text corpus — 文本语料库  
digital corpus — 数字语料库

Synonyms  

collection  
archive  
compilation

Word Root  

Root: corpus (Latin, meaning “body”)  
Formation: corpus (单独词)  
Related Words: corporal, incorporate, corpse


3. allegation /ˌæləˈɡeɪʃən/n — a statement that someone has done something wrong or illegal, typically without proof中文释义: 指控；陈述。  
Examples:  

The politician denied the allegations of corruption.  
Allegations of fraud were investigated by the authorities.

Common Phrases  

make an allegation — 提出指控  
serious allegation — 严重指控  
unfounded allegation — 无根据的指控

Synonyms  

accusation  
charge  
claim

Word Root  

Root: alleg- (Latin allegare, meaning “to assert, bring forward”)  
Suffix: -ation 表示“行为或过程”  
Formation: alleg + -ation → allegation  
Related Words: allege, delegate, legal

title: 8.reveal |usage |derived
content:
reveal /rɪˈviːl/v — to make something known that was previously secret or unknown中文释义: 揭示；透露；显示。  
Examples:  

The study reveals new insights about climate change.  
She revealed the truth about her past.

Common Phrases  

reveal a secret — 透露秘密  
He refused to reveal the secret.


reveal the truth — 揭示真相  
The investigation revealed the truth.


self-reveal — 自我揭示  
The diary reveals the author’s feelings.



Synonyms  

disclose  
uncover  
expose

Word Root  

Root: vel- (Latin: “to cover”) → 与隐藏、覆盖相关  
Prefix: re- 表示“回、重新、向后”  
Formation: re + veal → reveal  
Related Words:  
convey — 传达  
veil — 面纱，遮蔽  
unveil — 揭幕，公开




usage /ˈjuːɪdʒ/n — the way in which something is used; practice or custom中文释义: 使用；用法；习惯。  
Examples:  

The usage of this word has changed over time.  
Proper usage of tools improves efficiency.

Common Phrases  

language usage — 语言使用  
Correct language usage is important in writing.


word usage — 单词用法  
The dictionary explains word usage clearly.


daily usage — 日常使用  
The device is suitable for daily usage.



Synonyms  

application  
practice  
utilization

Word Root  

Root: use (Latin uti, meaning “to use”) → 与使用、应用相关  
Suffix: -age 表示“行为或结果”  
Formation: use + -age → usage  
Related Words:  
user — 用户  
useful — 有用的  
reuse — 再使用




derived /dɪˈraɪvd/v — to come from a source or origin; to obtain something from a particular source中文释义: 源自；衍生；得到。  
Examples:  

The word “salary” is derived from Latin.  
Many modern technologies are derived from earlier inventions.

Common Phrases  

derive from — 来自；源自  
This custom is derived from ancient traditions.


be derived from — 起源于  
The concept is derived from classical physics.


derive benefit — 获益  
Students derive great benefit from practice.



Synonyms  

originate  
stem  
obtain

Word Root  

Root: riv- (Latin rivus, meaning “stream”) → 比喻“来源、流向”  
Prefix: de- 表示“从、来源”  
Formation: de + rive + -d → derived  
Related Words:  
derivation — 衍生  
derive — 得到  
river — 河流（比喻流向）

title: 9.exploit | prime |gap-filling
content:
exploitverb — to use something well in order to gain as much from it as possible中文释义: 充分利用；开发；运用。Examples:  

We need to exploit renewable energy sources more efficiently.  
The team is keen to exploit new opportunities in the market.


verb — to treat a person or situation as an opportunity to gain an advantage for yourself (disapproving)中文释义: 剥削；利用他人以谋私利（含贬义）。Examples:  

The company was accused of exploiting child labour.  
He exploited his friend’s trust to get money.


verb (computing) — to use a weakness in a computer system to gain access or cause damage中文释义: （计算机）利用系统漏洞攻击或入侵。Examples:  

Hackers tried to exploit a security flaw in the website.  
The virus exploited a bug in the operating system.


noun — a brave, exciting, or unusual act or adventure中文释义: 英勇行为；冒险事迹。Examples:  

The film tells the exploits of a daring pilot.  
His military exploits earned him several medals.


primeadjective — most important; main中文释义: 主要的；首要的。Examples:  

The prime reason for the failure was poor communication.  
Safety is our prime concern.


adjective — of the best quality; excellent中文释义: 最佳的；优质的。Examples:  

This restaurant serves prime beef.  
He’s in the prime years of his career.


noun — the time in your life when you are strongest, most successful, or most active中文释义: 全盛时期；黄金期。Examples:  

She’s still in her prime as an athlete.  
Many singers retire long before their prime.


verb — to prepare someone or something for a particular situation or purpose中文释义: 使准备好；事先告知；做好准备。Examples:  

The coach primed the team for the final match.  
She primed herself with a list of possible interview questions.


noun (mathematics) — a number that can be divided only by itself and 1中文释义: （数学）素数；只能被 1 和自身整除的数。Examples:  

2, 3, 5, and 7 are all prime numbers.  
Prime numbers play an important role in modern cryptography.


gap-fillingnoun — an exercise in which you fill in missing words to complete sentences or texts中文释义: 填空练习；补全句子练习（常用于语言学习）。Examples:  

The teacher gave us a gap-filling exercise to test vocabulary.  
Gap-filling tasks help learners improve their grammar.


noun — something done temporarily to fill a shortage or absence中文释义: 临时补缺；过渡性措施。Examples:  

The part-time role was just a gap-filling job until she found full-time work.  
The company introduced a gap-filling policy during the transition period.

title: 11.among | forward |addition |adjustment|advertisement|amount
content:
1. among /əˈmʌŋ/preposition — in the middle of or surrounded by a group of people or things中文释义: 在……之中；被……围绕。  
Examples:  

She was sitting among her friends at the party.  
The decision caused disagreement among the team members.

Synonyms: amidst, surrounded by, in the midst of  
Common Phrases
among friends — 在朋友之间  
He felt relaxed among friends.


divide among — 在……之间分配  
The money was divided among the children.


popular among — 在……中受欢迎  
This song is popular among teenagers.




2. forward /ˈfɔːrwərd/adverb — toward a place, time, or position that is in front中文释义: 向前；朝前。  
Examples:  

She took a step forward and smiled.  
Looking forward, we expect sales to grow next year.

Synonyms: ahead, onward, frontwards  
Common Phrases
look forward to — 期待  
I’m looking forward to the weekend.


move forward — 前进；推进  
Let’s move forward with the plan.


step forward — 挺身而出  
Several volunteers stepped forward to help.




3. addition /əˈdɪʃən/noun — the process of adding something to something else中文释义: 添加；增加。  
Examples:  

The addition of new members strengthened the team.  
Sugar is a common addition to coffee.

Synonyms: increase, supplement, increment  
Common Phrases
in addition to — 除……之外  
In addition to English, he speaks French.


an addition to — ……的补充  
The new library is a welcome addition to the school.


make an addition — 做出增加  
We made an addition to the list.




4. adjustment /əˈdʒʌstmənt/noun — a small change made to improve or correct something中文释义: 调整；改动。  
Examples:  

The camera needs a slight adjustment.  
She made a few adjustments to her schedule.

Synonyms: modification, alteration, adaptation  
Common Phrases
make an adjustment — 做出调整  
We had to make an adjustment to the plan.


price adjustment — 价格调整  
The store announced a price adjustment on electronics.


emotional adjustment — 情感适应  
Moving to a new city requires emotional adjustment.




5. advertisement /ədˈvɜːrtɪsmənt/noun — a notice, picture, or short film promoting a product, service, or event中文释义: 广告；宣传。  
Examples:  

I saw an advertisement for a new phone on TV.  
The company placed an advertisement in the local newspaper.

Synonyms: commercial, promotion, publicity  
Common Phrases
TV advertisement — 电视广告  
The TV advertisement was very catchy.


online advertisement — 网络广告  
Online advertisements target specific audiences.


job advertisement — 招聘广告  
He applied for a position he saw in a job advertisement.




6. amount /əˈmaʊnt/noun — a quantity of something, especially that can be measured or counted中文释义: 数量；总额。  
Examples:  

He spent a large amount of money on the trip.  
The total amount due is $500.

Synonyms: quantity, sum, total  
Common Phrases
a large/small amount of — 大量的／少量的  
She drinks a large amount of water every day.


the amount of time — 时间量  
The amount of time required depends on the task.


total amount — 总金额  
Please check the total amount before paying.

title: AI-apps-wrods-1
content:
1. classic /ˈklæsɪk/adj — judged over a period of time to be of the highest quality and outstanding of its kind中文释义：经典的；典型的。
Examples:  

She wore a classic little black dress to the party.  
That movie is considered a classic in cinema history.

Common Phrases:  

classic example — 典型例子  
classic design — 经典设计  
classic literature — 经典文学

Synonyms:  

timeless  
traditional  
exemplary

Word Root:  

来自拉丁语 classicus → first-class → 典型、经典


2. explore /ɪkˈsplɔːr/v — to examine or investigate something carefully中文释义：探索；探究。
Examples:  

They plan to explore the ancient ruins next summer.  
Scientists continue to explore the effects of climate change.

Common Phrases:  

explore possibilities — 探索可能性  
explore ideas — 探讨想法  
space exploration — 太空探索

Synonyms:  

investigate  
examine  
research

Word Root:  

来自拉丁语 explorare → 检查、侦查 → 探索


3. portrait /ˈpɔːrtrət/n — a painting, drawing, or photograph of a person; description of a character中文释义：肖像；人物描写。
Examples:  

The artist painted a beautiful portrait of his wife.  
The novel provides a vivid portrait of rural life.

Common Phrases:  

family portrait — 家庭肖像  
character portrait — 人物描写  
self-portrait — 自画像

Synonyms:  

image  
depiction  
representation

Word Root:  

来自法语 portrait → 描绘 → 肖像


4. landscape /ˈlændskeɪp/n — all the visible features of an area of land; natural scenery中文释义：风景；地貌。
Examples:  

The landscape of the countryside was breathtaking.  
Photographers often capture landscapes at sunrise.

Common Phrases:  

rural landscape — 乡村风景  
urban landscape — 城市景观  
landscape painting — 风景画

Synonyms:  

scenery  
view  
panorama

Word Root:  

来自荷兰语 landschap → 描绘土地 → 风景


5. brand /brænd/n — a type of product made by a particular company; a kind or category中文释义：品牌；类型。
Examples:  

This brand of coffee is my favorite.  
They launched a new brand of sportswear.

Common Phrases:  

well-known brand — 知名品牌  
luxury brand — 奢侈品牌  
brand image — 品牌形象

Synonyms:  

label  
trademark  
make

Word Root:  

来自古英语 brand → 烙印 → 品牌


6. stunningly /ˈstʌnɪŋli/adv — in a way that is extremely impressive or surprising中文释义：极其；惊人地。
Examples:  

She was stunningly beautiful in that red dress.  
The performance was stunningly executed.

Common Phrases:  

stunningly beautiful — 极其美丽  
stunningly effective — 非常有效  
stunningly obvious — 极其明显

Synonyms:  

remarkably  
extraordinarily  
impressively

Word Root:  

来自 stun → 使震惊 → 极其惊人地


7. stunning /ˈstʌnɪŋ/adj — extremely impressive, attractive, or surprising中文释义：极好的；惊人的。
Examples:  

The view from the mountaintop was absolutely stunning.  
She received a stunning compliment.

Common Phrases:  

stunning view — 惊人的景色  
stunning result — 惊人的结果  
stunning appearance — 惊人的外表

Synonyms:  

amazing  
gorgeous  
breathtaking

Word Root:  

来自 stun → 使震惊 → 极好的


8. noticeable /ˈnoʊtɪsəbl/adj — easy to see or recognize中文释义：明显的；显著的。
Examples:  

There was a noticeable improvement in her English.  
A noticeable change in temperature occurred overnight.

Common Phrases:  

highly noticeable — 非常明显  
noticeable difference — 明显差异  
noticeable effect — 显著影响

Synonyms:  

evident  
observable  
perceptible

Word Root:  

来自 notice → 注意 → 明显的


9. material /məˈtɪriəl/n — the matter from which a thing is made; substance中文释义：材料；原料。
Examples:  

This dress is made of high-quality material.  
The factory uses recycled material to produce paper.

Common Phrases:  

raw material — 原材料  
construction material — 建筑材料  
study material — 学习资料

Synonyms:  

substance  
fabric  
component

Word Root:  

来自拉丁语 materialis → 物质 → 材料

title: AI-apps-wrods-2
content:
1. remediation /ˌriːmiːdiˈeɪʃn/n — the act of correcting or improving something; making amends or repairs中文释义：补救；矫正；修复（常出现在教育和环境等领域）
Examples:  

The school provides remediation for students who are struggling with math.  
Soil remediation is necessary to clean up the polluted area.

Common Phrases:  

academic remediation — 学术补习  
environmental remediation — 环境修复

Synonyms:  

correction  
repair  
improvement

Word Root:  

Root: remedi- (Latin: “to cure, to remedy”) → 与补救、矫正相关  
Suffix: -ation 表示名词  
Related Words:  
remediate — 修复；补救  
remedial — 补救的；矫正的




2. ordinary /ˈɔːrdəneri/adj — not unusual or different in any way中文释义：普通的，一般的
Examples:  

an ordinary sort of day — 平平常常的一天  
in the ordinary course of events — 在一般情况下  
ordinary people like you and me — 像你我这等普通人  
This was no ordinary meeting. — 这次会议非同寻常

Common Phrases:  

ordinary life — 普通生活  
ordinary circumstances — 普通情况

Synonyms:  

common  
usual  
typical

Word Root:  

来自拉丁语 ordinarius → regular, customary → 普通的


3. extraordinary /ɪkˈstrɔːrdəneri/adj — 1. unexpected, surprising, or strange; 2. not normal; greater or better than usual中文释义：意想不到的；令人惊奇的；奇怪的；非凡的；卓越的
Examples:  

It’s extraordinary that he managed to sleep through the party. — 真想不到他竟然从聚会开始一直睡到结束  
What an extraordinary thing to say! — 真是咄咄怪事  
an extraordinary achievement — 卓越的成就  
She was a truly extraordinary woman. — 她是位非常杰出的女性  
They went to extraordinary lengths to explain their behaviour. — 他们竭力为自己的行为辩解

Common Phrases:  

extraordinary event — 非凡事件  
extraordinary ability — 卓越能力

Synonyms:  

exceptional  
remarkable  
unusual

Word Root:  

Root: extra- (Latin: beyond) + ordinary → 超越普通 → 非凡


4. fraction /ˈfrækʃn/n — 1. a numerical part of a whole (数学：分数)；2. a small part or fragment (小部分；碎片)中文释义：分数；小部分；碎片
Examples:  

1/2 is a proper fraction, while 5/3 is an improper fraction. — 1/2是真分数，而5/3是假分数  
She struggled to convert the fraction to a decimal. — 她努力把分数转换成小数  
Only a tiny fraction of solar energy reaches the Earth’s surface. — 只有极小部分的太阳能到达地球表面  
The ancient vase was shattered into fractions. — 这个古董花瓶摔成了碎片

Common Phrases:  

proper fraction — 真分数  
improper fraction — 假分数

Synonyms:  

portion  
segment  
part

Word Root:  

来自拉丁语 fractus → broken → 分裂、部分


5. commission /kəˈmɪʃn/n — 1. committee or group assigned to a task; 2. payment for services (commission); 3. formal request or assignment; 4. military appointmentv — to formally assign someone to a task or grant an appointment中文释义：委员会；佣金；正式委托；任职；委任  
Examples:  

The government set up a commission to investigate the corruption scandal. — 政府成立了一个委员会来调查腐败丑闻  
She earns a 10% commission on every car she sells. — 她每卖出一辆车就能赚取10%的佣金  
The artist received a commission to paint a portrait of the president. — 这位艺术家受委托为总统画一幅肖像  
He received his commission as a lieutenant in the army. — 他获得了陆军中尉的委任状  
The company commissioned a study on consumer behavior. — 该公司委托进行了一项关于消费者行为的研究  
She was commissioned as a captain in the navy last year. — 她去年被正式任命为海军上尉

Common Phrases:  

sales commission — 销售佣金  
government commission — 政府委员会  
commissioned artwork — 受委托的作品

Synonyms:  

assign  
authorize  
delegate

Word Root:  

来自拉丁语 committere → entrust → 委托

title: words with -- undertaking  mission operation Labor Disseminate  Reinforce Comprehensive"
content:
1. undertaking /ˈʌndərteɪkɪŋ/n — a task, project, or responsibility that someone commits to; a formal pledge中文释义：承诺；事业，任务
Examples:  

Building a bridge across the river is a major undertaking.  
He undertook the difficult task with determination.

Common Phrases:  

a difficult undertaking — 艰巨的任务  
give an undertaking — 作出承诺

Synonyms:  

task  
project  
commitment

Word Root:  

Root: undertake → 承担  
Suffix: -ing → 名词化  
Formation: undertake + -ing → undertaking


2. mission /ˈmɪʃn/n — an important task or purpose assigned to a person or group中文释义：使命；任务
Examples:  

Their mission is to provide clean water to the village.  
He accepted the mission with great enthusiasm.

Common Phrases:  

mission impossible — 不可能的任务  
life mission — 人生使命

Synonyms:  

assignment  
duty  
task

Word Root:  

Root: miss- (Latin: “to send”) → 派遣、送  
Formation: miss + -ion → mission


3. operation /ˌɑːpəˈreɪʃn/n — the act of working, functioning, or performing a process; a surgical procedure中文释义：手术；运作，操作
Examples:  

The patient is recovering well after the operation.  
Business operations have improved this quarter.

Common Phrases:  

medical operation — 医疗手术  
business operation — 业务运作

Synonyms:  

procedure  
process  
activity

Word Root:  

Root: oper- (Latin: “work”) → 工作、操作  
Suffix: -ation → 名词  
Formation: oper + -ation → operation


4. labor /ˈleɪbər/n — physical or mental work; workforce中文释义：劳动；劳动力
Examples:  

Many jobs still require manual labor.  
Labor costs have increased this year.

Common Phrases:  

manual labor — 体力劳动  
labor cost — 劳动力成本

Synonyms:  

work  
toil  
employment

Word Root:  

Root: labor- (Latin: “work”) → 工作  
Formation: labor → labor


5. disseminate /dɪˈsemɪneɪt/v — to spread information, knowledge, or ideas widely中文释义：传播，散布
Examples:  

The internet helps to disseminate information quickly.  
Scientists disseminate research findings through journals.

Common Phrases:  

disseminate knowledge — 传播知识  
disseminate information — 散布信息

Synonyms:  

spread  
broadcast  
circulate

Word Root:  

Root: semin- (Latin: “seed”) → 播种  
Prefix: dis- → 分散  
Formation: dis + semin + -ate → disseminate


6. reinforce /ˌriːɪnˈfɔːrs/v — to strengthen or support something中文释义：加强，巩固
Examples:  

The teacher used examples to reinforce the lesson.  
Security measures were reinforced after the incident.

Common Phrases:  

reinforce an idea — 加强观点  
reinforce security — 加强安全

Synonyms:  

strengthen  
bolster  
support

Word Root:  

Root: force → 力量  
Prefix: re- → 再次  
Formation: re + force → reinforce


7. comprehensive /ˌkɑːmprɪˈhensɪv/adj — including all or nearly all elements or aspects of something中文释义：全面的，综合的
Examples:  

The report provides a comprehensive overview of the problem.  
We need a comprehensive plan for the project.

Common Phrases:  

comprehensive study — 综合研究  
comprehensive understanding — 全面理解

Synonyms:  

complete  
thorough  
extensive

Word Root:  

Root: prehens- (Latin: “to grasp”) → 抓取  
Prefix: com- → 全部  
Formation: com + prehens + -ive → comprehensive

title: Essential | Proficiency | Mnemonic
content:
1. essential /ɪˈsenʃl/adj — absolutely necessary; extremely important中文释义: 必要的；基本的  
Examples:  

Water is essential for life.  
Reading is essential for improving your vocabulary.

Common Phrases:  

essential skills — 必要技能  
essential requirements — 基本要求  
essential component — 必要组成部分

Synonyms:  

necessary  
crucial  
vital

Word Root:  

Root: essent- → 本质，存在相关  
Suffix: -ial 表示形容词  
Formation: essent + -ial → essential  
Related Words:  
essentially — 本质上  
essentials — 必需品




2. proficiency /prəˈfɪʃnsi/n — the ability to do something well; competence中文释义: 熟练程度；精通  
Examples:  

She has high proficiency in English.  
Language proficiency is required for the job.

Common Phrases:  

language proficiency — 语言能力  
proficiency test — 熟练度测试  
demonstrate proficiency — 展示熟练程度

Synonyms:  

competence  
skill  
expertise

Word Root:  

Root: profic- (Latin: “to make progress”) → 与能力、进步相关  
Suffix: -ency 表示名词  
Formation: profic + -ency → proficiency  
Related Words:  
proficient — 熟练的  
proficiently — 熟练地




3. mnemonic /nɪˈmɑːnɪk/n — a device such as a pattern of letters, ideas, or associations that assists in remembering something中文释义: 助记符；记忆方法  
Examples:  

“HOMES” is a mnemonic for remembering the Great Lakes.  
Teachers often use mnemonics to help students remember vocabulary.

Common Phrases:  

mnemonic device — 助记工具  
mnemonic rule — 助记规则  
use a mnemonic — 使用助记符

Synonyms:  

memory aid  
cue  
reminder

Word Root:  

Root: mnemon- (Greek: “memory”) → 与记忆相关  
Suffix: -ic 表示形容词/名词  
Formation: mnemon + -ic → mnemonic  
Related Words:  
mnemonist — 记忆高手  
mnemonically — 用助记法地

title: Preface | Premise | Fragile | Frustration | Significantly | Impediment | Sprout | Seedling | Seed | Cone | Priority | Recruit | Thrill
content:
1. preface /ˈprefəs/n — an introduction to a book, typically stating its subject, scope, or aims中文释义: 序言；开端  
Examples:  

He wrote the preface to the book.  
The preface explains the author’s motivation for writing.

Common Phrases:  

book preface — 书序  
preface remarks — 序言致辞

Synonyms:  

introduction  
foreword


2. premise /ˈpremɪs/n — a statement or idea that is assumed to be true and from which a conclusion is drawn中文释义: 前提；假设  
Examples:  

The argument is based on a false premise.  
A good conclusion follows logically from the premise.

Common Phrases:  

basic premise — 基本前提  
false premise — 错误假设

Synonyms:  

assumption  
proposition  
basis


3. fragile /ˈfrædʒaɪl/adj — easily broken or damaged中文释义: 易碎的；脆弱的  
Examples:  

The vase is fragile, handle with care.  
Fragile ecosystems need protection.

Common Phrases:  

fragile balance — 脆弱平衡  
fragile health — 健康脆弱

Synonyms:  

delicate  
breakable  
vulnerable


4. frustration /frʌˈstreɪʃn/n — the feeling of being upset or annoyed because of inability to change or achieve something中文释义: 挫折；沮丧  
Examples:  

She felt frustration at her slow progress.  
The delays caused considerable frustration.

Common Phrases:  

deep frustration — 深深的挫折  
frustration with — 对……的沮丧

Synonyms:  

annoyance  
disappointment  
exasperation


5. significantly /sɪɡˈnɪfɪkəntli/adv — in a sufficiently great or important way as to be worthy of attention中文释义: 显著地  
Examples:  

Sales have increased significantly this year.  
The new policy significantly improved efficiency.

Common Phrases:  

increase significantly — 显著增长  
significantly better — 明显更好

Synonyms:  

considerably  
substantially  
markedly


6. impediment /ɪmˈpedɪmənt/n — a hindrance or obstruction in doing something中文释义: 障碍；阻碍  
Examples:  

Lack of funds is a major impediment to research.  
Poor communication can be an impediment to teamwork.

Common Phrases:  

speech impediment — 言语障碍  
impediment to progress — 进步障碍

Synonyms:  

obstacle  
barrier  
hindrance


7. sprout /spraʊt/v — to begin to grow; n — a new shoot or growth from a plant中文释义: 发芽；嫩芽  
Examples:  

The seeds sprouted within a week.  
Young sprouts are rich in nutrients.

Common Phrases:  

sprout leaves — 发芽叶子  
sprout quickly — 快速生长

Synonyms:  

germinate  
shoot  
bud


8. seedling /ˈsiːdlɪŋ/n — a young plant grown from a seed中文释义: 幼苗  
Examples:  

The seedling was planted in the garden.  
Protect the seedlings from frost.

Common Phrases:  

young seedling — 幼苗  
plant seedling — 种植幼苗

Synonyms:  

sapling  
young plant


9. seed /siːd/n — the grain or ripened ovule of a plant from which a new plant can grow中文释义: 种子  
Examples:  

The farmer planted the seeds in spring.  
Save seeds for next year’s crop.

Common Phrases:  

plant seeds — 种植种子  
seed germination — 种子发芽

Synonyms:  

kernel  
grain


10. cone /koʊn/n — a conical fruit or structure of a conifer tree中文释义: 圆锥形果；球果  
Examples:  

Pine cones fell from the trees.  
The cone contains seeds for reproduction.

Common Phrases:  

pine cone — 松果  
seed cone — 种子球果

Synonyms:  

pine fruit  
fir cone


11. priority /praɪˈɒrəti/n — the fact or condition of being regarded or treated as more important中文释义: 优先；优先权  
Examples:  

Safety is our top priority.  
Give priority to urgent tasks.

Common Phrases:  

top priority — 最重要的事情  
high priority — 高优先级

Synonyms:  

precedence  
importance  
preference


12. recruit /rɪˈkruːt/v — to enlist or hire new members or employees中文释义: 招募；征募  
Examples:  

The company is recruiting new staff.  
They recruit volunteers for the project.

Common Phrases:  

recruit staff — 招聘员工  
recruit participants — 招募参与者

Synonyms:  

enlist  
hire  
enroll


13. thrill /θrɪl/n — a sudden feeling of excitement and pleasure; v — to cause excitement中文释义: 激动；兴奋  
Examples:  

Riding a roller coaster gives me a thrill.  
The news thrilled the audience.

Common Phrases:  

thrill of victory — 胜利的喜悦  
thrilling experience — 激动人心的经历

Synonyms:  

excitement  
exhilaration  
delight

title: ubiquitous | essential | upbeat | resume | specific | specification | indeed | rigorous | accurate | rather than | vaguely | precisely | intuition | vague | discipline | ultimately | precision
content:
1. ubiquitous /juːˈbɪkwɪtəs/adj — present, appearing, or found everywhere中文释义: 无处不在的  
Examples:  

Smartphones are ubiquitous in modern life.  
The brand became ubiquitous after the ad campaign.

Common Phrases:  

ubiquitous presence — 无处不在  
ubiquitous technology — 普及技术  
increasingly ubiquitous — 日益普及

Synonyms:  

omnipresent  
pervasive  
universal


2. essential /ɪˈsenʃ(ə)l/adj — absolutely necessary; extremely important中文释义: 基本的；必要的  
Examples:  

Water is essential for survival.  
Reading is essential for learning a language.

Common Phrases:  

essential skills — 必要技能  
essential requirements — 基本要求  
essential component — 必要组成部分

Synonyms:  

necessary  
crucial  
vital


3. upbeat /ˈʌpbiːt/adj — cheerful and optimistic中文释义: 乐观的  
Examples:  

She kept an upbeat attitude despite setbacks.  
The mood was upbeat throughout the celebration.

Common Phrases:  

upbeat mood — 乐观心情  
upbeat attitude — 积极态度  
stay upbeat — 保持乐观

Synonyms:  

cheerful  
positive  
optimistic


4. resume /rɪˈzuːm/ (v.) | /ˈrezəmeɪ/ (n.)v — begin again after a pause; n — a brief account of one’s education, work experience, and qualifications中文释义: (v.) 恢复；(n.) 简历  
Examples:  

He will resume work soon.  
Her resume impressed the HR.

Common Phrases:  

resume work — 恢复工作  
job resume — 求职简历  
resume activities — 重新开始活动

Synonyms:  

(v.) continue, restart  
(n.) CV, curriculum vitae


5. specific /spəˈsɪfɪk/adj — clearly defined or identified中文释义: 具体的  
Examples:  

Give specific examples.  
The instructions were very specific.

Common Phrases:  

specific details — 具体细节  
be more specific — 更具体  
specific requirements — 具体要求

Synonyms:  

particular  
precise  
explicit


6. specification /ˌspesɪfɪˈkeɪʃ(ə)n/n — a detailed description of the design, materials, and standards of something中文释义: 规格  
Examples:  

Follow the technical specifications.  
The specifications of the device are listed in the manual.

Common Phrases:  

product specification — 产品规格  
technical specification — 技术规格  
meet the specification — 符合规格

Synonyms:  

requirement  
standard  
criterion


7. indeed /ɪnˈdiːd/adv — used to emphasize a statement or response; truly中文释义: 的确；确实  
Examples:  

The results were indeed surprising.  
She is indeed very talented.

Common Phrases:  

yes indeed — 的确  
indeed true — 确实如此  
indeed correct — 的确正确

Synonyms:  

truly  
certainly  
really


8. rigorous /ˈrɪɡərəs/adj — extremely thorough, accurate, or strict中文释义: 严格的  
Examples:  

The test was rigorous but fair.  
They followed a rigorous training program.

Common Phrases:  

rigorous standards — 严格标准  
rigorous testing — 严格测试  
rigorous approach — 严谨方法

Synonyms:  

strict  
thorough  
exacting


9. accurate /ˈækjərət/adj — correct in all details; exact中文释义: 准确的  
Examples:  

The report was accurate and detailed.  
Make sure your measurements are accurate.

Common Phrases:  

accurate information — 准确信息  
accurate measurement — 精确测量  
highly accurate — 高度精确

Synonyms:  

exact  
precise  
correct


10. rather than /ˈræðər ðæn/conj — instead of中文释义: 而不是  
Examples:  

She chose tea rather than coffee.  
He focused on quality rather than quantity.

Common Phrases:  

rather than A, B — 与其……不如……  
prefer A rather than B — 宁可选择A而非B

Synonyms:  

instead of  
in place of


11. vague /veɪɡ/adj — not clearly expressed or defined中文释义: 模糊的  
Examples:  

His directions were too vague.  
I have a vague memory of the place.

Common Phrases:  

vague idea — 模糊概念  
vague description — 模糊描述  
vaguely remember — 模糊地记得

Synonyms:  

unclear  
indefinite  
ambiguous


12. vaguely /ˈveɪɡli/adv — in a way that is not clearly expressed or known中文释义: 模糊地  
Examples:  

He vaguely recalled her name.  
I vaguely understood the instructions.

Common Phrases:  

vaguely remember — 模糊记得  
vaguely aware — 模糊意识到

Synonyms:  

indistinctly  
unclearly  
hazily


13. precisely /prɪˈsaɪsli/adv — exactly; in a detailed and accurate manner中文释义: 精确地  
Examples:  

Measure precisely to avoid errors.  
That’s precisely what I mean.

Common Phrases:  

precisely correct — 精确无误  
precisely defined — 精确定义

Synonyms:  

exactly  
accurately  
correctly


14. intuition /ˌɪntuˈɪʃ(ə)n/n — the ability to understand something immediately without the need for conscious reasoning中文释义: 直觉  
Examples:  

Her intuition told her to wait.  
Trust your intuition when making decisions.

Common Phrases:  

trust your intuition — 相信你的直觉  
intuition-based — 基于直觉

Synonyms:  

instinct  
insight  
hunch


15. discipline /ˈdɪsəplɪn/n — a branch of knowledge or training; practice of training people to obey rules中文释义: 纪律；学科  
Examples:  

Military discipline is strict.  
Biology is a science discipline.

Common Phrases:  

maintain discipline — 维持纪律  
academic discipline — 学术学科

Synonyms:  

field  
subject  
order


16. ultimately /ˈʌltɪmətli/adv — in the end; finally中文释义: 最终  
Examples:  

Ultimately, hard work pays off.  
The project was ultimately successful.

Common Phrases:  

ultimately decide — 最终决定  
ultimately succeed — 最终成功

Synonyms:  

finally  
eventually  
in the end


17. precision /prɪˈsɪʒ(ə)n/n — the quality of being exact and accurate中文释义: 精确  
Examples:  

The machine operates with precision.  
Work with precision to ensure safety.

Common Phrases:  

precision engineering — 精密工程  
with precision — 精确地

Synonyms:  

accuracy  
exactness  
meticulousness

title: dimension | maintenance | loose | tableau | portfolio | assurance | integrate | sandbox | specification | precise
content:
1. dimension /dɪˈmenʃən/n — a measurable extent of some kind, such as length, breadth, depth, or height中文释义: 方面；尺寸  
Examples:  

We need to consider every dimension of the problem.  
The room has impressive dimensions.

Common Phrases:  

social dimension — 社会方面  
economic dimension — 经济方面

Synonyms:  

aspect  
measure  
extent

Word Root:  

Root: dimens- (Latin: “to measure”)  
Suffix: -ion 表示名词  
Formation: dimens + -ion → dimension


2. maintenance /ˈmeɪntənəns/n — the process of maintaining or preserving someone or something中文释义: 维护；保养  
Examples:  

Regular maintenance of machinery is essential.  
The house requires constant maintenance.

Common Phrases:  

routine maintenance — 日常维护  
maintenance work — 维护工作

Synonyms:  

upkeep  
servicing  
preservation

Word Root:  

Root: ten- (Latin: “to hold”)  
Prefix: main- → 保持  
Formation: main + tenance → maintenance


3. loose /luːs/adj — not firmly or tightly fixed in place中文释义: 松动的；不牢固的  
Examples:  

The screw is loose and needs tightening.  
She wore a loose dress for comfort.

Common Phrases:  

loose connection — 松动的连接  
loose fitting — 宽松的衣服

Synonyms:  

slack  
unfastened  
free

Word Root:  

Origin: Old English los “not tight”


4. tableau /ˈtæbloʊ/n — a graphic description or representation; a striking scene中文释义: 绘画；画面  
Examples:  

The artist painted a tableau of village life.  
The play ended with a dramatic tableau.

Common Phrases:  

dramatic tableau — 戏剧性的画面  
visual tableau — 视觉画面

Synonyms:  

picture  
scene  
representation

Word Root:  

Origin: French tableau “picture, painting”


5. portfolio /pɔːrtˈfoʊlioʊ/n — a collection of works or documents中文释义: 文件夹；作品集  
Examples:  

He presented his portfolio to the potential clients.  
The artist’s portfolio contains his best paintings.

Common Phrases:  

investment portfolio — 投资组合  
creative portfolio — 创意作品集

Synonyms:  

collection  
binder  
dossier

Word Root:  

Root: port- (Latin: “to carry”)  
Suffix: -folio “leaf, sheet”


6. assurance /əˈʃʊərəns/n — a positive declaration intended to give confidence; a guarantee中文释义: 保证；担保  
Examples:  

The company gives assurance of quality.  
He gave me his assurance that the work would be finished on time.

Common Phrases:  

life assurance — 人寿保险  
assurance of success — 成功的保证

Synonyms:  

guarantee  
promise  
pledge

Word Root:  

Root: sure (Latin: “certain”)  
Suffix: -ance 表示名词


7. integrate /ˈɪntɪɡreɪt/v — combine (one thing) with another so that they become a whole中文释义: 整合；合并  
Examples:  

The new system integrates all company functions.  
They tried to integrate technology into the classroom.

Common Phrases:  

integrate into — 整合进  
fully integrated — 完全整合的

Synonyms:  

unify  
combine  
incorporate

Word Root:  

Root: integer (Latin: “whole”)


8. sandbox /ˈsændbɑːks/n — a contained area for playing or testing中文释义: 沙箱；测试区  
Examples:  

Children were playing in the sandbox.  
Developers used a sandbox to test the software safely.

Common Phrases:  

testing sandbox — 测试沙箱  
sandbox environment — 沙箱环境

Synonyms:  

play area  
test area


9. specification /ˌspesɪfɪˈkeɪʃən/n — an exact statement of particulars中文释义: 规格；说明书  
Examples:  

Follow the technical specifications.  
The machine was built according to the specifications.

Common Phrases:  

product specification — 产品规格  
technical specification — 技术规格

Synonyms:  

detail  
requirement  
description

Word Root:  

Root: spec- (Latin: “to look”)  
Suffix: -ation 表示名词


10. precise /prɪˈsaɪs/adj — marked by exactness and accuracy of expression or detail中文释义: 精确的；准确的  
Examples:  

Measure the ingredients with precise accuracy.  
The instructions must be precise.

Common Phrases:  

precise measurement — 精确测量  
precise time — 精确时间

Synonyms:  

exact  
accurate  
correct

Word Root:  

Root: pre- (Latin: “before”) + cis- (cut) → “cut exactly”

title: direction | accuracy | exhibited | scenarios | informal | optimal | facilitate | migrate | disruption | detective
content:
1. direction /dəˈrekʃən/n — the path along which someone or something moves; guidance or management中文释义: 方向；指引  
Examples:  

The teacher gave us direction on the project.  
The boat changed direction suddenly.

Common Phrases:  

change direction — 改变方向  
in the right direction — 朝正确方向

Synonyms:  

guidance  
course  
orientation

Word Root:  

Root: direct- (Latin: “to guide”)  
Suffix: -ion 表示名词


2. accuracy /ˈækjərəsi/n — the quality of being correct or precise中文释义: 准确性  
Examples:  

The accuracy of the measurements is crucial.  
He prides himself on the accuracy of his reports.

Common Phrases:  

high accuracy — 高准确性  
accuracy rate — 准确率

Synonyms:  

correctness  
precision  
exactness

Word Root:  

Root: accur- (Latin: “careful, exact”)  
Suffix: -acy 表示名词


3. exhibited /ɪɡˈzɪbɪtɪd/adj — shown publicly; displayed中文释义: 展出的；陈列的  
Examples:  

The painting was exhibited in the national gallery.  
He exhibited great patience during the process.

Common Phrases:  

publicly exhibited — 公开展出  
exhibited behavior — 表现出的行为

Synonyms:  

displayed  
presented  
shown

Word Root:  

Root: hibit- (Latin: “to hold, show”)  
Prefix: ex- 表示“外”


4. scenarios /sɪˈnɑːrioʊz/n — a description of possible events or situations中文释义: 场景；情节  
Examples:  

We planned for all possible scenarios.  
The worst-case scenario was avoided.

Common Phrases:  

likely scenario — 可能的场景  
scenario planning — 情景规划

Synonyms:  

situation  
setting  
outline

Word Root:  

Origin: Italian scenario “scene, setting”


5. informal /ɪnˈfɔːrməl/adj — not formal or official; casual中文释义: 非正式的  
Examples:  

We had an informal meeting over coffee.  
He prefers informal attire at work.

Common Phrases:  

informal communication — 非正式沟通  
informal setting — 非正式场合

Synonyms:  

casual  
relaxed  
unofficial

Word Root:  

Prefix: in- “not”  
Root: formal


6. optimal /ˈɒptɪməl/adj — best or most favorable中文释义: 最佳的；最理想的  
Examples:  

We are looking for the optimal solution.  
Optimal performance requires proper rest.

Common Phrases:  

optimal conditions — 最佳条件  
optimal strategy — 最优策略

Synonyms:  

ideal  
best  
most favorable

Word Root:  

Root: opt- (Latin: “best”)  
Suffix: -imal


7. facilitate /fəˈsɪlɪteɪt/v — make (an action or process) easy or easier中文释义: 促进；帮助  
Examples:  

The teacher facilitated the discussion.  
Technology can facilitate communication.

Common Phrases:  

facilitate learning — 促进学习  
facilitate process — 简化流程

Synonyms:  

assist  
help  
ease

Word Root:  

Root: facil- (Latin: “easy”)  
Suffix: -itate 表示动词


8. migrate /maɪˈɡreɪt/v — move from one region or habitat to another中文释义: 迁移  
Examples:  

Birds migrate south in the winter.  
Workers migrate to cities for jobs.

Common Phrases:  

migrate seasonally — 季节性迁移  
migrate to urban areas — 迁移到城市地区

Synonyms:  

move  
relocate  
shift

Word Root:  

Root: migr- (Latin: “to move, wander”)


9. disruption /dɪsˈrʌpʃən/n — disturbance or problems that interrupt an event, activity, or process中文释义: 破坏；瓦解  
Examples:  

The storm caused major disruptions to travel.  
Industrial action led to disruption in services.

Common Phrases:  

service disruption — 服务中断  
disruption of supply — 供应中断

Synonyms:  

disturbance  
interference  
interruption

Word Root:  

Root: rupt- (Latin: “to break”)  
Prefix: dis-


10. detective /dɪˈtɛktɪv/n — a person, usually a police officer, who investigates crimes中文释义: 侦探  
Examples:  

The detective solved the mystery.  
She works as a private detective.

Common Phrases:  

police detective — 警探  
detective story — 侦探小说

Synonyms:  

investigator  
sleuth  
inspector

Word Root:  

Root: detect- (Latin: “to uncover”)  
Suffix: -ive 表示名词或形容词

title: material | suffix and prefix | intermediate | sentimental | refrain | essential | employable | scale | auxiliary | derive | exposure
content:
1. material /məˈtɪriəl/n — the matter from which a thing is or can be made中文释义: 材料；原料  
Examples:  

The dress is made of high-quality material.  
Wood is a common construction material.

Common Phrases:  

raw material — 原材料  
construction material — 建筑材料

Synonyms:  

substance  
fabric  
component

Word Root:  

Root: mater- (Latin: “matter, substance”)


2. suffix /ˈsʌfɪks/ & prefix /ˈpriːfɪks/n — a letter or group of letters added at the end (suffix) or beginning (prefix) of a word中文释义: 后缀和前缀  
Examples:  

The suffix “-ness” forms nouns from adjectives.  
“Un-“ is a common prefix meaning “not”.

Common Phrases:  

word prefix — 单词前缀  
grammatical suffix — 语法后缀

Synonyms:  

affix  
ending / beginning

Word Root:  

Prefix: pre- “before”  
Suffix: -fix “attach”


3. intermediate /ˌɪntərˈmiːdiət/adj — in the middle; between two points, levels, or stages中文释义: 中间的；中级的  
Examples:  

He is an intermediate student in English.  
The bridge serves as an intermediate stop between cities.

Common Phrases:  

intermediate level — 中级水平  
intermediate stage — 中间阶段

Synonyms:  

middle  
mid-level  
median

Word Root:  

Root: inter- (Latin: “between”)


4. sentimental /ˌsentɪˈmentl/adj — relating to feelings, especially showing tenderness or nostalgia中文释义: 多愁善感的  
Examples:  

She became sentimental while looking at old photos.  
The movie was too sentimental for my taste.

Common Phrases:  

sentimental value — 情感价值  
sentimental journey — 情感之旅

Synonyms:  

emotional  
nostalgic  
tender

Word Root:  

Root: sent- (Latin: “feel”)


5. refrain /rɪˈfreɪn/v — stop oneself from doing something中文释义: 避免；克制  
Examples:  

Please refrain from smoking in this area.  
She refrained from commenting on the matter.

Common Phrases:  

refrain from — 避免做某事

Synonyms:  

abstain  
avoid  
withhold

Word Root:  

Root: frain (Old French: “restrain”)


6. essential /ɪˈsenʃl/adj — absolutely necessary; extremely important中文释义: 基本的；必要的  
Examples:  

Water is essential for life.  
Good communication skills are essential in any job.

Common Phrases:  

essential skills — 必备技能  
essential requirement — 必要条件

Synonyms:  

necessary  
fundamental  
crucial

Word Root:  

Root: essent- (Latin: “to be”)


7. employable /ɪmˈplɔɪəbl/adj — having the necessary skills to be employed中文释义: 可就业的  
Examples:  

Graduates need to be employable in the modern job market.  
The course improves students’ employable skills.

Common Phrases:  

employable skills — 就业能力  
employable graduate — 就业毕业生

Synonyms:  

job-ready  
marketable  
qualified

Word Root:  

Root: ploy (Latin: “to fold, use”)  
Prefix: em- “put into”


8. scale /skeɪl/n — the relative size or extent of something; a system of measurement中文释义: 规模；尺度  
Examples:  

The project is on a large scale.  
Use a scale to measure the ingredients accurately.

Common Phrases:  

on a large scale — 大规模  
scale of measurement — 测量尺度

Synonyms:  

size  
magnitude  
level

Word Root:  

Root: scala (Latin: “ladder, steps”)


9. auxiliary /ɔːɡˈzɪljəri/adj — providing supplementary or additional help中文释义: 辅助的  
Examples:  

Auxiliary staff supported the main team.  
The auxiliary engine provides backup power.

Common Phrases:  

auxiliary equipment — 辅助设备  
auxiliary staff — 辅助人员

Synonyms:  

additional  
supplementary  
supportive

Word Root:  

Root: auxilium (Latin: “help, aid”)


10. derive /dɪˈraɪv/v — obtain something from (a source or origin)中文释义: 派生；来源  
Examples:  

Many English words derive from Latin.  
He derives great satisfaction from teaching.

Common Phrases:  

derive from — 来源于  
derive benefit — 获得好处

Synonyms:  

obtain  
originate  
stem

Word Root:  

Root: rivus (Latin: “stream”)


11. exposure /ɪkˈspoʊʒər/n — the state of being exposed to contact with something中文释义: 接触；暴露  
Examples:  

Prolonged exposure to sunlight can damage your skin.  
The exhibition provided exposure to modern art.

Common Phrases:  

exposure to risk — 风险暴露  
media exposure — 媒体曝光

Synonyms:  

contact  
experience  
vulnerability

Word Root:  

Root: ex- “out” + ponere “to place”

title: taciturn | appetite | critical | reproduce | asset | volatility | liability | prepayment | formula | aggregate | explicitly | objective | maturity
content:
1. taciturn /ˈtæsɪtɜːrn/adj — reserved or uncommunicative in speech; saying little中文释义: 沉默寡言的  
Examples:  

He is naturally taciturn and rarely speaks in meetings.  
Her taciturn nature sometimes makes her seem aloof.

Common Phrases:  

taciturn person — 沉默寡言的人

Synonyms:  

silent  
reticent  
reserved

Word Root:  

Root: tacitus (Latin: “silent”)


2. appetite /ˈæpɪtaɪt/n — a natural desire to satisfy a bodily need, especially for food中文释义: 食欲  
Examples:  

He has a healthy appetite after exercise.  
The aroma of the food whetted their appetite.

Common Phrases:  

loss of appetite — 食欲不振  
stimulate appetite — 增进食欲

Synonyms:  

hunger  
desire  
craving

Word Root:  

Root: appetitus (Latin: “desire”)


3. critical /ˈkrɪtɪkl/adj — expressing adverse or disapproving comments; involving analysis and judgment中文释义: 批判的；关键的  
Examples:  

The critic gave a critical review of the play.  
Critical thinking is essential in problem-solving.

Common Phrases:  

critical role — 关键作用  
critical analysis — 批判性分析

Synonyms:  

analytical  
judgmental  
crucial

Word Root:  

Root: criticus (Greek: “judge”)


4. reproduce /ˌriːprəˈdjuːs/v — make a copy of something; bring forth again中文释义: 复制；繁殖  
Examples:  

The company can reproduce the document quickly.  
Plants reproduce through seeds.

Common Phrases:  

reproduce results — 重现结果  
reproduce images — 复制图像

Synonyms:  

duplicate  
replicate  
generate

Word Root:  

Prefix: re- “again”  
Root: producere (Latin: “to lead forth”)


5. asset /ˈæsɛt/n — a useful or valuable thing, person, or quality; property owned中文释义: 资产  
Examples:  

Real estate is a valuable asset.  
Her language skills are a great asset in her career.

Common Phrases:  

tangible asset — 有形资产  
intangible asset — 无形资产

Synonyms:  

property  
resource  
advantage

Word Root:  

Root: assettum (Old French: “thing owned”)


6. volatility /ˌvɒləˈtɪlɪti/n — liability to change rapidly and unpredictably, especially for the worse中文释义: 挥发性；不稳定性  
Examples:  

Stock market volatility makes investing risky.  
The volatility of oil prices affects global economies.

Common Phrases:  

high volatility — 高波动性  
market volatility — 市场波动

Synonyms:  

instability  
unpredictability  
fluctuation

Word Root:  

Root: volatilis (Latin: “flying, changeable”)


7. liability /ˌlaɪəˈbɪlɪti/n — the state of being responsible for something; a legal or financial obligation中文释义: 责任；义务  
Examples:  

The company has liability for any damages caused.  
Personal liability can affect your credit.

Common Phrases:  

legal liability — 法律责任  
limited liability — 有限责任

Synonyms:  

responsibility  
obligation  
accountability

Word Root:  

Root: ligare (Latin: “to bind”)


8. prepayment /ˌpriːˈpeɪmənt/n — the action of paying for something before it is due中文释义: 预付款  
Examples:  

He made a prepayment for the apartment.  
Prepayment of loans can save interest.

Common Phrases:  

prepayment penalty — 预付款罚金  
advance prepayment — 提前支付

Synonyms:  

advance payment  
upfront payment

Word Root:  

Prefix: pre- “before”  
Root: payment


9. formula /ˈfɔːrmjələ/n — a mathematical relationship or rule expressed in symbols中文释义: 公式  
Examples:  

Use the formula to calculate the area of a circle.  
Chemistry requires memorizing many formulas.

Common Phrases:  

mathematical formula — 数学公式  
formula for success — 成功的公式

Synonyms:  

equation  
method  
recipe

Word Root:  

Root: formula (Latin: “small form, rule”)


10. aggregate /ˈæɡrɪɡət/v — combine into a whole; n — a whole formed by combining several elements中文释义: 聚集；集合体  
Examples:  

The data were aggregated to show trends.  
The city is an aggregate of many different communities.

Common Phrases:  

aggregate demand — 总需求  
aggregate score — 总分

Synonyms:  

assemble  
combine  
total

Word Root:  

Root: aggregare (Latin: “to add to”)


11. explicitly /ɪkˈsplɪsɪtli/adv — in a clear and detailed manner, leaving no room for confusion or doubt中文释义: 明确地  
Examples:  

The instructions explicitly state the rules.  
He explicitly mentioned the need for safety.

Common Phrases:  

explicitly state — 明确说明  
explicitly prohibited — 明确禁止

Synonyms:  

clearly  
plainly  
unmistakably

Word Root:  

Root: explicitus (Latin: “unfolded, clear”)


12. objective /əbˈdʒektɪv/n — a goal or aim; adj — not influenced by personal feelings中文释义: 目标；客观的  
Examples:  

The objective of the project is to improve efficiency.  
Scientists try to remain objective in experiments.

Common Phrases:  

achieve objectives — 实现目标  
objective analysis — 客观分析

Synonyms:  

aim  
goal  
impartial

Word Root:  

Root: ob- “against” + jacere “to throw”


13. maturity /məˈtʃʊrəti/n — the state of being fully developed; the due date for payment中文释义: 成熟；到期  
Examples:  

The bond reaches maturity in five years.  
He showed emotional maturity beyond his age.

Common Phrases:  

reach maturity — 到期  
emotional maturity — 情感成熟

Synonyms:  

development  
ripeness  
due date

Word Root:  

Root: maturus (Latin: “ripe, fully grown”)

title: neutral | anticipate | exhaust | permutation | prior | consolidate | parallelly | presenter | scenario
content:
1. neutral /ˈnjuːtrəl/adj — not supporting or helping either side in a conflict; impartial中文释义: 中性的  
Examples:  

Switzerland remained neutral during the war.  
Use neutral colors in your design for a professional look.

Common Phrases:  

neutral stance — 中立立场  
neutral color — 中性色

Synonyms:  

impartial  
unbiased  
objective

Word Root:  

Root: neuter (Latin: “neither”)


2. anticipate /ænˈtɪsɪpeɪt/v — regard as probable; expect or predict中文释义: 预料  
Examples:  

We anticipate a busy week ahead.  
She anticipated that he would be late.

Common Phrases:  

anticipate problems — 预料问题  
anticipate results — 预期结果

Synonyms:  

expect  
foresee  
predict

Word Root:  

Prefix: ante- “before”  
Root: capere “to take”


3. exhaust /ɪɡˈzɔːst/v — drain of energy or resources; n — gases expelled from an engine中文释义: 排气；使精疲力尽  
Examples:  

The long hike exhausted him.  
The car’s exhaust contains harmful gases.

Common Phrases:  

exhaust system — 排气系统  
exhaust resources — 消耗资源

Synonyms:  

drain  
tire  
emission

Word Root:  

Prefix: ex- “out”  
Root: haurire (Latin: “to draw out”)


4. permutation /ˌpɜːrmjʊˈteɪʃn/n — a way in which a set or number of things can be ordered or arranged中文释义: 排列  
Examples:  

There are six possible permutations of three objects.  
Genetic permutations result in diverse traits.

Common Phrases:  

permutation formula — 排列公式  
permutation of elements — 元素排列

Synonyms:  

arrangement  
combination  
order

Word Root:  

Prefix: per- “through”  
Root: mutare “to change”


5. prior /ˈpraɪər/adj — existing or coming before in time, order, or importance中文释义: 先前的；优先的  
Examples:  

Prior knowledge helps in learning new topics.  
We must consider prior commitments.

Common Phrases:  

prior experience — 先前经验  
prior approval — 事先批准

Synonyms:  

previous  
earlier  
preceding

Word Root:  

Root: prior (Latin: “former, previous”)


6. consolidate /kənˈsɒlɪdeɪt/v — combine into a single more effective or coherent whole中文释义: 综合；巩固  
Examples:  

The company consolidated its offices into one building.  
The manager consolidated all the reports for the meeting.

Common Phrases:  

consolidate power — 巩固权力  
consolidate resources — 整合资源

Synonyms:  

combine  
unify  
strengthen

Word Root:  

Prefix: con- “together”  
Root: solidare (Latin: “to make solid”)


7. parallelly /ˈpærəlelɪ/adv — occurring at the same time or in a corresponding way中文释义: 并行地  
Examples:  

Tasks were processed parallelly to save time.  
Multiple projects run parallelly in the company.

Common Phrases:  

work parallelly — 并行工作  
process parallelly — 并行处理

Synonyms:  

concurrently  
simultaneously  
side by side

Word Root:  

Root: parallelos (Greek: “beside one another”)


8. presenter /prɪˈzentər/n — a person who introduces or hosts a program or event中文释义: 主持人  
Examples:  

The TV presenter introduced the news segment.  
She works as a presenter for a radio show.

Common Phrases:  

show presenter — 节目主持人  
news presenter — 新闻主持人

Synonyms:  

host  
anchor  
announcer

Word Root:  

Root: praesentare (Latin: “to show, display”)


9. scenario /sɪˈnɑːriəʊ/n — a written outline of a film, play, or planned sequence of events; a possible situation中文释义: 设想；场景  
Examples:  

We planned several scenarios for the project.  
The worst-case scenario was considered.

Common Phrases:  

scenario planning — 情景规划  
hypothetical scenario — 假设情景

Synonyms:  

situation  
outline  
plan

Word Root:  

Root: scena (Latin: “stage, scene”)

title: Advanced Vocabulary in 60 Minutes-1
content:
1. preposterous /prɪˈpɑːstərəs/adj — completely unreasonable or ridiculous; contrary to common sense中文释义：荒谬的；反常的。
Examples:  

The idea that the earth is flat is preposterous.  
His excuse was so preposterous that no one believed him.

Common Phrases:  

preposterous claim — 荒谬的说法  
preposterous behavior — 荒唐行为

Synonyms:  

absurd  
ridiculous  
ludicrous

Word Root:  

pre-（在前） + posterus（在后） → “前后颠倒” → 荒谬


2. perfunctory /pərˈfʌŋktəri/adj — done quickly and without real interest, effort, or care中文释义：敷衍的；马虎的。
Examples:  

He gave a perfunctory nod and walked away.  
Her apology was perfunctory and insincere.

Common Phrases:  

perfunctory response — 敷衍回应  
perfunctory greeting — 敷衍的问候

Synonyms:  

superficial  
cursory  
indifferent


3. truculent /ˈtruːkjələnt/adj — eager to fight; aggressively defiant or hostile中文释义：好斗的；粗暴的；凶狠的。
Examples:  

His truculent attitude scared everyone.  
The animal became truculent when threatened.

Common Phrases:  

truculent behavior — 暴躁行为  
truculent speech — 充满攻击性的言辞

Synonyms:  

aggressive  
hostile  
combative


4. austere /ɔːˈstɪr/adj — strict and serious in manner; plain and without decoration中文释义：严峻的；朴素的；简朴的。
Examples:  

The teacher had an austere manner.  
His room was austere, with only a bed and a desk.

Common Phrases:  

austere lifestyle — 简朴的生活方式  
austere expression — 严肃表情

Synonyms:  

severe  
strict  
plain


5. capricious /kəˈprɪʃəs/adj — changing suddenly for no reason; unpredictable; impulsive中文释义：反复无常的；任性的；多变的。
Examples:  

The weather here is extremely capricious.  
She is known for her capricious decisions.

Common Phrases:  

capricious behavior — 任性行为  
capricious changes — 反复无常的变化

Synonyms:  

unpredictable  
fickle  
impulsive


6. defamatory /dɪˈfæmətɔːri/adj — damaging someone’s reputation by false statements中文释义：诽谤的；中伤的。
Examples:  

The article contained defamatory remarks.  
He sued the newspaper for publishing a defamatory story.

Common Phrases:  

defamatory statement — 诽谤性的言论  
defamatory content — 诽谤内容

Synonyms:  

slanderous  
libelous  
malicious


7. esoteric /ˌesəˈterɪk/adj — understood by only a small number of people with special knowledge中文释义：深奥的；难懂的；只有内行才懂的。
Examples:  

The philosopher’s ideas are too esoteric for most readers.  
He gave an esoteric explanation that puzzled the audience.

Common Phrases:  

esoteric knowledge — 深奥知识  
esoteric concepts — 深奥概念

Synonyms:  

obscure  
mysterious  
arcane

Word Root:  

来自希腊语 esōterikos → “内部的、秘密的” → 深奥、隐晦

title: Advanced Vocabulary in 60 Minutes-1
content:
参考:https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uLN6IdRtDhg
1. ubiquitous /juːˈbɪkwɪtəs/adj — present, appearing, or found everywhere中文释义：无处不在的。
Examples:  

Smartphones have become ubiquitous in modern society.  
His influence was ubiquitous throughout the industry.

Common Phrases:  

ubiquitous presence — 无处不在的存在  
ubiquitous technology — 普及的技术

Synonyms:  

pervasive  
widespread  
omnipresent

Word Root:  

ubi-（拉丁语：where）  
ubiquity — 普遍存在


2. cumbersome /ˈkʌmbərsəm/adj — large or heavy and therefore difficult to carry or use中文释义：繁重的；笨重的。
Examples:  

The equipment is too cumbersome to move.  
The process was slow and cumbersome.

Common Phrases:  

cumbersome procedure — 繁琐的流程  
cumbersome equipment — 笨重设备

Synonyms:  

unwieldy  
clumsy  
bulky


3. facetious /fəˈsiːʃəs/adj — treating serious issues with deliberately inappropriate humor中文释义：滑稽的；乱开玩笑的。
Examples:  

He made a facetious remark at the wrong time.  
Stop being facetious; this is serious.

Common Phrases:  

facetious comment — 滑稽的评论  
facetious tone — 玩笑语气

Synonyms:  

humorous  
playful  
joking


4. arduous /ˈɑːrdʒuəs/adj — very difficult; requiring a lot of effort中文释义：艰巨的；费力的。
Examples:  

Climbing the mountain was an arduous task.  
It takes arduous work to achieve success.

Common Phrases:  

arduous journey — 艰辛的旅程  
arduous process — 艰难过程

Synonyms:  

difficult  
exhausting  
demanding


5. presumptuous /prɪˈzʌmptʃuəs/adj — showing too much confidence; disrespectfully bold中文释义：放肆的；冒昧的。
Examples:  

It was presumptuous of him to assume he’d be invited.  
Don’t be presumptuous when dealing with clients.

Common Phrases:  

presumptuous attitude — 放肆态度  
presumptuous behavior — 冒昧行为

Synonyms:  

arrogant  
bold  
overconfident


6. pensive /ˈpensɪv/adj — deeply or seriously thoughtful中文释义：沉思的；忧郁的。
Examples:  

She sat in a pensive mood by the window.  
His pensive expression suggested he was lost in thought.

Common Phrases:  

pensive look — 沉思的样子  
pensive silence — 沉默的沉思

Synonyms:  

thoughtful  
reflective  
contemplative


7. circuitous /sərˈkjuːɪtəs/adj — longer than the most direct way; roundabout中文释义：迂回的；绕行的。
Examples:  

He took a circuitous route home.  
Her explanation was circuitous and confusing.

Common Phrases:  

circuitous path — 迂回的道路  
circuitous explanation — 兜圈子的解释

Synonyms:  

indirect  
roundabout  
winding


8. conscientious /ˌkɑːnʃiˈenʃəs/adj — very careful and responsible; done with great attention中文释义：认真负责的；尽责的。
Examples:  

She is a conscientious worker.  
He makes conscientious efforts to improve.

Common Phrases:  

conscientious student — 认真学习的学生  
conscientious effort — 尽责努力

Synonyms:  

responsible  
diligent  
careful


9. meticulous /məˈtɪkjələs/adj — extremely careful with details中文释义：细致的；一丝不苟的。
Examples:  

He is meticulous about his work.  
The plan was prepared with meticulous attention to detail.

Common Phrases:  

meticulous planning — 周密计划  
meticulous details — 极其细致的细节

Synonyms:  

detailed  
precise  
thorough


10. convoluted /ˈkɑːnvəluːtɪd/adj — extremely complex and difficult to follow中文释义：复杂的；盘绕的；晦涩的。
Examples:  

The story has a convoluted plot.  
His explanation was so convoluted that no one understood.

Common Phrases:  

convoluted reasoning — 复杂的推理  
convoluted design — 复杂的设计

Synonyms:  

complex  
complicated  
tangled

title: english study tips！
content:
Start with the basics: Learn the alphabet, common phrases, and simple grammar rules. You can find a lot of resources online or consider taking a course at a language school.
Practice, practice, practice: Speaking, listening, reading, and writing are all important aspects of learning English. Try to practice as much as possible and find opportunities to use the language in real-life situations.
Watch movies and TV shows in English: This is a great way to improve your listening skills and learn new vocabulary. You can also use subtitles to help you follow along.
Read books and articles in English: Reading is a great way to improve your vocabulary and grammar skills. Start with easy books and articles and gradually work your way up to more challenging material.
Find a language exchange partner: This is someone who speaks English fluently and is interested in learning your native language. You can practice speaking and listening with each other, and help each other improve your language skills.
Remember that learning a language takes time and effort, but with persistence and dedication, you can achieve your goals. Good luck!

There books that you can read  when you get time

title: ielts word--地理位置
content:
1. latitude /ˈlætɪtjuːd/n — the distance north or south of the equator, measured in degrees中文释义：纬度。
Examples:  

The tropical rainforests are located near the equator at low latitudes.  
High latitudes experience colder climates.

Common Phrases:  

low latitude — 低纬度  
high latitude — 高纬度  
latitude line — 纬线

Synonyms:  

parallel  
geographic coordinate

Word Root:  

来自拉丁语 latitudo → 宽度 → 纬度


2. horizon /həˈraɪzən/n — the line at which the earth’s surface and the sky appear to meet中文释义：地平线。
Examples:  

The sun disappeared below the horizon in a spectacular sunset.  
Sailors watched the horizon carefully for approaching ships.

Common Phrases:  

beyond the horizon — 在地平线之外  
horizon line — 地平线

Synonyms:  

skyline  
view

Word Root:  

来自希腊语 horizōn → 限制、边界 → 地平线


3. altitude /ˈæltɪtjuːd/n — the height of an object or point in relation to sea level or ground level中文释义：海拔高度。
Examples:  

The airplane reached a cruising altitude of 35,000 feet.  
Mount Everest has the highest altitude in the world.

Common Phrases:  

high altitude — 高海拔  
altitude sickness — 高原反应

Synonyms:  

height  
elevation

Word Root:  

来自拉丁语 altitudo → 高度 → 海拔


4. disaster /dɪˈzæstər/n — a sudden event that causes great damage or loss of life中文释义：灾难。
Examples:  

The earthquake was one of the worst natural disasters in history.  
Floods and hurricanes are common natural disasters.

Common Phrases:  

natural disaster — 自然灾害  
disaster relief — 灾难救援

Synonyms:  

catastrophe  
calamity  
tragedy

Word Root:  

来自拉丁语 disaster → 不幸的星象 → 灾难


5. mishap /ˈmɪshæp/n — a minor accident or unlucky event中文释义：小事故。
Examples:  

Our camping trip went smoothly except for a minor mishap with the tent.  
She laughed off the mishap with her coffee spill.

Common Phrases:  

minor mishap — 小事故  
unfortunate mishap — 不幸的小意外

Synonyms:  

accident  
misfortune

Word Root:  

mis-（错误） + hap（运气） → 运气不佳 → 小事故


6. catastrophic /ˌkætəˈstrɒfɪk/adj — causing sudden and severe damage or suffering中文释义：灾难性的。
Examples:  

Climate change could have catastrophic consequences for coastal cities.  
The hurricane was catastrophic for the small town.

Common Phrases:  

catastrophic event — 灾难性事件  
catastrophic failure — 灾难性失败

Synonyms:  

disastrous  
ruinous  
devastating

Word Root:  

来自希腊语 katastrophē → 翻转 → 灾难


7. endanger /ɪnˈdeɪndʒər/v — to put someone or something at risk or in danger中文释义：危及；使遭受危险。
Examples:  

Poaching continues to endanger many wildlife species.  
Driving recklessly can endanger lives.

Common Phrases:  

endanger wildlife — 危及野生动物  
endanger safety — 危及安全

Synonyms:  

jeopardize  
threaten  
imperil

Word Root:  

来自古法语 en + danger → 置于危险 → 危及


8. jeopardise /ˈdʒepədaɪz/v — to put someone or something in a situation where they could be harmed or fail中文释义：危害；危及（英式拼写）。
Examples:  

Smoking can seriously jeopardise your health.  
Ignoring safety rules may jeopardise the project.

Common Phrases:  

jeopardise health — 危害健康  
jeopardise success — 危及成功

Synonyms:  

endanger  
threaten  
risk

Word Root:  

来自古法语 jeu parti → 未定的局 → 危害


9. destructive /dɪˈstrʌktɪv/adj — causing great harm or damage中文释义：破坏性的。
Examples:  

The hurricane caused destructive winds and flooding.  
Vandalism is destructive to public property.

Common Phrases:  

destructive force — 破坏力  
destructive behavior — 破坏性行为

Synonyms:  

damaging  
harmful  
ruinous

Word Root:  

来自拉丁语 destruere → 拆毁 → 破坏


10. greenhouse /ˈɡriːnhaʊs/n — a building made of glass where plants are grown; or gases that trap heat in the atmosphere中文释义：温室；温室效应。
Examples:  

Greenhouse gases like carbon dioxide contribute to global warming.  
Tomatoes grow well in a greenhouse.

Common Phrases:  

greenhouse gas — 温室气体  
greenhouse effect — 温室效应

Synonyms:  

glasshouse  
hotbed (for metaphorical use)

Word Root:  

来自英语 green + house → 种植物的温室

title: Vocabulary
content:
1. regulator /ˈrɛɡjʊleɪtər/n — a person or organization that supervises a particular activity or industry中文释义: 监管者。  
Examples:  

Regulators monitor the banking industry. 监管者监督银行业。  
The energy regulators set electricity prices. 能源监管者设定电价。

Common phrases:  

financial regulator — 金融监管者  
energy regulator — 能源监管者  
government regulator — 政府监管者


2. economic /ˌiːkəˈnɒmɪk/adj — relating to the economy or finances中文释义: 经济的。  
Examples:  

Economic growth is a priority for the government. 政府优先考虑经济增长。  
Economic policies affect employment rates. 经济政策影响就业率。

Common phrases:  

economic growth — 经济增长  
economic policy — 经济政策  
economic trend — 经济趋势


3. macroeconomic /ˌmækrəʊˌiːkəˈnɒmɪks/n — the branch of economics concerned with large-scale or general economic factors中文释义: 宏观经济学。  
Examples:  

Macroeconomic indicators show inflation is rising. 宏观经济指标显示通胀在上升。  
Analysts study macroeconomic trends to forecast growth. 分析师研究宏观经济趋势以预测增长。

Common phrases:  

macroeconomic policy — 宏观经济政策  
macroeconomic trend — 宏观经济趋势  
macroeconomic indicator — 宏观经济指标


4. microeconomic /ˌmaɪkrəʊˌiːkəˈnɒmɪks/n — the branch of economics concerned with individual markets, consumers, and firms中文释义: 微观经济学。  
Examples:  

Microeconomic theory explains consumer behavior. 微观经济学理论解释消费者行为。  
Supply and demand are central concepts in microeconomics. 供需是微观经济学的核心概念。

Common phrases:  

microeconomic factor — 微观经济因素  
microeconomic model — 微观经济模型  
microeconomic behavior — 微观经济行为


5. projection /prəˈdʒɛkʃən/n — a forecast or estimate of future events or trends; the act of projecting中文释义: 投射；预测；规划。  
Examples:  

Economic projections suggest growth next year. 经济预测显示明年将增长。  
The architect made a projection of the building on the wall. 建筑师在墙上投射了建筑图。

Common phrases:  

sales projection — 销售预测  
budget projection — 预算预测  
future projection — 未来预测


6. disperse /dɪˈspɜːrs/v — to scatter or spread widely; to cause to vanish中文释义: 分散；驱散。  
Examples:  

The crowd began to disperse after the concert. 音乐会结束后人群开始散开。  
Seeds disperse with the wind. 种子随风传播。

Common phrases:  

disperse seeds — 播撒种子  
disperse crowd — 驱散人群  
disperse energy — 分散能量


7. outstanding balance /ˌaʊtˈstændɪŋ ˈbæləns/n — the amount of money that remains unpaid中文释义: 未结清余额。  
Examples:  

You need to pay your outstanding balance by the end of the month. 你需要在本月底前支付未结清余额。  
The bank sent a notice about my outstanding balance. 银行寄来关于我未结清余额的通知。

Common phrases:  

pay outstanding balance — 支付未结清余额  
outstanding account — 未结清账户  
monitor outstanding balance — 监控未结清余额

8. aggregation /ˌæɡrɪˈɡeɪʃən/n — the act of collecting or bringing together items into a whole中文释义: 聚集；集合；汇总。  
Examples:  

The aggregation of data is necessary for analysis. 数据聚合对于分析是必要的。  
The aggregation of small companies led to a larger corporation. 小公司的合并形成了一个大公司。

Synonyms: collection, accumulation, assembly  
Common phrases:  

data aggregation — 数据汇总  
aggregation of information — 信息聚合  
social aggregation — 社会聚集


9. dimension /dɪˈmɛnʃən/n — a measurable extent of something in space; an aspect or feature of a situation中文释义: 尺寸；规模；方面。  
Examples:  

What are the dimensions of this room? 这间房间的尺寸是多少？  
His research explores the social dimensions of education. 他的研究探讨教育的社会层面。

Synonyms: size, aspect, extent  
Common phrases:  

financial dimension — 财务维度  
social dimension — 社会方面  
spatial dimensions — 空间尺寸


10. via /ˈviːə/prep — by means of a particular person, system, or route中文释义: 通过；经由。  
Examples:  

You can send the document via email. 你可以通过电子邮件发送文件。  
We traveled to Paris via London. 我们经过伦敦前往巴黎。

Synonyms: through, by way of, by means of  
Common phrases:  

via email — 通过电子邮件  
via satellite — 通过卫星  
via online platform — 经由在线平台


11. incorporate /ɪnˈkɔːpəreɪt/v — to include or integrate something as part of a whole中文释义: 包含；合并。  
Examples:  

The new plan incorporates all our suggestions. 新计划包含了我们所有的建议。  
We should incorporate feedback from users into the design. 我们应该将用户反馈纳入设计中。

Synonyms: include, integrate, combine  
Common phrases:  

incorporate feedback — 纳入反馈  
incorporate technology — 融入技术  
incorporate ideas — 融合想法


12. embed /ɪmˈbɛd/v — to fix something firmly into a surrounding mass or place中文释义: 嵌入；插入。  
Examples:  

The bullet was embedded in the wall. 子弹嵌在墙里。  
The video was embedded in the webpage. 视频被嵌入网页中。

Synonyms: implant, insert, fix  
Common phrases:  

embedded system — 嵌入式系统  
deeply embedded — 深深植入  
embed code — 嵌入代码

title: The accumulation of quantitative changes can lead to qualitative changes.
content:
1. accumulation /əˌkjuːmjəˈleɪʃn/n — the process of collecting or gradually increasing something中文释义：积累；堆积；累积。

title: ielts word-- the envelope of gases surrounding the Earth; the mood or feeling of a place
